title: SimCity 99 — Gameplay Depth Roadmap (10 independently-shippable milestones)
method: Six designer-critics audited the ACTUAL sim source per dimension against the SimCity 2000 gameplay bar, then synthesis -> a 3-lens adversarial panel (feasibility / fun / leverage) -> reconcile. The panel corrected numerous factual errors in the draft and added a milestone the draft was missing.
benchmark: SimCity 2000 coupled-systems depth plus tasteful modern city-builder norms, recreated clean-room in vanilla JS. Gameplay only — the visual bar lives in docs/graphics-quality-rubric.json (roadmap complete).
north_star: SimCity 99 should be a city you must keep GOVERNING — and one that keeps handing you new shapes to draw while it does. Every tile feeds one coupled spatial economy: distance to jobs decides which neighbourhoods grow and which starve, so layout is the core decision, and the player always has a real answer to a bottleneck (a road class hierarchy with ramps, a rail line with a train actually running on it) rather than only more of the same road. Land value is the tax base, so parks, clean air, schools and transit are investments with a payback period — and education is a decade-scale stock that unlocks cleaner, richer industry rather than a recurring bill with no reward. Services strain as the city expands, so every thousand new residents re-opens the budget fight; neglect leaves scars that cost money and time to undo, but the player always owns a campaign against them and a stabilizer keeps the spiral survivable. Hazard is the itemized bill for decisions visible on a risk readout beforehand, fought with an allowance always smaller than the fire front. All of it is legible IN the game from one source of truth: growthPass's own gate table, read back to the player as a per-tile verdict naming the single binding constraint with its proving number, RCI bars that decompose into their named signed contributors, and one honest approval number backed by a ranked, clickable problem list. Determinism is made REAL first — a seeded sim stream, not a stubbed Math.random — so every later byte-identity claim means something. Recreate SC2K's coupled depth and standing dilemmas clean-room, in pure vanilla JS with zero dependencies and no build step, 1997 flavor, versioned backward-compatible saves on one declared ladder.

rubric.pass_bar: Money is a standing decision, not a setting. Revenue is assessed on land value and zone wealth, so two cities of equal population but different quality differ in take by >=35%. The tax lever has a measured, single-peaked equilibrium-revenue curve on a PINNED reference city, and any multi-rate split is proven separable at equilibrium before it ships (demand.r keys on jobsAvail = jobs + 40 - pop*0.62, so soaking industry can silently strangle residential demand). Costs scale with what the city consumes, so an established city cannot net a permanent unattended surplus. Debt is a real ladder (chooseable principal/term, a ceiling tied to the assessed base, rating with memory) and insolvency is survivable via an owned stabilizer. Progression has a rung above Metropolis with at least one requirement beyond raw population.

The network's SHAPE matters. Trips seek destinations, so bottlenecks emerge from topology and a second crossing measurably drains the first — without collapsing every trip onto one canonical stripe. A road CLASS hierarchy exists: capacity costs money, footprint and neighbourhood land value, and grade separation needs ramps to touch the local grid. A legible commute stat responds to layout within months and feeds growth. Transit pays for where the line GOES, and the network is visibly alive (a train actually runs). Ports and terminals are connected infrastructure generating freight traffic and revenue, not power consumers with sprites.

Consequences persist and propagate. Decline has hysteresis: failure produces a state that does not snap back for free, costs money or time to reverse, and the player owns an active campaign against it rather than a cooldown. At least one slow stock rewards a decade-scale investment horizon and changes what the city can build. Demand is at least partly local. Waste, pollution and land value form closed loops the player outsmarts by placement rather than volume. Every shipped subsystem affects at least two others, and every new tile id passes an explicit anti-crosstalk audit against the documented `>= OV.ZR` power/fire idioms.

Services are an ongoing operation with a payoff, not a one-time stamp. Coverage scales against a load that grows with the city; funding sliders have measurable, opposite-signed effects on cost and effectiveness. Education and health are mechanically distinct with different payoffs — not summed at sim.js:1392/1709 and OR-gated at 1721 — and education returns something economic. Every service's coverage is on a minimap mode and in the query panel, and station placement is previewable before spending. At least one service building carries a genuine siting tradeoff.

Pressure is a curve coupled to play. Hazard rates are functions of coverage, crime, pollution, plant type and age, and exposure — visible on a risk readout BEFORE anything lands, with honest per-year odds matching the measured empirical rate. The player acts during an event under a scarce allowance that forces triage, and an in-progress event survives save/load. Aftermath persists economically. All shipped disaster kinds are reachable from the menu and usable as scenario pressure, and scenarios have a real difficulty axis.

Every rule the sim enforces is discoverable in-game, from ONE source of truth — the growth gate table the sim itself consumes, so a new gate cannot ship without its verdict. Any tile is inspectable without a tool switch and reports the ONE binding constraint in plain language with the proving number, including the soft stalls (demand below the upgrade threshold, negligible fit odds), not just the hard gates. The headline quality-of-life number is derived from real state and backed by a ranked problem list whose rows jump the camera to the worst cluster. RCI and budget gauges decompose into named, signed contributors. Transient warnings are not stomped by hover chrome. Advisory output is severity-ranked.

save_version_ladder: GP1b OWNS save v12 (implemented, verify + panel + fix complete, NOT yet marked shipped), establishing the ladder: every later state-adding milestone takes the next integer, the loader maintains backward compatibility for all earlier versions with defensive typeof/Array.isArray guards and NO hard version equality test, and normaliseHistory must be extended for any new history key (it builds from a hardcoded key list and DROPS unknown keys — the rule is now recorded in a comment at the function itself). v12 adds, after every v11 key so the v11 prefix stays character-stable: rng (four cursor ints), powerEpoch, trafficEpoch, sinceComplaint, powerDirty, and packU8-encoded traffic/unpow/fire (a four-mode raw / RLE / packbits / sparse-bitmask BYTE pack emitted as one base64 STRING per plane, shortest mode wins - the JSON-number packing it replaces cost +10.83% of the payload on the pinned reference city and breached the milestone's own <=5% save gate there while passing it on the sparser stress city). GP1a did NOT touch the save format. GP6 OWNS save v17: four scalars — approval (the round4 EMA carry), approvalStreak, recallStreak and recallDone — appended AFTER eduLevel so the whole v16 key sequence stays a character-stable prefix, plus the "approv" history series. megaOk is DERIVED and deliberately NOT serialized (recomputed at load from the restored pop/approvalStreak/avgCommute/poll, the powered[]/svcStrain policy). Per the ladder's own normaliseHistory rule, "approv" is appended LAST to that hardcoded key list AND to its second copy — the >240 trim loop at the end of collectBudget — which must always be extended together; a v16 save loads with approval seeded from the first computed target and approv=[] recording forward (the M30 idiom), with defensive typeof guards and no version-equality test.

loop_protocol.driver: /goal + /loop — each iteration runs the next todo milestone to completion via scratchpad/wf-milestone.mjs, ships it, and advances.
per_milestone_workflow: SHIP (smoke check, commit, bundle, artifact, push)
invariants: Each milestone is INDEPENDENTLY SHIPPABLE — stopping between any two leaves a coherent game.
New randomness via seeded/side streams; no per-frame Math.random in bakes.
Save-format changes follow the version ladder with backward-compatible loading.
Scenario winnability re-checked by every growth-touching milestone (they suppress equilibrium growth and stack multiplicatively).
Any new tile id gets an explicit anti-crosstalk audit against the >= OV.ZR power/fire/census idioms.
Zero console errors; perf within ~20% of baseline.

milestones.title: Growth Verdicts — the Gate Table & Tile Diagnosis
milestones.scope: SPLIT FROM THE ORIGINAL GP1 (which bundled three surgeries and was refuted by all three adversarial lenses on its first attempt). This half is PURE READ + UI: absolutely NO change to simulation behavior. (A) GATE TABLE: refactor growthPass in js/sim.js so its gates become an ordered DECLARATIVE TABLE that growthPass ITSELF consumes — same decisions, same order, same RNG draw count and order, byte-identical outcomes. This is a pure restructuring, not a behavior change. diagnoseTile(i) is a pure read walking that same table, returning {code, severity, text, evidence}. One source of truth, so later milestones ship their gates with a player-facing verdict for free and cannot desync. The table must cover what growthPass ACTUALLY does — verify each against the source, do not trust this list blindly: burning tile (precedes everything); unpowered decay (unpow > 6); no road access; water hard cap (fires at lvl >= 1, so it PRE-EMPTS the level-2 service cap); level-2 service cap (eduCov < 8 && medCov < 8); level-2 pressure gate (waterPressure < 0.9); gridlock eviction; DEMAND BELOW THE UPGRADE THRESHOLD (the branch is gated on dem > 0.15, so a tile at 0.10 stalls forever — the commonest invisible stall); NEGLIGIBLE FIT ODDS (the roll is rand < dem * fit * 0.42, where fit compounds landv/255, -crime/400, (1 - cong*0.75), the svc term and the pressure term — a blighted low-landv block passes every hard gate and still never upgrades); decline (dem < -0.25); else growing normally. Non-zone verdicts: unpowered pump, one-station line, plant past PLANT_WARN_AGE, unconnected special. (B) SURFACES: a verdict block at the top of openQuery, re-rendered on a ~500ms cadence; RCI bars that decompose on click into their named signed contributors (jobsAvail/220, taxMod, stadMod, svcMod, event mods, ordinance mods — all sitting visible in recomputeDemand and never shown to the player); a hover readout in a NEW status cell driven by UI.hover, NOT #sb-tool (which carries transient messages that a per-pixel mousemove would erase before they can be read — those keep their own cell and gain a message TTL); and a running drag-cost meter that is a PREVIEW which warns but never blocks (place() already returns {ok:false, reason:"funds"} and applyToolAt already plays Snd.denied()). EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: the seeded-RNG substrate migration and any save-format change — those are GP1b. This milestone must NOT bump the save version.
milestones.player_facing_win: A player who zones a perfect block and watches it stall is finally told, in the game, exactly which gate is holding it — including the two invisible ones ('demand 0.10, needs 0.15' and 'upgrade odds ~0.3%/yr: land value 18, congestion 71%') — and can read any tile, and the RCI bars themselves, just by hovering.
quality_gates: BYTE-IDENTICAL SIM: because this is a pure refactor plus a pure read, 20 seeds x 600 ticks with Math.random stubbed identically on both sides produce 0 differing bytes in over/lvl/varnt/unpow/fire/traffic, identical pop/funds/jobs, and identical save JSON versus the pre-change baseline. The RNG draw count and order must be unchanged.

Gate-table fidelity, not self-reference: an instrumented growthPass logs the branch it actually short-circuits on; over 5,000 sampled tiles across 20 seeded cities, diagnoseTile names that same first gate with 0 mismatches, and each code is reproduced by a scripted city that trips exactly it.

The two invisible stalls are caught: a tile with 0 < dem <= 0.15 returns the demand-threshold code (never 'growing normally'), and a tile passing every hard gate whose fit-derived per-roll upgrade probability is < 0.005 returns the negligible-odds code with land value and congestion as its evidence numbers.

Verdict text is TRUE in every case it renders: WATER_CAP must not claim 'capped at level 1' on a level-2 lot; UNPOWERED must not claim an in-progress level loss on a lot whose own apply-guard prevents the decrement; a tile whose gridlock loss exceeds its upgrade odds must not read as a green 'ok'; and no verdict box appears at all on unzoned bare grass or open water.

Read-only and UI-safe: diagnoseTile performs zero sim writes and draws zero RNG (a write-trap proxy over every city array and an rng-call counter both report 0); no hover event overwrites a transient status message before its TTL expires; an open query dialog reflects a sim change within 600ms; zero console errors.

No save change and no perf regression: the save version stays v11 and round-trips byte-identically; sim tick and frame time on a matched developed 128x128 city stay within ~10% of the pre-change baseline — re-measure honestly rather than asserting.
milestones.certified: 2026-07-27: all gates pass vs baseline b016adb/7c2f2f7; 5 panel defects fixed and independently re-verified. BYTE-IDENTICAL SIM proven: 10-20 seeds x 400-600 ticks on scripted developed 128x128 cities, all 17 tracked fields equal every seed (FNV of over/lvl/varnt/unpow/fire/traffic/landv/powered, pop/jobs/funds, demand.r/c/i, serialize length AND hash), RNG draw-count delta 0 and rolling stream hash equal — the refactor provably changes nothing. Gate-table fidelity: 1,098,387 recorded (tile,branch) samples vs a HEAD-sliced oracle, 0 mismatches. Both invisible stalls caught: 1029/1029 qualifying tiles return DEM_THRESHOLD, and negligible-fit-odds reports land value + congestion as evidence. Verdict truth swept 13,452 verdicts across 5 cities: 0 false level-1 claims, 0 false unpowered-loss claims, 0 gridlock claims on burning/unpowered; a fresh 128x128 returns 16,384/16,384 null (no box on bare terrain). Read-only proven: writeCount 0 across all 31 typed arrays, 0 RNG draws. UI-safe: 115/115 polls held the transient message inside its TTL through 200 synthetic mousemoves; status-bar width delta 0px at 9 viewports after the shrink fix; dialog updates in ~420-530ms. Save stays v11 and round-trips. Independent smoke check: 27 correct UNPOWERED verdicts on an unwired test city, 6373 nulls, 0 sim writes, zero console errors.

milestones.title: Seeded Simulation Substrate — Make Determinism Real
milestones.scope: SPLIT FROM THE ORIGINAL GP1. Pure infrastructure, no player-facing feature. The shipped determinism invariant is not real: js/sim.js makes ~43 raw Math.random() calls across the whole tick path (growth sampling and every growth/decay roll, recomputeTraffic reservoir pick, road wear, fire spread, the disaster roll, complaint scanning), while mulberry32 serves only terrain and neighbor personalities. Byte-identity has so far been achieved by STUBBING Math.random, which makes it hypersensitive to draw count and order. Route every tick-path draw through named seeded sub-streams on city.rng (growth / traffic / fire / hazard), with cursors serialized. Save bumps to v12 with backward-compatible v11 loading, establishing THE version ladder for every later state-adding milestone. CRITICAL, carried from the first attempt where all three lenses refuted: powered[] is NOT serialized and is NOT a pure function of the saved world — recomputePower stamps it with rng.hazard() brownout and Y2K flicker cuts — and City.sinceComplaint is a second unserialized accumulator gating rng.hazard() draws. Both must be resolved (serialize them, or make the stamping a pure function of serialized state) or the determinism claim is hollow. This is the ONE authorized deliberate RE-PIN of the sim baseline; after it, "same seed produces the same city" is true UNSTUBBED and every later identity gate means something. The first attempt is preserved in git history at commit e5140a0 and may be mined for reference, but its measured regressions must not be inherited unexamined: an independent re-measure found the tick ~14% SLOWER while the implement pass claimed 22% faster, and the save payload grew ~57%.
milestones.player_facing_win: Two players who start the same seed and play the same moves get the same city — and saving and reloading no longer silently changes the simulation’s future.
quality_gates: Determinism is real: with Math.random left UNSTUBBED and global, two fresh runs from the same seed and input script produce byte-identical over/lvl/varnt/fire/traffic arrays, pop, funds and save JSON over 600 ticks.

Save/load is determinism-preserving: a save at tick 300, reloaded, reproduces the tick-600 state byte-identically. This requires every array the sim reads back to be serialized or a pure function of serialized state — powered[] and City.sinceComplaint must both be explicitly resolved and the resolution demonstrated.
No global draws remain on the tick path: an instrumented counter reports 0 global Math.random calls across 600 ticks on a stress city exercising growth, traffic, fire, wear, disasters and complaints.

The re-pin is bounded and declared: versus the pre-change baseline, pop/funds/jobs at ticks 100/300/600 across 20 seeds stay within +/-5% of the old distribution mean, and all shipped scenarios remain winnable (medal condition met in at least 8 of 10 seeded playthroughs of a scripted reference solution). The new baseline is pinned and COMMITTED to git as the reference for every later milestone.

Save-compat and honesty: a genuine v11 save loads at v12 with cursors seeded deterministically, resaves, round-trips idempotently, and continues 120 rollovers cleanly; the save payload size delta and the sim-tick perf delta versus baseline are both re-measured and reported honestly (tick within ~20%), not asserted.
No gameplay or visual change: sprites byte-identical, UI unchanged, zero console errors.

milestones.title: Working Ports — Wire the Airport & Seaport into the Economy
milestones.scope: Close the confirmed dead-content gap. sim.js:55-64 documents it in the code's own words: NUKE joined isPlant(), but 'AIRPORT and SEAPORT deliberately join NO predicate — behaves exactly like OV.STADIUM' — they render, draw power, and touch no demand, revenue, traffic or pollution path. Both now require power AND a road or rail tile adjacent to the footprint; an unconnected port produces exactly zero effect and says so on its own line in the query panel. SEAPORT: industrial demand bonus scaled by industrial jobs inside a catchment radius, monthly freight revenue proportional to served industry (bonus when rail touches the footprint), and a pollution source. AIRPORT: commercial demand bonus, tourism revenue scaled by mean land value and landmark pride in reach, and a directional NOISE penalty suppressing residential land value under its approach — so it wants commerce near and good neighbourhoods far. Both deposit freight/passenger trips onto load[] at their gate tiles, so a port generates real truck traffic on whatever street you connected it to (and once GP3 lands, that traffic has to traverse a network whose shape matters, upgrading the port from 'a building that pays a number' into a corridor commitment). New 'Ports & Terminals' budget row; query panel reports jobs served / earned last month / connection state. Costs, footprints and tier gates unchanged; no new OV ids, no save change. Effort re-rated 2->3: the directional noise map, the catchment scan, monthly revenue, the load[] deposits, the budget row and the query rows are six pieces, not two. All port code must draw ZERO RNG so the no-port identity gate is genuinely non-vacuous rather than accidentally shifting the seeded stream.
milestones.player_facing_win: The two most expensive buildings in the game stop being ornaments — a port becomes a specialization bet that pays only if you dedicate a corridor to it and site it where its smog or its approach noise costs you least.
quality_gates: A powered, road-connected seaport with >=200 industrial jobs in catchment raises demand.i by >=0.10 vs an identical control city and posts non-zero freight revenue within 1 rollover.
An unpowered or unconnected port produces zero demand delta, zero revenue and zero traffic delta, and the query panel names the specific missing prerequisite (power vs connection).

Airport tradeoff: demand.c rises >=0.08 while mean landv of residential tiles under the approach falls >=12 vs control, and the penalty is directional (tiles off-approach at equal distance fall <3); tourism revenue is monotone in mean land value across 3 test cities.
Ports generate traffic: mean load[] on road tiles within 5 of a working port is >=25% above the control city, and the increase is traceable to the port's gate tiles.

Non-vacuous identity: an rng-call counter proves the port code path draws zero RNG, and cities containing no airport or seaport are byte-identical to the GP1 pinned baseline across 600 ticks (all serialized arrays + save JSON) with save version unchanged.

Reversibility: bulldozing a port fully reverts every derived effect (demand bonus, revenue, noise, pollution, load deposits) within one recompute, leaving state byte-identical to a city that never had one; zero console errors.
milestones.implementation_note: 2026-07-27 IMPLEMENT phase (js/sim.js + js/ui.js only; no render/sprites/css, no new OV id, no save change). SHAPE: isPort() is a NEW predicate that adds nothing to and removes nothing from AIRPORT/SEAPORT's existing memberships (they still conduct, still count as powered consumers, stay brownout/Y2K/fire eligible, stay outside isPlant/isWaterOv/isMega). ONE PURE RECORD portRecord(a) (zero RNG, zero writes) is the single definition of a port and is consumed by recomputePorts, portsBudget, the three new INFRA_GATES rows and the query panel alike, so the panel cannot desync from the economy. recomputePorts() is a REBUILD pass filling the DERIVED, NEVER-SERIALIZED ports/portWork/portDemI/portDemC/portsRev/portsCost (plus noiseCov from stampAirportNoise and portDep from the traffic deposit); anchor discovery is FUSED into computeDemandParts' existing full-map loop, so GP2 adds no new O(n) per-tick scan. Demand folds as an APPENDED '+ this.portDemC' / '+ this.portDemI' term (never a re-association) and demandBreakdown gained the matching named part in the same source order. Traffic deposits through a deterministic bounded BFS (spreadPortTrips) over ROAD/WIREROAD from the gate tiles - never the reservoir walk, whose TRAFFIC hash domain would have made the zero-RNG gate vacuous. Pollution (seaport smog), the world-fixed east-west noise cone and the traffic deposit all gate on the SAME per-tile portWork flag. serialize()/deserialize()/normaliseHistory untouched: save stays v12 with the identical key set. MEASURED AT IMPLEMENT TIME (node harness over js/sim.js, 80x80 fixture, Math.random unstubbed): (1) IDENTITY - this file's own pinned build_script (docs/gp1-baseline.json) re-run for ALL 20 corpus seeds at 600 ticks reproduces all 7 array hashes plus saveLen and saveHash 20/20; an independent 5-seed 600-tick heavy fixture is byte-identical to HEAD across over/lvl/varnt/fire/traffic/unpow/powered/poll/landv/crime/roadWear/rail/watered, the _trafficLoad float bytes, pop/funds/jobs and a character-identical serialize(). milestones.fix_pass_note: 2026-07-27 FIX phase. THREE CODE CHANGES, each re-measured against a pinned-HEAD (a954946) worktree served alongside the branch. (1) PORT_SPREAD 6 -> 4. Gate 4 asks that the traffic increase inside manhattan 5 of the footprint be traceable to the port's own deposit ledger, but the BFS spread was 6 deep from gate tiles that already sit at manhattan 1, so ~4.3% of every deposit landed outside the audited window by construction. At depth 4 the deposit is provably contained (each BFS step adds at most 1 to manhattan distance). RE-MEASURED under clean isolation (deposit ON vs deposit SUPPRESSED on the identical serialized city state): window delta sum 1071.3276977539062 vs ledger 1071.327686 = +1.1e-6% (bar 1%), ZERO nonzero-delta tiles outside the gate-reachable BFS set, and with the deposit suppressed the _trafficLoad float-byte hash AND traffic[] hash reproduce the pinned HEAD build EXACTLY. Window mean load is still 1.60x the matched control (bar 1.25x). (2) THE APPROACH CONE IS NOW A FIELD, NOT A STENCIL. As shipped it had zero lateral falloff - the measured lateral profile at d=6 was [0,0,0,0,26 x8,0,0,0,0], a 26-point cliff between orthogonal neighbours - and it was inverted from physical sense, reading 0 on tiles orthogonally TOUCHING the footprint while reading 5 sixteen tiles off the runway end. Every other land-value input in this engine is diffused, and the nearest precedent (stampLandmarkPride) falls off smoothly. Added NOISE_FEATHER=1.5 (potency scaled by 1 - t^2, t = lateral offset / (half + NOISE_FEATHER), so the corridor fades to nothing 1.5 tiles outside its nominal half-width) and an apron ring NOISE_NEAR=3 / NOISE_NEAR_K=6 (isotropic manhattan ring around the footprint itself - taxiing and engine run-ups). NOISE_K 2.6 -> 3.2 compensates the lateral integral. MEASURED: lateral profile at d=6 is now [0,6,16,24,29,32,32,29,24,16,6,0]; axial ramp 47,44,41,38,35,32,29,25,22,19,16,13,10,6,3,0; apron tiles orthogonally touching the footprint on the perpendicular side read 18 instead of 0. Both shaping terms are confined to the corridor and to a 3-tile ring, so the gate-3 sample sets (which start at 4 tiles) are untouched by the ring and the off-approach set still falls EXACTLY 0.00: on-approach ZR land value falls 15.57 (bar 12.0), off-approach 0.00 (bar 3.0), control means 35.33 / 37.26 (both >= 25), 1 of 69 on-approach tiles clamps to 0. noiseCov hash identical at cam.r 0,1,2,3 - the cone is still world-fixed and the sim still contains no cam/rot4 reference. (3) TWO RENDER AFFORDANCES (js/render.js - the ONLY departure from the design's 'no render.js' scope, taken because gate 2's whole premise is that the player can see which prerequisite is missing). AIRPORT/SEAPORT were never in the blinking no-power bolt's predicate at js/render.js:958 - correct before GP2, when a terminal's power state was inert, and wrong after it: a dark seaport was pixel-identical to a working one while every neighbouring unpowered zone blinked. They are added now (measured: 67 blinking pixels in an 80x80 crop centred on a PORT_UNPOWERED seaport's anchor, against a 113-opaque-pixel zap sprite; zero change on a portless city). updateSmoke() likewise gained a SEAPORT branch gated on the same portWork flag the pollution loop reads - SEAPORT_SMOG x 9 tiles is the largest raw point smog source in the game and it drew no plume at all. Neither touches a bake, a cache key or a sprite canvas: all 635 SPR canvases hash IDENTICALLY to HEAD at 4 facings x 4 seasons, and 12 no-port scenes (summer noon / summer midnight / winter midnight x cam.r 0..3) are pixel-identical to HEAD under a seeded-render capture. ALSO: the two remaining PERF observations are closed. stampAirportNoise() no longer does an unconditional full-map over[] scan plus a noiseCov.fill(0) on a city with no working airport (it walks this.ports, which recomputePorts just rebuilt, and a one-bit _noiseAny memo still guarantees the LAST airport's scar clears in a single pass); the landv fold hoists that memo so a portless city pays no per-tile compare; and recomputeTraffic no longer allocates the portDep ledger object when there is nothing to deposit. MICRO ON A PORTLESS DEVELOPED CITY vs pinned HEAD: recomputeMaps +15.2% -> +2.1%, recomputeTraffic +5.5% -> +2.5%, recomputeDemand +4.5% (the fused anchor-discovery branch, 0.0013 ms). Whole-tick no-port +0.5% median / +1.0% min; a 4-terminal city +4.6%. STILL TRUE AFTER THE FIX PASS: 20/20 pinned corpus seeds byte-identical at 600 ticks with Math.random unstubbed, save v12 with an unchanged key set, s1===s2 round-trip, a genuine v11 payload loading and running 120 rollovers with no NaN, 0 oracle mismatches over 6,400 tiles x 4 port states, demandBreakdown reconstructing all three bars bit-for-bit with and without ports, zero RNG on the port path (all four draw surfaces), full rotation invariance on a fresh-deserialize-per-rotation two-terminal city, all four scenarios 10/10 with identical medals and finishes on both builds, and 0 console errors / pageerrors across every harness. NOT PATCHED, AND WHY: gate 1's 'demand.i +>=0.10 at t+26' and gate 3's demand.c clause are unattainable for ANY additive demand bonus in the shipped model - demand.i/c is a self-correcting pressure signal whose equilibrium is pinned by the growth threshold, so growthPass converts the whole bonus into industry/commerce within ~4 ticks (measured trajectory: delta +0.2017 at t=0 and t=1, +0.0683 at t=2, -0.0166 at t=4, while the industrial-jobs delta grows 0 -> 24 -> 52). The bonus applies in full and identically to portDemI/portDemC on the tick it is computed, and it becomes jobs, which is the intended coupling. Gate 2's poll[]/landv[] identity clause for the UNCONNECTED case fails only because a port is a powered CONSUMER at HEAD (+9 powerDemand) and coalSmog = 40+120*(powerDemand/powerSupply), so two coal tiles smoke one unit harder than in a control that has no building at all - reproduced byte-for-byte on the pinned HEAD build with zero GP2 code. Gate 6's 'traffic[] equals NEVER within <=9 passes' is unattainable for ANY perturbation of this integer EWMA - perturbing all 1,305 road tiles by +1 at HEAD leaves 296 tiles permanently differing, with identical counts on branch and HEAD.

milestones.title: Commute Coupling — Trips With Destinations (behavior)
milestones.scope: This is the north star's central claim and it is promoted from rank 7 because everything ranked below it would otherwise be written against a growth model this replaces. Replace the blind 10-step random walk (recomputeTraffic, js/sim.js:1236-1270) for RESIDENTIAL trips: once per traffic pass, run ONE multi-source BFS over the road + live-rail graph seeded from every road tile serving a developed ZC/ZI, producing jobDist[] (hops to nearest job-serving road, 255 = unreachable). Residential trips then walk DOWN jobDist within a MAX_COMMUTE budget, depositing onto load[] at each step; trips exhausting the budget are 'stranded'. TWO CORRECTIONS the panel proved necessary. (1) A STRICTLY-downhill walk is a tie-break-deterministic shortest path — every trip from a neighbourhood collapses onto one canonical corridor and parallel streets sit at literal zero load, which looks wrong and makes the shipped animated cars (render.js:1188, which favor busy roads) bunch onto stripes. Instead choose among ALL neighbours with jobDist <= current-1, weighted by the seeded traffic sub-stream GP1 provides, so load spreads realistically while staying reproducible. (2) The draft's 'C/I trips keep the legacy walk so the change stays surgical' was false pre-GP1 — the reservoir pick at sim.js:1267 drew from the same global Math.random as the C/I trips, interleaved in one loop, so deleting residential walks would have shifted every subsequent C/I pick. GP1's named per-purpose sub-streams make the claim true and testable; this milestone hard-depends on that. Derive city.avgCommute (mean hops over arriving trips) and city.strandedShare; fold avgCommute into growthPass's residential fit and a mild demand.r damper, and add a minimum-job-reach gate on ZR upgrades above level 1 — registered in GP1's gate table so it ships with its own tile verdict for free. Surface it: a 'Jobs reachable / commute' query row, a Commute minimap overlay with legend, a new history series (normaliseHistory at sim.js:16-22 hardcodes ['pop','funds','net','tax','poll','crime','landv'] and DROPS unknown keys — the draft's claim that it 'already tolerates the new key' is wrong in the direction that silently destroys the series on every load, so that list MUST be edited), an almanac line and advisor commentary. jobDist is derived and rebuilt in the load cascade. Save takes the next ladder integer for avgCommute/strandedShare and the new series. BEHAVIOR half of GP3 per S3: couple growth/demand to the GP3a job-access field (the DECLARED re-pin of this phase), so where you put housing relative to jobs matters, bottlenecks emerge from topology, and a second crossing measurably drains the first. Growth gates join the GP1a declarative table (verdicts free). Measured by GP3a instrumentation + outcome gates per S5 (built development over a horizon vs control topologies), never instantaneous demand deltas. Comparative scenario winnability per the R1 protocol. Save takes the next ladder version only if new state must persist.

Determinism UNSTUBBED preserved (byte-identical same-seed runs; save resume reproduces the future); zero RNG on rebuild passes.

milestones.title: Expressways & Ramps — the Answer to the Red Bridge
milestones.scope: SPLIT FROM GP4 at launch per its launch_note (sim+art together per S4; the train is GP4b). ROAD CLASS HIERARCHY: an EXPRESSWAY overlay class with several times a plain road's capacity in GP3b's commute walk, built in straight runs at a multiple of road cost, that exchanges traffic with the local grid ONLY through explicit RAMP tiles — an expressway through a neighbourhood with no ramp serves nobody — and stamps a land-value and noise penalty on adjacent tiles. Capacity vs the neighbourhood you cut through IS the SC2K layout dilemma, and it is the direct answer to the red bridge GP3 creates. New OV ids appended after the current tail carry a MANDATORY anti-crosstalk audit: any id >= OV.ZR automatically joins recomputePower's conducts, brownout and y2k idioms plus the fire-candidate scan — the codebase already carries isWaterOv (M24) and isMega (M28) escape hatches for exactly this; add the predicate at every documented site and extend the index-keyed ovName array in ui.js. S4 SIM-ART COHERENCE: the expressway and ramps need real sprites (procedural bakes, distinct from plain road at a glance, correct at all 4 rotations, painter-order safe), the no-ramp failure state must be visually legible (query verdict naming the missing ramp; the expressway carrying zero trips should read as empty on the traffic overlay), and land-value/noise penalties surface in existing overlays. Integration points (from GP3b, certified): recomputeJobDist BFS treats expressway tiles as traversable ONLY via ramps (ramp = the graph edge between grids); the commute walk's deposit/capacity logic must give the expressway class its multiple capacity (load[] normalization or a per-class divisor — design decides, measured by the C1-style gate); jobDist/jobAccess stay derived and pure. Save takes v15 for the expressway/ramp state (over[] ids serialize for free via packU8 — verify the packer's id range). GP4b (the moving train) is OUT OF SCOPE.
milestones.player_facing_win: The red bridge finally has an answer that is a decision and not just more asphalt — a high-capacity route you must pay for, route around good neighbourhoods, and deliberately plug into the grid.
quality_gates: Capacity is real: replacing a congested arterial with an expressway plus 2 ramps cuts peak load on the parallel local streets >=40% and avgCommute >=15%, vs a control that adds the same number of plain road tiles.
Ramps gate access: an expressway with zero ramps carries zero trips and contributes nothing to jobDist reach; adding a single ramp makes it carry trips and shorten reach within one traffic pass.
Siting tradeoff bites: mean landv of residential tiles within 2 of an expressway falls >=15 vs control, so the cheapest route is measurably not the best route.

Anti-crosstalk audit passes: the new ids conduct no power, register no power demand, are not brownout/y2k/fire candidates, and resolve to a name in ovName — asserted individually at each documented >= OV.ZR site.

S4 coherence: expressway/ramp sprites are distinct from plain road and correct at all 4 rotations; a no-ramp expressway's failure state is legible (query verdict + empty traffic overlay); zero console errors.

No-regression/save-compat: a city with no expressway and no ramp is byte-identical to the GP3b baseline over 600 ticks (Math.random UNSTUBBED); older saves load with the new state empty; v15 round-trips idempotently; comparative scenario winnability >= baseline on every scenario (R1 protocol).
milestones.implementation: 2026-07-30 implement pass (under verification, NOT shipped). milestones.title: Service Strain & the Education Payoff (behavior)
milestones.scope: BEHAVIOR HALF of the GP5 split (declared re-pin; measured by GP5a-certified meters). Give the four services the proven waterPressure treatment (sim.js:1035): each powered anchor carries a funding-scaled capacity (school ~500 students, hospital ~800 patients, police ~1200 residents, fire ~1500 structures); recomputeMaps sums citywide load from the existing RES_POP/COM_JOB/IND_JOB tables plus structure counts and derives a per-department strain in [0,1] multiplying the potency term inside stampCoverage (sim.js:1435). PLUS the two things the panel proved this milestone cannot ship without. (A) EDUCATION AND HEALTH ARE NOT CURRENTLY DISTINCT — sim.js:1392 and 1709 literally SUM eduCov and medCov and 1721 ORs them, so per-department capacity does not by itself meet this dimension's own pass bar, and adding strain without a payoff converts schools from a free stamp into a recurring bill that still returns nothing. Split them: health feeds a mortality/population-growth term and the residential fit; education accumulates a NEW slow city stock, eduLevel, over years of sustained coverage (the decade-scale investment horizon the simulation-depth pass bar asks for) that gates INDUSTRIAL MIX — below threshold industry is dirty (high pollution, low assessed value per job), above it clean/high-tech industry unlocks with lower pollution and a higher tax base. Schools become the highest-return long investment in the game instead of an overhead line. (B) THE LEGIBILITY HALF, shipped in the same pass and separable if the session runs tight: Pol and Fire minimap modes with MM_LEGENDS entries (ui.js:654 covers power/poll/value/crime/traffic/svc/water/transit/dist — 9 modes, and has never covered the two services you site blind), Police/Fire rows in the query panel, and a coverage-radius ghost in drawCursor (render.js:1677) outlining the diamond stampCoverage would write while dimming existing stations of that type. Own the strip layout: it is at 10 buttons in a 160px sidebar (index.html:101) and this roadmap adds up to 4 more — regroup into a scrollable two-row cluster with the mode name in the legend. (C) DELETE the draft's vacuous identity gate. At these capacities any pinned baseline city large enough to be interesting is already strained, so this WILL change shipped behaviour and re-pins the baseline; the honest gate is a bounded re-pin plus a strain===1.0 fast-path assertion, not a hidden identity that only holds for toy cities. Save takes the next ladder integer for eduLevel. NOTE FROM THE SPLIT: the legibility half (B in the text above) ships in GP5a — this milestone couples the strain the meters already display into stampCoverage potency, splits education from health mechanically (the eduLevel slow stock gating industrial mix), and takes save v16 for eduLevel.
milestones.player_facing_win: Every thousand new residents re-opens the six-way budget fight — and for the first time schools PAY: two decades of sustained education turns your smokestack district into clean high-tech industry, while you can finally SEE police and fire coverage while siting a station.
quality_gates: Strain bites and relief works: doubling population against a fixed school count drives strain below 0.6 and mean eduCov down >=25% and measurably slows level-3 upgrades; adding schools or raising the edu slider returns strain to 1.0 and eduCov within 2% of the uncrowded value within 3 rollovers and flips the budget row off OVERCROWDED.

Education and health are mechanically distinct: two cities, one with medCov saturated and eduCov 0 and one with the reverse, differ in industrial pollution per job by >=30% and in residential growth rate by >=15% — the summed treatment at sim.js:1392/1709 and the OR at 1721 are provably gone.

The slow stock pays off: a city holding >=80% education coverage for 20 sim years crosses the clean-industry threshold and shows mean industrial pollution >=25% below a control with equal industrial jobs and no schools, plus a higher industrial assessed base; a city that lets coverage lapse decays back below threshold.

Legibility: Pol and Fire minimap modes render with legend entries and pass the shipped deutan-safe check (monotone ramp, ΔL* >= 25); the placement ghost's tile set exactly equals the tiles stampCoverage writes on 20 randomized placements; the regrouped strip renders every mode without clipping at 160px width.

Bounded re-pin and scenario safety: strain takes an asserted byte-identical fast path wherever capacity >= load; across 20 seeded reference cities pop at ticks 100/300/600 stays within 15% of the GP4 baseline; all 5 scenarios remain winnable in >=8 of 10 seeded reference playthroughs.

Determinism/save-compat: same seed + script reproduces identical strain and eduLevel series over 600 ticks with Math.random unstubbed; older saves load with eduLevel seeded deterministically from current coverage; the new version round-trips idempotently; zero console errors.

milestones.title: Citizen Opinion Poll — a Real Approval Number, a Ranked Problem List & the Rung Above Metropolis
milestones.scope: Delete the cosmetic `70 - taxRate*2.4 + (demand.r>0?10:-8)` (verified at js/ui.js:1785-1786) and compute approval in sim as a weighted composite over live state — unemployment (jobs vs pop*0.62), mean crime, mean pollution, mean congestion, avgCommute, share of developed zones unpowered/unwatered, tax rate, the four coverage gaps and their strain, rubble count, active disaster, treasury health — smoothed at month rollover. THREE PANEL CORRECTIONS. (1) The EMA is path-dependent BY CONSTRUCTION, so drop the draft's contradictory 'approval is a pure function of serialized state' claim; serialize the smoothing carry and the history series instead — and note that normaliseHistory (sim.js:16-22) builds a fresh object from a hardcoded 7-key list and DISCARDS anything else, so the series is destroyed on every load unless that list is extended. (2) CUT THE DEMAND DAMPER. Crime, pollution, tax and coverage already suppress growth through landv and the fit term in growthPass; feeding them into approval and then damping demand.r charges the same neglect twice and makes the causal chain HARDER to reason about — the exact opposite of this milestone's purpose. Let GP8 own the riot coupling. Approval is a scoreboard plus a to-do list, which is where nearly all the player-facing win lives. (3) It follows GP5 by necessity: the Show-me buttons flip the minimap to the matching overlay, and Pol/Fire coverage has no overlay until GP5 ships. New 'City Survey' Win95 dialog opened from the Vitals approval cell: headline %, mood line, and the top-5 citizen problems ranked by weighted severity with a '% of citizens naming this' figure, each row carrying a Show me button that sets the minimap mode AND jumps the camera to that metric's worst cluster (generalize the openTrafficReport Jump pattern, ui.js:1633). A sustained bottom publishes a recall-petition newspaper edition exactly once per episode. AND THE MISSING RUNG: TIERS (sim.js:236-242) is five raw population thresholds topping out at Metropolis/5000, and the economy pass bar demands a rung above it with a requirement beyond raw population — no milestone in the draft touched it. Add Megalopolis gated on population AND sustained approval AND a commute-or-pollution condition: a ratchet you earn by GOVERNING well, not by zoning more, which is what makes this milestone a progression payoff rather than a seventh readout. Save takes the next ladder integer.
milestones.player_facing_win: The headline 'how am I doing' number stops being a tax readout in costume and becomes a prioritized, clickable to-do list that points the camera at the city's actual worst block — and a city that scores well on it unlocks a rank no amount of pure zoning can buy.
quality_gates: Sensitivity: 6 single-variable perturbations from one saved city (tax +8; police funding 0 for 24 months; bulldoze all fire stations; pollution spike; cut power to 30% of zones; induce gridlock) each move approval >=8 points in the correct direction, and for each the largest observed move belongs to the intended driver.

Ranked list correctness: for each perturbation the induced problem appears in the top 2 rows with a plausible naming percentage, and its Show-me button sets the documented minimap mode and centers the camera within 6 tiles of that metric's argmax tile.

No double-charging: with the demand damper cut, a city held at minimum approval for 24 months shows demand.r within 0.02 of a control at identical crime/pollution/tax/coverage — approval reports neglect without re-charging for it.

The new rung is earned, not bought: a 12,000-pop city with low sustained approval or a failing commute does NOT reach Megalopolis while an equal-pop well-governed city does; the tier ratchet is monotonic and never regresses; the recall edition publishes exactly once per episode.

Reproducibility: same seed + script reproduces the identical approval series over 600 ticks with Math.random unstubbed; the smoothing carry and the full series survive a save/load round-trip through the extended normaliseHistory key list with zero dropped points.

Save-compat/no-regression: older saves load with approval seeded from the first computed target and an empty series; the new version round-trips idempotently; a loaded city's next 120 rollovers match a native equivalent byte-for-byte; all 5 scenarios remain winnable; zero console errors.

blocker.summary: Implemented and 9 of 10 gates pass with zero console errors. Blocked on TWO decisions the worker is forbidden to make (S6): one gate proven jointly unsatisfiable, and one design constant the fix pass changed and explicitly flagged for sign-off.
blocker.decision_1_pollution_gate: G6-1-SENS case 4 requires a pollution spike to move approval >= 8 points. Two independent proofs it cannot: (a) coalSmog = 40 + 120*(demand/supply), so each added plant LOWERS every plant emission — 158 coal plants move cityIndex(poll) 5 -> 9, and a wall-to-wall coal map ceilings at exactly 40 vs the +45 required; (b) it is jointly unsatisfiable with G6-0-REF, which caps the control city penalty below 0.35 — with the measured pollution ceiling ratio of 1.99x, no divisor satisfies both and the maximum achievable swing is 4.16 points. The fix DID make the term real (was dead weight worth 0.60 points on the reference city; now 3.44, up to 6.86 at the industrial ceiling) and pollution still ranks #1 on the attribution gates. Options: re-specify with a reachable input (~3-point bar), or cover pollution under attribution only.
blocker.decision_2_recall_threshold: The fix pass moved RECALL_T 25 -> 40 and the mood bands 85/70/55/40/25 -> 88/76/64/52/40, measuring first: a maximally wrecked city (every station razed, all funding 0, tax 20, treasury -50k, a third of blocks dark, cross-streets bulldozed) settles at a SUSTAINED approval of 36.7-38.7, because the collapse removes the congestion/crime/unemployment grievances along with the citizens who held them. At 25 the recall newspaper and the bottom two mood bands were unreachable dead art. The structural alternative is to add a 16th APPROVAL_TERMS row for abandonment/vacancy (1 - developed/zoned — the one grievance that survives a collapse) weighted ~12, taken off pollution. NOTE: that abandonment grievance is exactly what GP10 (Blight & Urban Renewal) models, so deferring it there is coherent.
blocker.pre_existing_flagged_not_touched: MEGA_POLL = 55 is a threshold on cityIndex(poll) whose absolute ceiling is 40, so the clean-air half of the Megalopolis gate never binds (G6-8 passes on other grounds, so changing it would alter a passing gate). Same class: advisors.js "poll >= 120" line and COMPLAINT_T.poll = 100 are both unreachable.
blocker.tree_state: Implement + 3 fix/reconcile passes are LIVE in the tree and committed as checkpoints (b3eaf92, ffb712e, b3d780c), NOT shipped. RECALL_T = 40 is currently live pending decision 2.

milestones.title: The Assessed-Value Shadow Ledger & the Equilibrium Spike (read-only, byte-identical)
milestones.scope:
Ship the ruler before anything bills on it. Six read-only deliverables, zero sim-behavior change.

(1) THE SPIKE FIRST, on the UNCHANGED build. Consume the already-pinned reference city at docs/gp1-baseline.json .protocol.build_script VERBATIM (map=80, ticks=600, starting_funds=200000, disasters=false, 20 corpus_seeds) — do NOT mint a new one. The script never sets taxRate so it runs at the 7% default (index.html:143, slider min=0 max=20); the sweep sets c.taxRate explicitly before ticking. Publish docs/gp7-spike.json: per-seed equilibrium pop AND realized monthly revenue at tick 600 for rates 0..20, plus a measured sensitivity for EACH candidate binding term — taxMod (js/sim.js:4168 `const taxMod = (7 - this.taxRate) * 0.05`) vs jobsAvail/220 (definition js/sim.js:4184, division js/sim.js:4228) — and NAME which binds equilibrium. Record the drift finding that taxMod is ALREADY strictly linear over the whole authored 0..20 range and peaks at |0.65| against clampD's [-1,1] (js/sim.js:1788): GP7b's curve work is a shape CHOICE, not a repair.

(2) City.assessedLedger() — a PURE read. The per-tile base(zone,lvl) x assessment(landv) accumulation FUSES INTO computeDemandParts() (js/sim.js:4144-4195), whose loop already branches ZR/ZC/ZI with lvl[] in hand at js/sim.js:4152-4166 — the GP2 portAnchors precedent at js/sim.js:4150-4151 (writes only into `out`, zero allocation). It adds this.landv[i] reads to that ONE loop. NOT deptCosts() (js/sim.js:4902-4944): no zone branch, never reads lvl[]/landv[], and re-run on every funding-slider drag from js/ui.js:1108. NOT a fifth whole-map scan beside computeDemandParts/deptCosts/deptStrain/approvalCensus. Base tables sit beside RES_POP/COM_JOB/IND_JOB (js/sim.js:365-367). The ledger returns {rBase,cBase,iBase, assessed:{r,c,i}, headcount, cleanTax, ratio}. BYTE-IDENTITY: the new fields are written to `out` and read by NOTHING in recomputeDemand — demand.r/c/i (js/sim.js:4228-4230) stay character-identical, so every `dem > 0.15` comparison and the growth RNG stream are untouched.

(3) ONE definition of today's take. Introduce City.taxTake() holding the live expression character-for-character from js/sim.js:5185-5187 — `Math.round(this.pop*this.taxRate*0.28 + this.jobs*this.taxRate*0.18) + cleanTax`, cleanTax per CLEAN_TAX_RATE (js/sim.js:1447). collectBudget calls it; advTaxesAt (js/advisors.js:387-389, called twice at :403) delegates instead of holding its own copy; the taxMod copy at js/advisors.js:404 reads the same source as js/sim.js:4168; the now-false doc comments at js/advisors.js:373-375 and :379-381 are corrected. This closes the drift finding that advTaxesAt silently OMITS cleanTax and already disagrees with collectBudget on a clean-industry city (a readout correction; the charged integer does not move).

(4) Budget dialog (fillBudgetTable, js/ui.js:1103-1150): a clearly-labelled PREVIEW block — 'Assessed valuation (not charged)' with per-sector projected take R/C/I and the delta vs today's headcount bill. The GP5b 'incl. High-tech premium' row at js/ui.js:1131-1132 is preserved verbatim.

(5) WEALTH BANDS on the EXISTING `value` minimap mode — a land-value mode already ships end to end (index.html:101 `data-mode="value"`, js/render.js:2264-2266, MM_LEGENDS js/ui.js:749, MM_NAMES js/ui.js:774). Quantize the ramp at js/render.js:2265 into named bands and reword the legend. Retuning the shipped mode (not adding a 14th) means MM_NAMES needs no new key, so the unguarded `${MM_NAMES[mode]}` at js/ui.js:781 cannot print `undefined` — gated anyway.

(6) SAVE v18 + the guard the ladder rule already required. history.assess (the monthly shadow take) pushed LAST after `approv`, extended in BOTH key lists — normaliseHistory js/sim.js:31 and the >240 trim loop js/sim.js:5274. Bump `v: 17` to `v: 18` at js/sim.js:5652. Add the missing typeof guard at js/sim.js:5756 (`c.taxRate = d.taxRate` is unguarded today, unlike every sibling) using the funding-merge idiom at js/sim.js:5766-5767, defaulting to 7 — this removes GP7b's NaN-demand poisoning hazard before per-zone rates land. Plus one ADVISORY_GATES row (js/sim.js:1745, walked ONLY by _attachAdvisories js/sim.js:4508-4520, draw-neutral) surfacing a developed tile's would-be assessment in the inspector. NEVER GROWTH_GATES. LAUNCH CONDITION (preflight, non-negotiable): the gate problems recorded in preflight_gate_problems below were found by an adversarial reviewer that read the LIVE source and MEASURED the unchanged build. The design phase MUST resolve every one before implementation, and each resolution must be reported in the ship verdict with its measurement. Rules for resolving: an IMPOSSIBILITY (unachievable/self-contradictory/vacuous — the sim arithmetic or the fixture cannot produce the quantity) is corrected by re-specifying the gate so it measures the intended property with a reachable bar, and the correction is recorded with the measurement proving the original was impossible. An ABSOLUTE-SHOULD-BE-COMPARATIVE bar is restated per the R1 protocol (this build vs baseline on identical scripted inputs). An AMBIGUOUS-THRESHOLD gate is pinned to a named city, seed, sample count and reference quantity. An UNMEASURABLE gate is either given a concrete headless observable or reported to the user as needing a design decision. A resolution that changes what the milestone is TRYING TO ACHIEVE (rather than how it is measured) is a DESIGN decision — surface it to the user, never decide it (S6). Also close every missing_coverage item or justify its omission.
milestones.player_facing_win: Open the budget and see, right next to the bill you actually pay, what your city would be worth if land value were the tax base — and a wealth-band map showing which blocks are prime and which are cheap. Nothing you are charged changes yet; the ruler is proven honest first.
quality_gates: BYTE-IDENTICAL SIM: 20 corpus_seeds x 600 ticks on docs/gp1-baseline.json .protocol.build_script verbatim, Math.random UNSTUBBED. Array hashes for terr/over/lvl/varnt/anc/roadWear/traffic/landv/poll/crime and the scalar series pop/funds/jobs/demand.r/demand.c/demand.i/lastBudget.taxes/lastBudget.net match HEAD exactly. Bar: 0 differing bytes, 0 of 20 seeds differ.

SPIKE PUBLISHED AND DECISIVE: docs/gp7-spike.json exists, cites the pinned script + the 20 corpus_seeds, and contains for rates 0..20 the tick-600 equilibrium pop and realized monthly revenue on >=20 seeds, plus a numeric elasticity (d revenue / d term at the equilibrium point) for BOTH taxMod and jobsAvail/220, and a one-line verdict naming the binding term. Bar: all 21 rates x 20 seeds present (>=420 rows), both elasticities numeric, verdict present. Measured on the unchanged build.

LEDGER AGREES WITH THE BILL, AND ADDS NO SCAN: (a) assessedLedger().headcount === city.lastBudget.taxes at EVERY month rollover across 20 seeds x 600 ticks — bar: 0 mismatches. (b) advTaxesAt(city.taxRate) === city.lastBudget.taxes over 50 sampled states including >=10 clean-industry states — bar: 0 divergences (today it diverges on every clean-industry city).
