Bar: SHADOW assessed take differs by >=35%, while the ACTUAL charged take differs by <=2% — proving the ruler reads land value before anything bills on it.

S4 VISIBILITY: (a) minimap pixel-hash of the banded `value` mode is IDENTICAL at cam.r 0/1/2/3 (renderMinimap is north-up, js/render.js:2243 — assert it, do not assume). (b) The lowest band differs from the highest by >=60 in at least two RGB channels. (c) Object.keys(MM_LEGENDS) and Object.keys(MM_NAMES) are set-equal, and rendering all 13 modes produces non-empty legends with zero occurrences of the substring 'undefined'. (d) A developed tile's assessment is readable in the inspector at all 4 rotations.

SAVE v18 / DETERMINISM: v18 written at js/sim.js:5652; v17 and v12 saves load with 0 console errors and no version-equality test anywhere; a save with taxRate deleted, null, or a string loads at taxRate 7 and yields finite (non-NaN) demand.r/c/i over 120 rollovers — bar: 0 NaN. serialize->deserialize->serialize is byte-identical (idempotent round-trip). history.assess present in BOTH js/sim.js:31 and js/sim.js:5274; after 300 rollovers all 11 series have equal length — bar: 0 length mismatches. Same seed + script reproduces identical series over 600 ticks with Math.random UNSTUBBED.

NO DUPLICATE FORMULA LEFT BEHIND: exactly ONE arithmetic site in the tree computes the headcount take (grep for the 0.28/0.18 coefficient pair across js/ — bar: 1 hit, in js/sim.js) and exactly ONE computes taxMod (bar: 1 hit, js/sim.js:4168; js/advisors.js:404's copy delegates). The stale prose at js/advisors.js:373-375 and :379-381 matches the live code. Bar: 0 second copies, 0 false comments.
milestones.split_rationale: The read half is emphatically not vacuous: today NOTHING in the game shows what a tile is worth or what it would pay. The shadow ledger, the per-sector projected take, the banded wealth map and the spike are all pure reads over state that already exists (landv is a live derived Uint8Array, js/sim.js:1840), so they earn a real byte-identical gate. Three drift findings force this ordering. (a) The scope named deptCosts() as the accumulation home; deptCosts has no zone branch at all and is re-run on every slider drag — the correct home is computeDemandParts, and proving that fusion costs zero new scans and zero behavior change is exactly what a byte-identical half is for. (b) The scope quoted a PRE-GP5b tax expression; a behavior-first cutover transcribing it silently deletes the certified GP5b clean-industry premium and orphans js/ui.js:1131. Routing every consumer through one taxTake() FIRST makes that deletion impossible later. (c) The taxRate load at js/sim.js:5756 is unguarded; adding per-zone rates on top of it turns any malformed save into NaN demand citywide. Fixing the guard in the read half is free and de-risks GP7b. Finally, gate 1 of the original spec is itself a read deliverable and it decides GP7b's rate structure — running it after the cutover would make it unmeasurable.
milestones.save_version_plan: GP7a takes v18; GP7b takes v19. GP7a: bump `v: 17` to `v: 18` at js/sim.js:5652 for the one new serialized series, history.assess (the monthly shadow assessed take), pushed LAST after `approv` and added to BOTH key lists — normaliseHistory js/sim.js:31 and the >240 trim loop js/sim.js:5274 (the SECOND LIST WARNING at js/sim.js:23-27 and :5270-5272). A v17 save does NOT load with assess=[] — that clause was WRONG and is corrected here (design D3). normaliseHistory left-pads every SHORT series with zeros up to the longest key's length, because the M30 "loads as [] and records forward" idiom is silently broken once a city's history reaches the 240 cap: the trim at the end of collectBudget then fires on every rollover and shifts every key in its list, so a series that starts empty pushes 1 and is shifted straight back to 0, forever (preflight problem P5). The pad fires whenever the longest key is non-empty, not only at the cap. MEASURED: a v17 save taken from a 120-tick city (history length 5) loads with assess.length 5, zero-filled; a v17 save padded to the 240 cap loads with assess.length 240 and, after 800 further ticks, all 11 series are 240 and equal. assess === [] therefore holds for exactly one case, a save with NO history at all. Two consequences are USER DECISIONS, surfaced not decided (see design_user_decisions below): the zero-fill writes fabricated §0 months the shadow ledger never measured, and the same pad retroactively repairs commute / avgcom / approv on mature pre-v17 saves. GP7a ALSO lands the guard the ladder rule already required but that js/sim.js:5756 never had: `c.taxRate = d.taxRate` is unguarded, unlike every sibling field — replace with a typeof number check defaulting to 7, copying the funding-merge idiom at js/sim.js:5766-5767. This changes nothing on any well-formed save and removes GP7b's NaN-demand hazard. GP7b: v19 for credit-rating memory (new persisted state — creditRating at js/sim.js:673-680 is memoryless today), the urban-renewal key in this.funding (defaults js/sim.js:1992, merged on load at js/sim.js:5766-5767 so a v18 save loads at its default), the chooseable bond term, and per-zone rates if the separability measurement passes — a legacy scalar taxRate fans into every rate. Existing bonds need no migration: each serialized record already carries its own {principal, rate, term, remaining, monthly, balance} (js/sim.js:4861-4862, serialized at js/sim.js:5659), so amortization at js/sim.js:5204-5217 must keep reading b.* and never the global BOND_TERM. Both halves load every earlier version with defensive typeof/Array.isArray guards and NEVER a version-equality test. If the user prefers the read half not to touch the ladder at all, dropping history.assess (keeping the shadow ledger live-only in the budget dialog) lets GP7a ship at v17 unchanged, GP5a-style — but the month-over-month shadow-vs-actual series is the most legible part of the readout, so v18 is recommended.
milestones.launch_order_note:
Strict order: GP7a fully certified before GP7b begins. Three hard dependencies, not preferences. (1) GP7a's spike (docs/gp7-spike.json) is what DECIDES GP7b's rate structure and curve target; run after the cutover it measures a build that no longer exists. (2) GP7b's outcome gates are all stated in terms of realized take and assessed value — the numbers assessedLedger() reports. Those numbers are only admissible as evidence because GP7a's byte-identical gate proved the ledger agrees with the bill (0 mismatches over 20 seeds x 600 ticks) while changing nothing. (3) GP7a routes collectBudget, advTaxesAt and the advisor taxMod copy through single definitions and adds the missing taxRate load guard — doing the cutover first would, per the drift report, silently delete the certified GP5b cleanTax revenue line and its js/ui.js:1131 budget row, and would put per-zone rates on top of an unguarded load that NaN-poisons demand citywide.

S6 REPORTS FOR THE USER, NOT AMENDMENTS. Three items in the original spec are wrong in ways a worker must not quietly fix: (a) quality_gates[3] and [4] set absolute "in >=8 of 10 seeded runs" bars — the exact shape R1 already ruled mis-specified once, when the reference script never won two scenarios on EITHER build. GP7b's gates 4 and 5 above are restated COMPARATIVE against the pinned GP6 baseline worktree on identical scripted solutions; the user should confirm that restatement or supply different bars. (b) quality_gates[4] says "all 5 scenarios" — js/scenarios.js:91-286 contains exactly FOUR (gridlock-97, twister-season, blackout-summer-97, y2k-ready), so the gate was uncountable as written; restated over the four real ids. (c) The scope's stated accumulation home (deptCosts) and several of its line numbers are wrong by 2,600-3,000 lines against a 6,011-line js/sim.js; the split above is grounded in today's source and supersedes them.

S8 / S2 FLAG: GP7b as scoped is the largest behavior surface remaining in the plan — cutover, rate structure, curve reshape, assessed floor, urban-renewal line, debt ladder with rating memory, served-load upkeep, and railCov in the landv fold, carrying TWO independent declared re-pins. Recommend planning for a further split at GP7b's own launch (a natural seam is: cutover + assessed floor + no-free-surplus first, then debt ladder + urban renewal + transit-in-rent), and note that if GP7b is refuted twice the S2 two-strike rule forbids a third whole attempt. GP6 is live-but-uncertified at HEAD b3d780c (last SHIP a702c92, GP5b): GP7b touches GP6 surface — the APPROVAL_TERMS `tax` row at js/sim.js:1645-1649 reads the scalar c.taxRate twice — so treat GP6 as landing, not certified, and do not depend on its unshipped details.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7a quality_gates[3] — LAND VALUE SEPARATES IN THE SHADOW ONLY ('watered upper half vs dry lower half, pop and jobs each within 2%, mean landv differs by >=60')
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The named fixture cannot produce the measured quantity. The pinned build_script zones by BAND: y<30 zr, y<52 zc, y>=52 zi. The watered upper half (rows 4..43) therefore holds essentially ALL residential pop and almost no industry; the dry lower half holds the industry and ~zero pop. 'Pop and jobs each within 2%' between those two halves is impossible by construction. MEASURED landv gap between halves on 5 corpus seeds: 15.7, 19.6, 5.9, 8.9, 8.1 (all tiles) and 23.1 on developed tiles for seed 1 — the >=60 bar is nowhere near reachable on this fixture. Separately, the second half of the gate ('ACTUAL charged take differs by <=2%') is ALGEBRAICALLY IMPLIED by the selection criterion: today's take is round(pop*rate*0.28 + jobs*rate*0.18) + cleanTax, a linear function of pop and jobs, so matching pop and jobs within 2% forces the take within ~2% on any build — it proves nothing.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Build TWO purpose-made pinned sub-cities (not the halves of the reference city) matched on pop and jobs, and state the separation over DEVELOPED tiles where the spread is real (measured: 10.0 in a saturated-industry city vs 73.0 in a park-saturated city). Suggested bar: developed-tile mean landv differing by >=35, SHADOW assessed take differing by >=35%. Drop the '<=2% actual take' clause or replace it with the meaningful check: the charged integer is byte-identical to HEAD on both cities (already covered by gate 1).

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7a quality_gates[2](a) — 'assessedLedger().headcount === city.lastBudget.taxes at EVERY month rollover ... bar: 0 mismatches'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Three problems. (1) DECOMPOSITION: the scope defines the ledger's return as {..., headcount, cleanTax, ...} and defines taxTake() as round(pop*rate*0.28 + jobs*rate*0.18) + cleanTax, while lastBudget.taxes INCLUDES cleanTax (js/sim.js:5185-5187). So on any clean-industry city 'headcount === lastBudget.taxes' is false by exactly cleanTax — the gate contradicts the ledger shape the same scope defines, and gate 2(b) simultaneously insists cleanTax must be included. (2) VACUOUS AS RUN: MEASURED isCleanInd() === false on the pinned reference city at tick 600, so the 20-seed x 600-tick run never exercises cleanTax at all — the sub-gate passes trivially either way. (3) TIMING TRAP: if assessedLedger() re-measures rather than reading the committed _dparts snapshot, it CANNOT hit 0 mismatches — the source already documents this exact hazard for demandBreakdown (js/sim.js ~4245: recomputeDemand runs at the top of tick() and growthPass then moves pop/jobs underneath it, 'measured divergence up to 0.34'). And a re-scanning ledger called every rollover by the gate's own harness perturbs the scan count gate 2(c) measures.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Split it: '(a1) ledger.headcount + ledger.cleanTax === lastBudget.taxes at every rollover across 20 seeds — 0 mismatches; (a2) the same identity on >=10 purpose-built clean-industry cities where cleanTax > 0 — 0 mismatches; (a3) assessedLedger() is specified to read the committed _dparts snapshot, never a fresh census, and gate 2(c)'s scan count is measured with the ledger harness detached.'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[4] — CALIBRATION AND SCENARIO SAFETY ('this build wins on >= as many corpus_seeds as baseline for every scenario')
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Scenario cities are NOT seeded by the corpus: each SCENARIOS entry pins its own seed in source (gridlock-97 971104, twister-season 51996, blackout-summer-97 970601, y2k-ready 990704; js/scenarios.js:67 'new City(o.seed, 80)'). There is no corpus_seed axis to count wins over, so 'wins on >= as many corpus_seeds' is uncountable as written. The established harness varies k = 0..9 (the scripted reference solution at scratchpad/gp1b-scenario-ref.mjs jitters placements and slider timing by k), which is the axis the earlier '>= 8 of 10 seeded playthroughs' bar referred to. The gate's calibration clause also consumes 'the GP6 baseline's mean monthly take over rollovers 480-600', a number nothing in GP7a produces (GP7a's spike publishes tick-600 point values).
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'For each of the four scenarios, run the pinned scripted solution at k = 0..9 on this build and on the pinned GP6 baseline worktree (:8902). Bar: this build wins on >= as many of the 10 playthroughs as baseline for every scenario, and 0 scenario-k pairs regress.' And have GP7a's spike publish the 7% take as a mean over the same window GP7b calibrates against, so the calibration reference exists on the unchanged build.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7a quality_gates[1] — 'a numeric elasticity (d revenue / d term at the equilibrium point) for BOTH taxMod and jobsAvail/220 ... Measured on the unchanged build'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: taxMod is parameterised (vary taxRate), but jobsAvail/220 (js/sim.js:4184/4228) has NO knob: it is a derived census term, so 'd revenue / d term' for it cannot be measured on an unchanged build without injecting an offset — which is a modified build, contradicting the gate's own 'measured on the unchanged build' clause. The two elasticities are also not commensurable: taxMod enters demand.r/c/i with weights 1 / 0.6 / 0.4 while jobsAvail/220 enters only demand.r. MEASURED, the honest answer the gate is groping for is not an elasticity at all: at the reference equilibrium jobsAvail/220 = 2.51 against clampD's ceiling of 1.0 (js/sim.js:1788), so demand.r is SATURATED and taxMod's full |0.65| swing moves residential demand by exactly 0 for every rate from 0 to ~13. An elasticity number would report 0 for taxMod and be undefined for the other term, hiding the actual finding.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Replace the elasticity pair with a directly measurable saturation report: 'for each rate 0..20 publish the PRE-CLAMP raw demand.r/c/i and the clamp headroom, and state at which rate each bar leaves the clamp — bar: raw values and clamp flags present for all 21 rates x 20 seeds, plus a one-line verdict naming the binding term and the rate at which it starts binding.'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7a quality_gates[5] — 'history.assess present in BOTH js/sim.js:31 and js/sim.js:5274; after 300 rollovers all 11 series have equal length — bar: 0 length mismatches'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The gate does not say WHICH city. On a fresh city it passes. On a LOADED mature v17 save it cannot: the trim at js/sim.js:5273-5275 fires on this.history.pop.length > 240 and then shifts EVERY key, so a save whose history is already at the 240 cap pushes assess to 1 and immediately shifts it back to 0 on every rollover — history.assess stays permanently EMPTY, forever, and the lengths never equalise. The save_version_plan's claim that a v17 save 'loads with assess=[] and records forward (the M30 idiom)' is therefore false for any city older than 240 months. (Note 600 ticks = 25 rollovers, so this state needs ~5,760 ticks or a long-played save — it will be found by a player, not by the gate.)
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the fixture and add the migration: '(i) fresh city, 300 rollovers: all 11 series equal length; (ii) a v17 save whose history is at the 240 cap, loaded and run 30 rollovers: history.assess is non-empty and all 11 series are equal length' — which forces normaliseHistory (or the load path) to left-pad a newly added series to the incumbent length instead of relying on push-forward.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[7](d) — 'mean per-tick wall time and budget-dialog slider-drag latency each within 110% of HEAD'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: No repetition count, no warm-up, no variance discipline, and no statement of which machine or which city — headless wall-time in this container swings well over 10% run to run, so the gate can fail (or pass) on noise while the code is unchanged. GP7a's gate 2(c) already demonstrates the deterministic alternative (an instrumented count of full-length over[] iterations).
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Gate on deterministic operation counts plus a loose timing sanity band: 'instrumented count of full-length over[] passes per tick, and per drag of a funding slider, equals HEAD exactly (deptCosts adds no per-tile pass); AND median per-tick wall time over 5 runs x 600 ticks after one warm-up run is within 125% of HEAD measured in the same session.'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7a quality_gates[6] — 'grep for the 0.28/0.18 coefficient pair across js/ — bar: 1 hit, in js/sim.js'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The grep is not well defined and fails for unrelated reasons as literally written. '0.28' alone currently hits js/sim.js:4229, :4267 and :4280 (the demand.c shopper term and its breakdown rows), plus js/render.js, js/sprites.js and js/audio.js; and the advisors doc comment the same gate wants corrected writes the constants as '.28' / '.18', which a '0.28' grep misses entirely. A worker can also pass the bar trivially by hoisting the literals into a named constant.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'Exactly one LINE in js/ matches the regex 0\\.28[^\\n]*0\\.18 (the pair on one line), and it is in js/sim.js; and exactly one line matches \\(7 *- *[a-zA-Z.]*[Tt]axRate\\) *\\* *0\\.05. Doc comments may restate the formula only by naming taxTake()/taxMod, never by repeating the literals.'

preflight_missing_coverage: taxTake() as scoped has NO rate parameter, but advTaxesAt(rate) is called with the OLD rate at js/advisors.js:403 (advTaxesAt(O) vs advTaxesAt(N)) to compute the projected revenue loss. GP7a gate 2(b) only tests advTaxesAt(city.taxRate), so a delegation that ignores the argument passes every gate while making `loss` identically 0 and printing 'a projected §0 a month gone' in the Transportation advisor's protest. Needs a gate: advTaxesAt(r) for r in 0..20 on >=10 states equals a city-independent recomputation at rate r (including cleanTax scaling with r), not just at the live rate.

GP7b cutover has no gate retiring GP7a's PREVIEW framing: the budget block is shipped in GP7a labelled 'Assessed valuation (not charged)' (js/ui.js:1103-1150). After the cutover that label is a lie on screen and the GP5b 'incl. High-tech premium' row's relationship to the new bill is unstated. Needs an S4 gate on the post-cutover budget dialog text and on the preserved js/ui.js:1131-1132 row.

GP7b(6) TRANSIT IN RENT is the milestone's headline player-facing promise ('rail finally shows up as rent') and is a declared RNG re-pin (landv -> gFit at js/sim.js:1079), yet no gate measures it: nothing isolates railCov's contribution to landv, nothing shows it in the wealth-band map or inspector at 4 rotations, and no outcome gate compares realized take for a rail-served vs identical rail-less pinned city.

GP7b(5) 're-tie upkeep to SERVED LOAD by CONSUMING deptStrain/approvalCensus, never a second definition of load' is unmeasured. Gates cover perf and the surplus band but nothing asserts the bill and the strain meters agree — e.g. deptCosts' load inputs are bit-identical to the popLoad/jobLoad/structures and roadTiles/jam/jamShare the meters display, on the same tick, across 20 seeds.

Per-zone rates have no gate on the GP6 surfaces that read the SCALAR c.taxRate: APPROVAL_TERMS 'tax' row (js/sim.js:1645-1649, both the pen() penalty and the blurb) and js/advisors.js:192-199's three branches. Approval is an EMA carry that IS serialized, so an undefined/NaN taxRate there poisons persisted state permanently. Needs: approval finite and the survey/advisor strings free of 'undefined'/'NaN' under per-zone rates, across 120 rollovers and a save round-trip.

Nothing certifies the READOUT against the ledger. GP7a gate 2 proves assessedLedger() agrees with the bill, and gate 4 proves the minimap bands render, but no gate ties the numbers rendered in fillBudgetTable's preview (per-sector projected take R/C/I and the delta) to assessedLedger()'s {assessed.r/c/i, headcount} fields — the UI could print a differently-derived number and pass every gate.

GP7b gate 6(c) (credit-rating downgrade fires exactly once) has no fixture guaranteeing a downgrade occurs: on the pinned corpus the reference city runs a permanent surplus (measured funds 200,000 -> 440,865 over 600 ticks at 7%), so a 600-tick run may never downgrade and the '1 message per transition' bar is vacuous. Needs a scripted forced-downgrade (and forced-upgrade) fixture.

No gate covers the interaction between the new assessed FLOOR and the equilibrium-revenue curve at rate 0: with a floor, take is no longer 0 at 0% tax, which changes what 'revenue at 0%' means in gate 2 and creates an unattended-income path the no-free-surplus gate measures only at the calibrated rate. Either gate revenue at rate 0 explicitly, or state that the floor is rate-scaled.
milestones.split_of: GP7 (preflight-authored S3 split, grounded against the live source 2026-07-30)

design_gate_respecifications.preamble: GP7a design pass (S3 design phase, launch condition of the milestone's own scope block). Every preflight_gate_problem below was resolved BEFORE implementation and each resolution is recorded here with the measurement that forced it. Rule followed: an IMPOSSIBILITY is re-specified so it measures the intended property with a reachable bar; an AMBIGUOUS-THRESHOLD gate is pinned to a named city, seed and sample count; nothing was amended to make the work pass. The 16 criteria C1..C16 are the executable form of quality_gates[0..6] after these corrections.
design_gate_respecifications.P1_land_value_separates: quality_gates[3]. IMPOSSIBILITY, confirmed. The pinned script's band zoning makes a pop/jobs match between the watered and dry halves impossible by construction, and the '<=2% actual take' clause is algebraically implied by the selection criterion (today's take is linear in pop and jobs). MEASURED landv gap between halves on 5 corpus seeds: 15.7 / 19.6 / 5.9 / 8.9 / 8.1 — the >=60 bar is unreachable. RE-SPECIFIED (C8) over two purpose-built pinned fixtures committed verbatim in docs/gp7-spike.json .fixtures.prime/.cheap, both on the reference three-band split so land-value drivers are the ONLY authored difference, and over the SCALE-FREE statistic ledger.ratio (the assessed-base-weighted mean assessment), which needs no pop/jobs match. MEASURED LIVE through assessedLedger(): developed-tile mean landv 73.91 vs 37.47 (gap 36.44, bar >=35) and ratio 1.1206 vs 0.8225 (separation 36.24%, bar >=35%). The dropped '<=2% charged' clause is replaced by the meaningful check that both fixture cities are plane- and scalar-identical to b3d780c.
design_gate_respecifications.P2_ledger_reconciles: quality_gates[2](a). SELF-CONTRADICTORY, VACUOUS AND TIMING-TRAPPED, confirmed; split into three (C3/C4/C5). C3: the identity is headcount + cleanTax === lastBudget.taxes, not headcount === lastBudget.taxes (measured 0 mismatches over 125 rollovers on 5 seeds). C4: the pinned corpus NEVER exercises cleanTax — MEASURED isCleanInd() false at tick 600 with eduLevel 0.0046 — so the (a) clause was vacuous on the named fixture and a separate forced clean-industry fixture (eduLevel 0.9, a serialized scalar) is mandatory; measured 12/12 rollovers with cleanTax 852 and 0 identity mismatches. C5: assessedLedger() is specified to read the this._dparts snapshot, and the scan-count gate is measured with the ledger harness DETACHED (measured 0 added scans either way).
design_gate_respecifications.P3_gp7b_scenario_gate: OUT OF GP7a SCOPE, reported forward to GP7b: scenario seeds are pinned in source, not corpus-derived, so that gate is uncountable as written. GP7a's own obligation — publish the take as a mean over the window GP7b calibrates against — is DISCHARGED: docs/gp7-spike.json carries meanTakeWindow per row over rollovers 19..25.
design_gate_respecifications.P4_elasticity: quality_gates[1]. UNMEASURABLE ON AN UNCHANGED BUILD, confirmed, and replaced by the saturation report (C2). MEASURED: saturation.firstUnclampedRate {r:19, c:0, i:0} — the residential bar is pinned against clampD's +1 ceiling on all 20 seeds up to rate 14, so taxMod's full |0.65| swing moves demand.r by exactly 0 there. A numeric elasticity would have reported 0 and HIDDEN the finding; the published pre-clamp raw / headroom / clamped flag / medianJobsAvailOver220 per rate report it instead. The gate's 'both elasticities numeric' clause is struck and 21/21 saturation rows plus a verdict naming the binding term stand in its place.
design_gate_respecifications.P5_history_assess_cannot_grow: quality_gates[5]. CONFIRMED and fixed by the left pad in normaliseHistory (see save_version_plan above). SIDE EFFECT: quality_gates[4]'s 'v17 and older saves load clean with the new series EMPTY' clause and this fix are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. The MEASUREMENT is re-specified as C12 (short v17 save -> assess zero-filled to the incumbent length and all 11 series equal; a save with NO history -> assess === []; mature save -> 240 at load and 240 after 800 ticks), but the underlying choice — zero-fill vs null-padding — is a DESIGN decision and is surfaced, not decided (design_user_decisions U1/U2).
design_gate_respecifications.P6_wall_time: OUT OF GP7a SCOPE (GP7b's gate) but GP7a supplies the evidence and the alternative (C16): deterministic instrumented scan counts as the deciding bar, wall time only as a loose sanity band. MEASURED PROOF OF THE NOISE: mean per-tick wall time 0.327 ms on the implemented build vs 0.723 ms on the UNCHANGED baseline in the same session — a 2.2x swing between builds doing identical work, so a +/-10% wall-time bar decides on noise.
design_gate_respecifications.P7_grep_bars: quality_gates[6]. AMBIGUOUS-THRESHOLD, pinned to two line regexes (C14). MEASURED: `0\.28[^\n]*0\.18` -> exactly 1 hit, js/sim.js inside taxTake(). The preflight's OWN suggested taxMod regex `\(7 *- *[a-zA-Z.]*[Tt]axRate\) *\* *0\.05` now returns ZERO hits, because the single definition takes a parameter named `rate`; the correct bar is `\(7 *- *[A-Za-z._]+\) *\* *0\.05` -> exactly 1 hit, js/sim.js taxModFor(). A naive '0.28' grep also misses the '.28'/'.18' shorthand, so the advisor doc comments are read directly as part of the gate.
design_gate_respecifications.rollover_window: quality_gates[2]'s 'rollovers 480-600' clause is UNREACHABLE: the rollover block is a %24 gate, so 600 ticks on the pinned protocol produce exactly 25 rollovers per seed (measured 125 over 5 seeds). Restated everywhere as 'rollovers 19..25 (ticks 456..600)', which is the window docs/gp7-spike.json already publishes.
design_gate_respecifications.missing_coverage_closed: (i) advTaxesAt(r) rate-parameter coverage — C10 sweeps all 21 rates over >=60 states including 10 forced clean-industry ones (measured 0 divergences, spread 0 -> 37745, so a delegation that ignored its argument cannot pass). (ii) 'nothing certifies the READOUT against the ledger' — C9 parses the rendered #budget-table DOM and compares field by field to assessedLedger() (measured exact: r 7257 / c 1385 / i 1364 / total 10007 / billed 13211 === lastBudget.taxes / diff -3204 / '76% of the bill'). (iii) 'no gate covers revenue at rate 0' — the spike publishes take === 0 for every seed at rate 0 (drift finding 4), the reference point GP7b's floor question needs.
design_gate_respecifications.missing_coverage_deferred: Deferred to GP7b WITH JUSTIFICATION, all in the behavior half explicitly out of GP7a's read-only scope: retiring the '(not charged)' PREVIEW label after the cutover; transit-in-rent (railCov in the landv fold); served-load upkeep vs deptStrain/approvalCensus; per-zone rates on GP6's APPROVAL_TERMS and advisor surfaces — GP7a's taxRate load guard already removes the NaN-poisoning hazard those gates worry about (MEASURED: baseline NaN-poisons demand for 300/300 ticks on a taxRate-deleted save, this build 0/300); forced credit-rating downgrade fixture.
design_gate_respecifications.s4_visibility_gap_closed: Design D1. history.assess was serialized at v18 with NO visible expression — UI.graphSeries had no `assess` descriptor and #graph-series-strip no checkbox, so the only readout was the live budget block, which S4 and the milestone's own player_facing_win do not allow. FIXED on the GP6 `approv` precedent: one graphSeries descriptor (color #0a7d6a, label 'Assessed take', `idx` OMITTED so drawGraphLegend prints the § prefix like tax/net, seriesData's 100yr branch falling through to the monthly tail) plus one checkbox in index.html after the approv row, OFF by default so the default graph render stays pixel-identical. ONE DEVIATION FROM THE DESIGN, forced by a defect the design's 'idx OMITTED' instruction would have introduced: openGraphs' 100yr right-edge span label divides a series' point count by 12 iff `idx` is set, because until now `idx` doubled as the 'this series has no ANNUAL record and falls back to the monthly tail' signal — every tail-falling series happened to be an index. assess is money (no `idx`, so the legend prints §) but has no annual record, so with `idx` simply omitted a 240-month tail would caption as 'yr 240' instead of 'yr 20'. The two meanings are therefore separated: assess declares a new `monthly: true` flag and the span reducer tests `(idx || monthly)`. No shipped series changes value or path (all six annual/index descriptors are untouched), and the default render is unaffected because assess is off by default.
design_gate_respecifications.false_comments_fixed: Design D2, required by quality_gates[6]'s '0 false comments' bar. js/sim.js normaliseHistory's comment asserted that a v17 save short of the cap loads with assess === [] and only a capped one is padded — MEASURED FALSE (a 120-tick city's v17 save loads with assess.length 5, zero-filled). Rewritten to state what the code does. The ASSESS_* header comment's fixture figures were likewise re-stated against the LIVE ledger (cheap ratio 0.8225 / separation 36.24%, not the harness-side 0.8229 / 36.18%).
design_gate_respecifications.harness_discipline: Design D4, binding on the verify pass. (a) Prototype wrappers installed for whole-map scan counting MUST be restored before any later measurement in the same process, or every subsequent count is inflated. (b) A MAIN-CANVAS pixel hash is NOT a usable equality gate in this repo — three consecutive renderFrame passes on the SAME build produce three different hashes even with performance.now and Date.now frozen. Draw neutrality is therefore measured structurally (per-function source differential across the two builds) plus per-mode minimap hashes (C15/C11), never by hashing #game. (c) diagnoseTile takes a TILE INDEX, not (x, y).
design_gate_respecifications.baseline: Every identity comparison in C1..C16 is against b3d780c (GP6 live-but-uncertified), NOT a702c92.

design_user_decisions: U1 (BLOCKING THE SHIP VERDICT, not the code): quality_gates[4]'s clause 'v17 and older saves load clean with the new series EMPTY' and preflight problem P5's required fix are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. The left pad zero-fills assess to the incumbent length on every save that has any history (measured 5 on a 120-tick save, 240 on a capped save). Zero-fill writes fabricated §0 months the shadow ledger never measured; they will plot as a flat zero run in the new 'Assessed take' graph series until the first post-load rollover. The alternative — pad with null and teach the plotter to skip nulls — is a larger change to shipped M30 code. CONFIRM zero-fill, or choose null-padding.

U2: the same left pad RETROACTIVELY repairs commute / avgcom / approv for mature pre-v17 saves — a change to loaded state beyond GP7a's declared surface. Strictly additive and idempotent (round-trip measured byte-stable) but it is a load-path behavior change the milestone did not scope. CONFIRM.

U3 (lower stakes): if ZERO UI additions are wanted, D1's 'Assessed take' graph series can be dropped — but then history.assess has no visible expression at all and save_version_plan's own stated fallback applies: drop history.assess and ship GP7a at v17.

milestones.title: The Cutover, the Debt Ladder & the Stabilizer (declared re-pin, measured by GP7a)
milestones.scope:
Now re-pin against the instrumentation GP7a proved honest.

(1) CUTOVER: the tax line at js/sim.js:5185-5187 switches from headcount to the assessed sum assessedLedger() already computes, carrying cleanTax forward VERBATIM (CLEAN_TAX_RATE js/sim.js:1447, budget row js/ui.js:1131-1132 must survive). Calibrated so the pinned reference city at 7% collects within +/-10% of the GP6 baseline take.

(2) RATE STRUCTURE decided by GP7a's spike + the separability measurement, never assumed. If separability fails, ship ONE rate and publish the numbers.

(3) TAX CURVE: reshaping taxMod (js/sim.js:4168) is a DECLARED RE-PIN — it moves demand.r/c/i and therefore every `dem > 0.15` / `dem < -0.25` comparison in growthPass. demandBreakdown's rows (js/sim.js:4252-4287) must be updated in the SAME source order as the expressions at js/sim.js:4228-4230, never re-associated (the parts-sum-reproduces-raw invariant, js/sim.js:4233-4243).

(4) STABILIZER: (a) an assessed-value FLOOR per developed tile so revenue can never reach zero while developed tiles remain; (b) an urban-renewal budget line joining this.funding (defaults js/sim.js:1992, load merge js/sim.js:5766-5767) and fillBudgetTable (js/ui.js:1103-1150); (c) the REAL debt ladder — note the drift finding that BOND_PRINCIPAL is ALREADY a defaulted parameter (js/sim.js:4856 `issueBond(amount = BOND_PRINCIPAL)`) that flows through the annuity, the pushed record and the treasury; the UI simply never passes one (js/ui.js:1026). Genuinely new: a chooseable TERM (BOND_TERM js/sim.js:663 is hard-wired at js/sim.js:4860-4862), a ceiling tied to the assessed base replacing the flat BOND_MAX=4 (js/sim.js:664, :4857), and credit-rating MEMORY (creditRating js/sim.js:673-680 is purely memoryless today — memory is new serialized state). The amortization loop at js/sim.js:5204-5217 must keep reading b.term/b.remaining/b.monthly per bond and NEVER the global BOND_TERM, so serialized bonds (js/sim.js:4861-4862, js/sim.js:5659) keep loading. The button label at js/ui.js:1443 hardcodes BOND_PRINCIPAL and must show the chosen amount.

(5) NO FREE SURPLUS: re-tie road and service upkeep in deptCosts() (js/sim.js:4902-4944) to SERVED LOAD by CONSUMING deptStrain()'s existing popLoad/jobLoad/structures census (js/sim.js:4962-4996, load selection :4989-4990) and approvalCensus's roadTiles/jam/jamShare (js/sim.js:5040-5112, return :5101-5111) — never a second definition of load, or the strain meters and the bill will disagree. Keep deptCosts free of new per-tile work: it runs on every funding-slider drag (js/ui.js:1108) on top of deptStrain's scan (js/ui.js:1115).

(6) TRANSIT IN RENT (the milestone's own player-facing promise): railCov appears at js/sim.js:1826/1832/2611/2663/2980 but NEVER in the land-value fold at js/sim.js:3730-3741. Adding it is a second declared re-pin — landv feeds gFit (js/sim.js:1076-1099, landv read at :1079) -> gUpP -> applyUpgrade's growth-cursor draw.

(7) SAVE v19: rating memory, the urban-renewal funding key, chosen bond term, and per-zone rates if separable. A legacy scalar taxRate fans out into every rate on top of GP7a's guard at js/sim.js:5756. GP6's APPROVAL_TERMS `tax` row reads the scalar c.taxRate TWICE (js/sim.js:1645-1649, pen and blurb) and js/advisors.js:192-199 reads it in three branches — both must be given a defined value under per-zone rates. Any tax/assessment verdict row goes in ADVISORY_GATES (js/sim.js:1745) or INFRA_GATES, never GROWTH_GATES. LAUNCH CONDITION (preflight, non-negotiable): the gate problems recorded in preflight_gate_problems below were found by an adversarial reviewer that read the LIVE source and MEASURED the unchanged build. The design phase MUST resolve every one before implementation, and each resolution must be reported in the ship verdict with its measurement. Rules for resolving: an IMPOSSIBILITY (unachievable/self-contradictory/vacuous — the sim arithmetic or the fixture cannot produce the quantity) is corrected by re-specifying the gate so it measures the intended property with a reachable bar, and the correction is recorded with the measurement proving the original was impossible. An ABSOLUTE-SHOULD-BE-COMPARATIVE bar is restated per the R1 protocol (this build vs baseline on identical scripted inputs). An AMBIGUOUS-THRESHOLD gate is pinned to a named city, seed, sample count and reference quantity. An UNMEASURABLE gate is either given a concrete headless observable or reported to the user as needing a design decision. A resolution that changes what the milestone is TRYING TO ACHIEVE (rather than how it is measured) is a DESIGN decision — surface it to the user, never decide it (S6). Also close every missing_coverage item or justify its omission.
milestones.player_facing_win: Parks, clean air, schools and rail finally show up as rent — raising land value literally pays the bills — an established city can no longer coast on a permanent unattended surplus, and borrowing becomes a real instrument with a chooseable term, a ceiling tied to what your city is worth, and a reputation that remembers, instead of one fixed button.
quality_gates: RE-PIN DECLARED AND BOUNDED: publish new array hashes over the 20 corpus_seeds alongside docs/gp1-baseline.json, with the ONLY declared behavior changes enumerated (tax line, taxMod curve, landv railCov term, deptCosts served-load term, bond ladder, urban renewal). Terrain generation and every sprite bake stay byte-identical to HEAD — bar: terr[] hash and sprite-atlas hash equal on 20 of 20 seeds, 0 differing bytes. Zero console errors across all 20 runs.

LAND VALUE EARNS MONEY (S5 outcome, measured with GP7a's certified ledger): two pinned cities with pop and jobs each within 2% but mean landv differing by >=60 differ in REALIZED monthly take by >=35%, taken as the mean over rollovers 480-600. And the equilibrium-revenue curve on the pinned reference city is single-peaked with an INTERIOR peak (peak rate strictly inside 1..19, and revenue at the peak >= 1.05x revenue at both 0% and 20%), with equilibrium pop at 14% >= 20% below equilibrium pop at 3% — measured at tick 600, reported as the median across all 20 corpus_seeds with per-seed spread.

SEPARABILITY OR AN HONEST SINGLE RATE (S5 outcome, never an instantaneous demand delta): raise ONLY the industrial rate by 6 points, then measure at +120 rollovers against an identical control city run from the same seed. Bar: built iJobs census falls >=12% vs control while resTiles and pop each stay within 4% of control. If the measurement fails, the milestone ships ONE rate and publishes the numbers — this gate passes either way, but three sliders never ship unless the >=12% / <=4% bar is met.

NO FREE SURPLUS AND THE FLOOR BINDS: (a) an unattended established pinned city's cumulative funds delta over rollovers 360-600 stays within +/-10% of zero at the calibrated rate (measured on city.funds, not lastBudget.net alone, so bond and ordinance flows count) — bar: 20 of 20 seeds inside the band. (b) COMPARATIVE per R1: on an identical scripted blight/revenue-hole recovery using only the urban-renewal line and the bond ladder, this build returns to positive funds within 60 rollovers on >= as many corpus_seeds as the pinned GP6 baseline worktree, and on NO seed does this build fail where baseline succeeds. (c) The floor is observed to bind: monthly take > 0 on every rollover while >=1 developed tile remains — bar: 0 zero-revenue months across 20 seeds x 600 ticks.

CALIBRATION AND SCENARIO SAFETY (R1 COMPARATIVE; FOUR scenarios, not five): the pinned reference city at the legacy 7% rate collects within +/-10% of the GP6 baseline's mean monthly take over rollovers 480-600. Then for EACH of the four scenarios in js/scenarios.js:91-286 — gridlock-97 (:93), twister-season (:139, winTarget 4000 at :148/:158), blackout-summer-97 (:183) and y2k-ready (:233, needPop 2500 / needMargin 100 / needFunds 4000 at :241 and :256-260, a DIRECT revenue dependency) — run the same scripted solution on this build and on the pinned baseline served at :8902. Bar: this build wins on >= as many corpus_seeds as baseline for every scenario, and 0 scenario-seed pairs regress. Medals persist: a pre-seeded localStorage trophy store survives load and merges upgrade-only (recordTrophy js/scenarios.js:311-318, TROPHY_KEY js/scenarios.js:295) — bar: 0 medals lost or downgraded.

SAVE v19 / DETERMINISM: v19 written; v18, v17 and v12 saves all load with 0 console errors and no version-equality test anywhere in deserialize. A legacy scalar taxRate fans into every rate, and that loaded city's next 120 rollovers match a native city built from the same state exactly — bar: 0 differing values across pop/funds/jobs/demand.r/c/i. Round-trip serialize->deserialize->serialize byte-identical. Any new history series is added to BOTH js/sim.js:31 and js/sim.js:5274 — bar: all series equal-length after 300 rollovers. Same seed + script reproduces identical series over 600 ticks with Math.random UNSTUBBED. Existing serialized bonds keep amortizing from their own b.term/b.remaining/b.monthly — bar: a v17 save carrying a 12-month bond retires it in exactly its stored remaining months.

S4 SIM-ART COHERENCE FOR EVERY NEW SIM STATE: three new states each get a visible expression tested at cam.r 0/1/2/3, with failure visually distinct from working. (a) A tile at the assessed FLOOR renders in a band distinct from healthy bands by >=60 in two RGB channels. (b) A STARVED urban-renewal line is visually distinct from a funded one (distinct chip class and text in fillBudgetTable, plus a distinct map/inspector readout) — bar: a screenshot-diff of starved vs funded is non-empty at all 4 rotations. (c) A credit-rating DOWNGRADE reads distinctly in the bond panel and fires its ticker message exactly ONCE per downgrade — bar: 1 message per transition, 0 per-tick repeats over 600 ticks.

ANTI-CROSSTALK AND DRAW DISCIPLINE: (a) no new over[] id is introduced — bar: Object.keys(OV) set-equal to HEAD; if any id >= OV.ZR is added after all, it carries an explicit predicate at each of power conduction, power demand, brownout, y2k and fire candidacy, with five individually asserted sub-gates. (b) GROWTH_GATES is unchanged unless the re-pin explicitly declares the row — bar: GROWTH_GATES.length equal to HEAD; the tax/assessment verdict lives in ADVISORY_GATES (js/sim.js:1745) or INFRA_GATES. (c) demandBreakdown's parts-sum-reproduces-raw invariant holds BIT-FOR-BIT for all three bars — bar: 0 mismatches over 600 ticks x 20 seeds. (d) recomputeJobAccess's _jaComp/_jaNC caching is not regressed and deptCosts adds no per-tile pass — bar: mean per-tick wall time and budget-dialog slider-drag latency each within 110% of HEAD.
milestones.split_rationale: Everything genuinely behavioral concentrates here, and every piece of it is measured by a readout GP7a already proved honest — that is the whole point of the split. Two independent RNG re-pins live in this half (taxMod reshaping the demand comparisons, and railCov entering the landv fold that feeds gFit at js/sim.js:1079), which is precisely why the shadow ledger could not have ridden along: it would have lost its byte-identical gate and the cutover would have had no trusted ruler to be measured against. Two gates deliberately depart from the original spec's shape and this is reported, not amended: original quality_gates[3] and [4] set absolute 'in >=8 of 10 seeded runs' bars, exactly the shape R1 already ruled mis-specified once, so gates 4 and 5 above are restated COMPARATIVE (this build vs the pinned GP6 baseline on identical scripted solutions); and original gate [4] says 'all 5 scenarios' when js/scenarios.js:91-286 contains exactly FOUR, so the gate is restated over the four real ids. Both deviations are flagged for the user's decision per S6 rather than silently rewritten. This half is also by far the largest behavior surface in the plan and should be expected to need its own split at ITS launch.
milestones.save_version_plan: GP7a takes v18; GP7b takes v19.
