Both halves load every earlier version with defensive typeof/Array.isArray guards and NEVER a version-equality test. If the user prefers the read half not to touch the ladder at all, dropping history.assess (keeping the shadow ledger live-only in the budget dialog) lets GP7a ship at v17 unchanged, GP5a-style — but the month-over-month shadow-vs-actual series is the most legible part of the readout, so v18 is recommended.
milestones.launch_order_note:
Strict order: GP7a fully certified before GP7b begins. Three hard dependencies, not preferences. (1) GP7a's spike (docs/gp7-spike.json) is what DECIDES GP7b's rate structure and curve target; run after the cutover it measures a build that no longer exists. (2) GP7b's outcome gates are all stated in terms of realized take and assessed value — the numbers assessedLedger() reports. Those numbers are only admissible as evidence because GP7a's byte-identical gate proved the ledger agrees with the bill (0 mismatches over 20 seeds x 600 ticks) while changing nothing. (3) GP7a routes collectBudget, advTaxesAt and the advisor taxMod copy through single definitions and adds the missing taxRate load guard — doing the cutover first would, per the drift report, silently delete the certified GP5b cleanTax revenue line and its js/ui.js:1131 budget row, and would put per-zone rates on top of an unguarded load that NaN-poisons demand citywide.

S6 REPORTS FOR THE USER, NOT AMENDMENTS. Three items in the original spec are wrong in ways a worker must not quietly fix: (a) quality_gates[3] and [4] set absolute "in >=8 of 10 seeded runs" bars — the exact shape R1 already ruled mis-specified once, when the reference script never won two scenarios on EITHER build. GP7b's gates 4 and 5 above are restated COMPARATIVE against the pinned GP6 baseline worktree on identical scripted solutions; the user should confirm that restatement or supply different bars. (b) quality_gates[4] says "all 5 scenarios" — js/scenarios.js:91-286 contains exactly FOUR (gridlock-97, twister-season, blackout-summer-97, y2k-ready), so the gate was uncountable as written; restated over the four real ids. (c) The scope's stated accumulation home (deptCosts) and several of its line numbers are wrong by 2,600-3,000 lines against a 6,011-line js/sim.js; the split above is grounded in today's source and supersedes them.

S8 / S2 FLAG: GP7b as scoped is the largest behavior surface remaining in the plan — cutover, rate structure, curve reshape, assessed floor, urban-renewal line, debt ladder with rating memory, served-load upkeep, and railCov in the landv fold, carrying TWO independent declared re-pins. Recommend planning for a further split at GP7b's own launch (a natural seam is: cutover + assessed floor + no-free-surplus first, then debt ladder + urban renewal + transit-in-rent), and note that if GP7b is refuted twice the S2 two-strike rule forbids a third whole attempt. GP6 is live-but-uncertified at HEAD b3d780c (last SHIP a702c92, GP5b): GP7b touches GP6 surface — the APPROVAL_TERMS `tax` row at js/sim.js:1645-1649 reads the scalar c.taxRate twice — so treat GP6 as landing, not certified, and do not depend on its unshipped details.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[1] (LAND VALUE EARNS MONEY) / [3](a) / [4] — every 'rollovers 480-600' and 'rollovers 360-600' window
preflight_gate_problems.problem: MEASURED: the pinned protocol's 600 ticks produce exactly 25 month rollovers (history.pop.length === 25 after the pinned build_script + 600 ticks; the rollover block is a %24 gate). 'Rollovers 480-600' and 'rollovers 360-600' therefore do not exist in the pinned run — reaching rollover 600 needs 14,400 ticks, 24x the pinned protocol. Gate 2 is internally inconsistent on its own: it says 'measured at tick 600' AND 'taken as the mean over rollovers 480-600' in the same sentence. This is the incident-2 shape exactly: the fixture cannot produce the quantity the gate measures.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Pick ONE unit and state the tick count explicitly. Either (a) keep the pinned 600-tick protocol and measure over 'rollovers 19-25 (ticks 456-600)', or (b) declare an extended protocol ('the pinned build_script run to 14,400 ticks = 600 rollovers') and say so in every window, noting the cost (~10 s/seed at the measured 0.4 s/600 ticks, so it is affordable — but it must be declared, not assumed).

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[1] — 'two pinned cities with pop and jobs each within 2% but mean landv differing by >=60'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: MEASURED range of citywide MEAN landv on 80x80 builds: 43.1 (ordinary zoned city, pop 3648), 43.5 (saturated industry), 84.5 (a city with ~2/3 of the map paved in parks — pop only 1696). landv is 40 + diffused amenity - poll*0.7 - traffic*0.4 (js/sim.js:3730-3741), so the citywide mean has a hard floor near 40 for any non-polluted city and only reaches the mid-80s by spending the map on parks — which destroys the pop/jobs match the same gate requires. A >=60 gap in citywide mean landv with pop AND jobs matched within 2% is not demonstrably constructible.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the bar over DEVELOPED-tile mean landv (measured span 10 to 73, so >=40 is comfortably constructible) or lower the citywide bar to >=25, and let the pair be matched on pop and jobs by construction (zone-count tuning) rather than by search.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[1] — 'equilibrium pop at 14% >= 20% below equilibrium pop at 3%'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: MEASURED on the UNCHANGED build, pop drop from 3% to 14% per seed: seed 1 22.6%, seed 2 22.8%, seed 4 0.8%, seed 5 19.6%, seed 8 2.5% — median ~19.6%, i.e. HEAD FAILS this absolute bar today by a hair, and two of five seeds show no effect at all. The reason is structural: the response is a CLIFF, not a curve. demand.r sits pinned at clampD's ceiling (raw jobsAvail/220 = 2.51 against a clamp of 1.0) for every rate from 0 to 13, so taxMod (max |0.65|) cannot move residential demand at all until the rate crosses the collapse point (seed 1: pop 4608 at 10%, 3560 at 14%, 424 at 17%, 0 at 20%). The bar therefore measures WHERE THE CLIFF LANDS on a given seed, not the quality of the curve work — the same failure mode as the '>=8 of 10 seeded playthroughs' incident.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Make it comparative and shape-based: 'the pop-vs-rate curve on this build shows a strictly larger rate elasticity of equilibrium pop over the 3%..14% interval than the pinned GP6 baseline on the same 20 corpus seeds, on >= as many seeds as baseline and regressing on none' — plus publish the per-seed cliff rate so the user can set an absolute bar afterwards from real numbers.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[1] — 'single-peaked with an INTERIOR peak (peak rate strictly inside 1..19, revenue at the peak >= 1.05x revenue at both 0% and 20%)'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: MEASURED on the UNCHANGED build, seed 1, realized monthly take by rate: 0%->0, 3%->5,685, 7%->13,211, 10%->18,904, 14%->20,386, 17%->3,089, 20%->115. HEAD already has an interior peak near 14 and already clears 1.05x at both endpoints — the clause passes on a build that does none of the work. The 0% comparison is vacuous by construction in particular: the take is proportional to the rate, so revenue at 0% is 0 (or the new floor), and 'peak >= 1.05x of 0' is trivially true. 'Single-peaked' also has no tolerance band: a 21-point empirical median curve that dips by one dollar anywhere violates strict single-peakedness.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Drop the 0% endpoint. State it as: 'peak rate strictly inside 3..17; revenue at the peak >= 1.15x revenue at 20%; and the median curve is unimodal within a stated tolerance (no local dip greater than 2% of the peak)'. Add the comparative clause that makes it about the work: the peak must be at a strictly lower rate, or the post-peak decline strictly gentler, than the same curve measured on the unchanged build in docs/gp7-spike.json.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[2] — SEPARABILITY ('raise ONLY the industrial rate by 6 points ... built iJobs falls >=12% vs control while resTiles and pop each stay within 4%')
preflight_gate_problems.problem: MEASURED response of built iJobs to a demand.i shift of the size a +6 industrial-rate move produces (taxMod*0.4 = -0.12): global rate 7 -> 2,016 iJobs; rate 11 -> 2,008 (-0.4%); rate 12 -> 1,960 (-2.8%); rate 13 -> 1,600 but with pop simultaneously -20% (4,584 -> 3,680) because the whole city has gone over the cliff. Below the cliff the industrial response is ~3%, far short of 12%; at and above the cliff nothing is separable at all (pop moves as much as iJobs). Under the current curve no industrial-only rate move produces >=12% iJobs decline with pop within 4%. Because the gate is also written to 'pass either way', the practical effect is that the milestone's headline feature (per-zone rates) can never ship, and the gate cannot fail to reveal that — the decision is buried inside a gate that always passes.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Separate the decision from the gate. Gate: 'publish the separability measurement (iJobs / resTiles / pop vs an identical control at +120 rollovers, 20 seeds) in docs/gp7-spike.json — bar: numbers present.' Decision rule stated outside the gate: 'three sliders ship only if iJobs falls >= X% with pop and resTiles within Y%.' Set X from the measurement (the current physics supports roughly 3% at +6 points, so either X must drop or the rate delta must be much larger), and run it AFTER the taxMod reshape, since the reshape is the only thing that can move this number.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[3](a) — 'cumulative funds delta over rollovers 360-600 stays within +/-10% of zero'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: '+/-10% of zero' is zero — the denominator is undefined, so the bar is either literally unachievable (exact zero drift over 240 months) or unstated. There is no reference quantity named: 10% of the mean monthly take? of funds at the window start? of cumulative revenue over the window? MEASURED for scale: the pinned reference city at 7% ends 600 ticks with funds 440,865 from a 200,000 start and lastBudget.net +11,825/month, so the quantity being bounded is large and the choice of denominator changes the bar by orders of magnitude. (Compounded by the rollovers-vs-ticks problem above.)
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: '|funds(end) - funds(start)| <= 0.10 x (sum of realized monthly take over the same window)', with start/end stated in TICKS (e.g. ticks 360..600 of the pinned protocol), measured on city.funds, 20 of 20 seeds inside the band.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[3](c) — 'The floor is observed to bind: monthly take > 0 on every rollover while >=1 developed tile remains — bar: 0 zero-revenue months across 20 seeds x 600 ticks'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The pinned corpus never goes near zero revenue — MEASURED take on the reference city at 7% is 13,211/month with 964 developed tiles, and the sub-gate's title claims the floor is 'observed to bind' while the measurement can only observe that a healthy city has positive revenue. Every build, floor or no floor, passes. The only measured configuration where take approaches zero is rate 0 (take exactly 0) or the post-collapse city at rate 20 (pop 0, 4 developed tiles, take 115) — neither is in the gate's fixture.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Add an adversarial fixture that actually reaches the floor: 'bulldoze/blight the pinned city down to N developed tiles (and separately set taxRate 0) and assert monthly take > 0 on every rollover while >=1 developed tile remains, and assert take === 0 the rollover after the last developed tile is removed' — so the floor's boundary is what is observed, not a healthy city's solvency.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[4] — CALIBRATION AND SCENARIO SAFETY ('this build wins on >= as many corpus_seeds as baseline for every scenario')
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Scenario cities are NOT seeded by the corpus: each SCENARIOS entry pins its own seed in source (gridlock-97 971104, twister-season 51996, blackout-summer-97 970601, y2k-ready 990704; js/scenarios.js:67 'new City(o.seed, 80)'). There is no corpus_seed axis to count wins over, so 'wins on >= as many corpus_seeds' is uncountable as written. The established harness varies k = 0..9 (the scripted reference solution at scratchpad/gp1b-scenario-ref.mjs jitters placements and slider timing by k), which is the axis the earlier '>= 8 of 10 seeded playthroughs' bar referred to. The gate's calibration clause also consumes 'the GP6 baseline's mean monthly take over rollovers 480-600', a number nothing in GP7a produces (GP7a's spike publishes tick-600 point values).
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'For each of the four scenarios, run the pinned scripted solution at k = 0..9 on this build and on the pinned GP6 baseline worktree (:8902). Bar: this build wins on >= as many of the 10 playthroughs as baseline for every scenario, and 0 scenario-k pairs regress.' And have GP7a's spike publish the 7% take as a mean over the same window GP7b calibrates against, so the calibration reference exists on the unchanged build.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[6](b) — 'a screenshot-diff of starved vs funded is non-empty at all 4 rotations'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: A non-empty screenshot diff is not evidence of anything in this renderer: the scene carries animated, time- and RNG-dependent content (trains, smoke plumes at js/render.js:1568 gated on Math.random, choppers, ticker text), so two captures of the SAME state also diff non-emptily. The bar passes for a build in which starved and funded urban renewal render identically.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Make it a controlled comparison: 'capture starved vs funded from the same tick with animation frozen (or diff only the deterministic budget-dialog chip region and the inspector text): bar - the chip class and label strings differ, and the map/inspector readout for a starved tile differs from a funded one by >=60 in two RGB channels at cam.r 0/1/2/3, while a same-state capture pair diffs by 0 pixels in the same region.'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP7b quality_gates[7](d) — 'mean per-tick wall time and budget-dialog slider-drag latency each within 110% of HEAD'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: No repetition count, no warm-up, no variance discipline, and no statement of which machine or which city — headless wall-time in this container swings well over 10% run to run, so the gate can fail (or pass) on noise while the code is unchanged. GP7a's gate 2(c) already demonstrates the deterministic alternative (an instrumented count of full-length over[] iterations).
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Gate on deterministic operation counts plus a loose timing sanity band: 'instrumented count of full-length over[] passes per tick, and per drag of a funding slider, equals HEAD exactly (deptCosts adds no per-tile pass); AND median per-tick wall time over 5 runs x 600 ticks after one warm-up run is within 125% of HEAD measured in the same session.'

preflight_missing_coverage: taxTake() as scoped has NO rate parameter, but advTaxesAt(rate) is called with the OLD rate at js/advisors.js:403 (advTaxesAt(O) vs advTaxesAt(N)) to compute the projected revenue loss. GP7a gate 2(b) only tests advTaxesAt(city.taxRate), so a delegation that ignores the argument passes every gate while making `loss` identically 0 and printing 'a projected §0 a month gone' in the Transportation advisor's protest. Needs a gate: advTaxesAt(r) for r in 0..20 on >=10 states equals a city-independent recomputation at rate r (including cleanTax scaling with r), not just at the live rate.

GP7b cutover has no gate retiring GP7a's PREVIEW framing: the budget block is shipped in GP7a labelled 'Assessed valuation (not charged)' (js/ui.js:1103-1150). After the cutover that label is a lie on screen and the GP5b 'incl. High-tech premium' row's relationship to the new bill is unstated. Needs an S4 gate on the post-cutover budget dialog text and on the preserved js/ui.js:1131-1132 row.

GP7b(6) TRANSIT IN RENT is the milestone's headline player-facing promise ('rail finally shows up as rent') and is a declared RNG re-pin (landv -> gFit at js/sim.js:1079), yet no gate measures it: nothing isolates railCov's contribution to landv, nothing shows it in the wealth-band map or inspector at 4 rotations, and no outcome gate compares realized take for a rail-served vs identical rail-less pinned city.

GP7b(5) 're-tie upkeep to SERVED LOAD by CONSUMING deptStrain/approvalCensus, never a second definition of load' is unmeasured. Gates cover perf and the surplus band but nothing asserts the bill and the strain meters agree — e.g. deptCosts' load inputs are bit-identical to the popLoad/jobLoad/structures and roadTiles/jam/jamShare the meters display, on the same tick, across 20 seeds.

Per-zone rates have no gate on the GP6 surfaces that read the SCALAR c.taxRate: APPROVAL_TERMS 'tax' row (js/sim.js:1645-1649, both the pen() penalty and the blurb) and js/advisors.js:192-199's three branches. Approval is an EMA carry that IS serialized, so an undefined/NaN taxRate there poisons persisted state permanently. Needs: approval finite and the survey/advisor strings free of 'undefined'/'NaN' under per-zone rates, across 120 rollovers and a save round-trip.

Nothing certifies the READOUT against the ledger. GP7a gate 2 proves assessedLedger() agrees with the bill, and gate 4 proves the minimap bands render, but no gate ties the numbers rendered in fillBudgetTable's preview (per-sector projected take R/C/I and the delta) to assessedLedger()'s {assessed.r/c/i, headcount} fields — the UI could print a differently-derived number and pass every gate.

GP7b gate 6(c) (credit-rating downgrade fires exactly once) has no fixture guaranteeing a downgrade occurs: on the pinned corpus the reference city runs a permanent surplus (measured funds 200,000 -> 440,865 over 600 ticks at 7%), so a 600-tick run may never downgrade and the '1 message per transition' bar is vacuous. Needs a scripted forced-downgrade (and forced-upgrade) fixture.

No gate covers the interaction between the new assessed FLOOR and the equilibrium-revenue curve at rate 0: with a floor, take is no longer 0 at 0% tax, which changes what 'revenue at 0%' means in gate 2 and creates an unattended-income path the no-free-surplus gate measures only at the calibrated rate. Either gate revenue at rate 0 explicitly, or state that the floor is rate-scaled.
milestones.split_of: GP7 (preflight-authored S3 split, grounded against the live source 2026-07-30)

milestones.title: Civil Defense: the honest risk ruler (read-first, save-neutral, byte-identical)
milestones.scope:
READ HALF. Ships every readout GP8b will be measured by, and provably cannot move the sim.

1. HAZARD_TERMS declarative table + city.hazardReport() — PURE, zero RNG, zero writes, no cam.r. Model it exactly on the certified APPROVAL_TERMS/approvalReport pair (table at js/sim.js:1663-1725, report at js/sim.js:5114-5144): one frozen ordered table of rows {id,label,drivers:[{id,label,val,blurb}],mode,focus}, one census scan, rows sorted by score desc / id asc. SEVEN rows = the SEVEN BUILT KINDS (fire, tornado, ufo, quake, flood, riot, monster). Inputs are all already-maintained state — fireCov/polCov (js/sim.js:1842-1843), crime (1841), poll (1839), plantYear (1975) vs PLANT_WARN_AGE=40 (js/sim.js:508) on OV.NUKE anchors, the TERR.WATER coast-front scan idiom (js/sim.js:4640-4648), seasonOf(this.month) (js/sim.js:684-691), the unemployment term pop*0.62 vs jobs (js/sim.js:4184), and City.deptStrain() (js/sim.js:4962-4996) for the funding-scaled powered-anchor allowance. NEVER re-census what deptStrain already returns.

2. CALIBRATION, the S3 crux. On this half the published per-year odds MUST reproduce the SHIPPED spawn model, not a hypothetical one: aggregate = 1-(1-0.0009)^288 = 0.2284213823 from the per-tick gate at js/sim.js:5477, split by the kind ladder at js/sim.js:5481-5487 (fire .55, tornado .13, ufo .10, quake .08, flood .07, riot .055, monster .015). The vector's per-row scores are NORMALISED so that a documented reference city sits exactly on those shipped odds; the row scores are what GP8b will re-pin the roll against. This is the whole point of the split: the ruler is validated against measurable HEAD behaviour before anything consumes it.

3. #dlg-civdef panel (new dialog block in index.html beside #dlg-survey at index.html:383; open from MENUS.windows in js/ui.js:380+ and from the disasters menu). Per row: a Low/Elevated/High/Severe band chip, the single largest driver named in plain English, the live per-year odds figure, and a "Show me" button reusing the exact survey machinery (setMapMode + cam jump + streetNameFor, js/ui.js:2018-2028) — that path is already the ONE code path for mode switching (js/ui.js:815+).

4. Phase-1 defect #1, the byte-neutral half: extend MENUS.disasters (js/ui.js:372-379) from 3 kinds to all 7 (quake/flood/riot/monster rows). Draw-neutral by construction — a menu closure only fires on click. NOTE these four already spawn today from the random ladder (js/sim.js:5484-5487); this fixes MENU reachability only, not spawn rate. Sound: only Snd.siren/boom/ufo exist (js/audio.js:60-67); add distinct synth voices for quake/flood/riot/monster in the same house style.

5. Disaster Bugle front page — one {headline,sub,body} newsQueue push per kind, inserted in each startDisaster branch beside the existing pushMsg (js/sim.js:4606, 4618, 4633, 4658, 4672, 4685), INCLUDING before the fire branch's early return at js/sim.js:4607. Byte-neutral and provable: newsQueue is initialised at js/sim.js:2031, is absent from serialize(), and is reset to [] on load at js/sim.js:5948 — so no save byte moves. Rendered by the existing showEventPaper/newsFrame (js/ui.js:2084-2103), no new dialog.

6. S4 visibility: a 14th minimap mode "Risk" — extend MM_LEGENDS (js/ui.js:741-769), MM_NAMES (js/ui.js:773-776) and updateMapLegend (js/ui.js:778-814) TOGETHER (the GP6 stale-caption fix comment at js/ui.js:782-786 documents what happens otherwise), plus its renderMinimap branch. Four band swatches, visually distinct.

7. One ADVISORY_GATES row (js/sim.js:1745-1774, e.g. FIRE_RISK_HIGH) — the certified draw-neutral table, walked ONLY by _attachAdvisories (js/sim.js:4512-4522). Do NOT add a GROWTH_GATES row. Plus the advisors' first disaster lines in js/advisors.js (which today mentions only fire COVERAGE at lines 157, 260-267).

8. Optional auto-pause + camera jump on disaster start, behind a UI.prefs flag (savePrefs idiom), presentation only.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (GP8b owns): any change to the roll at js/sim.js:5477, scenario pressure (js/scenarios.js:367), dispatch, any save key, any history series, any new OV id. GP8a stays at save v17 with a character-identical payload. LAUNCH CONDITION (preflight, non-negotiable): the gate problems recorded in preflight_gate_problems below were found by an adversarial reviewer that read the LIVE source and MEASURED the unchanged build. The design phase MUST resolve every one before implementation, and each resolution must be reported in the ship verdict with its measurement. Rules for resolving: an IMPOSSIBILITY (unachievable/self-contradictory/vacuous — the sim arithmetic or the fixture cannot produce the quantity) is corrected by re-specifying the gate so it measures the intended property with a reachable bar, and the correction is recorded with the measurement proving the original was impossible. An ABSOLUTE-SHOULD-BE-COMPARATIVE bar is restated per the R1 protocol (this build vs baseline on identical scripted inputs). An AMBIGUOUS-THRESHOLD gate is pinned to a named city, seed, sample count and reference quantity. An UNMEASURABLE gate is either given a concrete headless observable or reported to the user as needing a design decision. A resolution that changes what the milestone is TRYING TO ACHIEVE (rather than how it is measured) is a DESIGN decision — surface it to the user, never decide it (S6). Also close every missing_coverage item or justify its omission.
milestones.player_facing_win: Before anything burns, the player can open Civil Defense and read what the city is actually exposed to — seven hazards, each with a band, a per-year odds figure and one plain-English sentence naming the thing most responsible — and every one of the seven disasters is finally reachable from the menu and gets its own Bugle front page when it lands.
quality_gates: BYTE-IDENTICAL SIM: against a git-worktree pin of the pre-GP8a commit served on :8902, 20 seeds x 600 ticks under the pinned build script with Math.random UNSTUBBED, serialize() at ticks 200/400/600 differs by 0 bytes in BOTH disastersEnabled states (40 runs, 120 checkpoints, 0 differing bytes), and rng.growth.s/rng.fire.s/rng.hazard.s/rng.build.s are equal at every checkpoint. The payload still declares v:17 and its key sequence is character-identical.

ZERO-DRAW READOUT: 1000 consecutive city.hazardReport() calls + 1000 openCivDef() opens + 1000 Risk-minimap repaints leave all four cursor ints unchanged (delta === 0 each) and serialize() byte-identical; building MENUS.disasters() 1000x leaves recCur.disasters unchanged (delta === 0) and spends 0 hazard draws.

MENU REACHABILITY + ONE BUGLE PER KIND: MENUS.disasters() returns exactly 7 kind rows plus the Random Disasters toggle (length === 8 counting the separator per the live shape); invoking each row on a coastal 80x80 test city starts that kind — recCur.disasters +1 for the 6 stateful kinds and >=1 burning fire[] tile for 'fire' (7/7) — and each launch pushes EXACTLY ONE newsQueue entry (20 launches per kind => exactly 20 entries per kind, 7 distinct headline strings, 0 duplicates).

HONEST ODDS AT THE CALIBRATION POINT: over 10 seeded 50-year headless soaks (14,400 ticks each, Math.random UNSTUBBED) the measured aggregate annual disaster rate is within ±20% RELATIVE of the odds the panel publishes for those same cities, the measured per-kind shares are each within ±20% relative of the panel's per-kind odds, and the analytic reference 1-(1-0.0009)^288 = 0.22842 lies inside the measured 95% interval.

NAMED CONTRIBUTOR IS THE ARGMAX: across 200 scripted city states spanning the driver ranges (fire coverage 0..255, police funding 0..100, pollution low/high, crime low/high, nuke age 0..60y, coastal and landlocked), the driver string the panel names equals the argmax of that row's own driver list in 200/200 cases, with ties broken by the documented id order.

BAND RESPONSE WITHIN ONE ROLLOVER: 4 scripted interventions — bulldoze every fire station; set funding.police 100->0; advance a nuke past PLANT_WARN_AGE (40y); zone a 20-tile coastal strip — each move their own row's band by >=1 band within <=24 ticks (4/4), and no unrelated row changes band in the same window (0 spurious band changes).

S4 ROTATION + FAILURE-STATE DISTINCTNESS: the Risk minimap mode produces an identical per-tile band buffer at cam.r 0/1/2/3 (0 differing tiles after the documented rotation mapping); MM_NAMES has exactly 14 entries and updateMapLegend returns a non-empty name+swatch string for 'risk' with no stale caption from the previously selected mode; the four band colours are 4 distinct hex values and a Severe row is distinguishable from a Low row from the swatch alone (no text needed), verified on screenshots at all 4 rotations.
ZERO CONSOLE ERRORS: boot, 600-tick soak, save/load round-trip, all 7 menu launches, panel opened at every band, and all 14 minimap modes cycled produce 0 console/page errors (favicon 404 excluded).
milestones.split_rationale: The read half is not vacuous: today there is no #dlg-civdef anywhere in index.html, no risk anything in js/ or css/, no disaster Bugle page (every startDisaster branch ends in pushMsg only — js/sim.js:4606/4618/4633/4658/4672/4685), no disaster advisor lines, and 4 of 7 kinds are missing from MENUS.disasters (js/ui.js:372-379). Every item above is instrumentation or presentation whose byte-neutrality is structurally provable rather than merely hoped for: hazardReport is pure, ADVISORY_GATES is walked only by diagnoseTile, newsQueue is never serialized (init js/sim.js:2031, reset on load js/sim.js:5948), and menu closures only fire on click. The drift report's sharpest warning was that GP8a as originally spec'd was NOT read-only because Phase 1 came first; this split resolves that by keeping the byte-neutral half of Phase 1 (menu registration) here and moving the behaviour-touching half (scenario pressure + difficulty axis) to GP8b, where its own gate is a behavioural measurement anyway. Calibrating the published odds to the SHIPPED 22.84%/yr model rather than to the future coupled model is what makes the honesty gate measurable on this half at all — the ruler is proved against today's sim, then GP8b re-pins the sim to the ruler. TWO MIS-SPECIFICATIONS ARE REPORTED, NOT SILENTLY REINTERPRETED (S6): (a) the spec's 7-row vector names MELTDOWN, which exists nowhere in the tree (the only 'meltdown' string is a transit joke at js/advisors.js:97) and omits TORNADO, which is built, menu-listed and the sole scenario pressure type; shipping MELTDOWN is an unpriced 8th kind (new sim branch + rotation-aware art + sound + Bugle page) beyond the 4->5 re-rate. Default assumed pending the user's decision: the vector's seven rows are the seven BUILT kinds and the plantYear/OV.NUKE age driver becomes a named contributor to the FIRE row. (b) The milestone's 'all 5 scenarios remain winnable' is unrunnable — js/scenarios.js:91-296 contains exactly four entries (gridlock-97, twister-season, blackout-summer-97, y2k-ready); GP7 and GP9 repeat the same error.
milestones.save_version_plan:
GP8a takes NO version bump and adds NO save key and NO history series. It stays at v17 (js/sim.js:5652) with a character-identical payload — that is what makes its byte-identical gate a real proof rather than a diff-tolerance. Nothing it ships is persistent state: hazardReport is derived-on-demand, newsQueue is never serialized (init js/sim.js:2031, reset to [] on load at js/sim.js:5948), the ADVISORY_GATES row is a pure read, and MENUS/minimap/dialog work is UI-only.

GP8b OWNS SAVE v18 — the next ladder integer after GP6's v17. Exactly one new key: `dispatch`, the emergency-unit roster, a plain JSON array of {kind,x,y,ticks,cost} objects appended AFTER recallDone (js/sim.js:5744-5745) so the entire v17 key sequence remains a character-stable prefix. Loaded with `Array.isArray(d.dispatch) ? ... : []`, no version-equality test anywhere in deserialize (js/sim.js:5749-5990); v17/v16/v14/v12 saves all load with an empty roster.

DO NOT re-add fire[] — GP1b already serializes it as a packU8 base64 plane at js/sim.js:5734 and restores it via unpackU8 at js/sim.js:5917 (the fix comment is at js/sim.js:5717-5719), and the mid-fire round-trip passes on HEAD today. The milestone spec's claim that "fire[] is not in serialize() at all" is stale by two ladder rungs; re-adding it would duplicate the key and break the character-stable-prefix rule. this.disaster is likewise already conditionally serialized (js/sim.js:5701) and restored (js/sim.js:5967) — the roster rides beside it, not inside it, precisely because startDisaster('fire') returns at js/sim.js:4607 without ever setting this.disaster, which is the 55%-likeliest kind.

hazVec is DERIVED and deliberately NOT serialized — recomputed at load from restored state, the GP6 megaOk precedent. If GP8b ships a monthly risk or disaster-rate history series, BOTH hardcoded key lists must be extended in the same commit: normaliseHistory (js/sim.js:31) and its mirror in the >240 trim loop at js/sim.js:5274 — the warning comments sit at js/sim.js:23-27 and js/sim.js:5270-5272.
milestones.launch_order_note:
Launch GP8a first, alone, and certify it before GP8b starts — the whole value of the split is that GP8b's coupling and calibration gates are measured by a ruler already proven honest against the shipped 22.84%/yr model.

SPLIT-BOUNDARY DECISION (the drift report flagged this as unwinnable-by-construction if left ambiguous): the milestone's Phase 1 is DIVIDED across the two halves. Menu registration of the four orphaned kinds (js/ui.js:372-379) goes in GP8a because a menu closure only fires on click and is therefore draw-neutral. Scenario-pressure generalization (js/scenarios.js:367-374) goes in GP8b because its own gate — ">=2 difficulty settings whose measured event frequency differs by >=2x" — is a behavioural measurement and cannot live under a byte-identical sim gate. GP8a's byte-identity gate must be run in BOTH disastersEnabled states, because the flag-off zero-draw property is already green on HEAD by GP1b's short-circuit design (js/sim.js:5477) and the real risk is regressing it, not achieving it.

Both halves are independently shippable per S8: GP8a alone delivers the Civil Defense panel, all seven kinds reachable from the menu, seven Bugle front pages, the Risk minimap mode and the first disaster advisor lines, with zero sim risk and no save bump. If the session caps after GP8a, the game is coherent and certified.

TWO ITEMS NEED A USER DECISION BEFORE GP8b IS BRIEFED (S6 — reported, not silently reinterpreted): (1) MELTDOWN appears in the spec's seven-row vector but exists nowhere in the tree (the only 'meltdown' string is a transit joke at js/advisors.js:97) while TORNADO — built, menu-listed and the sole scenario pressure type — is absent from it; shipping MELTDOWN is an unpriced 8th disaster kind requiring a new sim branch, rotation-aware art, a sound voice and a Bugle page, well beyond the 4->5 re-rate. The split assumes, pending the user's call, that the vector's seven rows are the seven BUILT kinds and that the plantYear/OV.NUKE age driver becomes a named contributor to the FIRE row. (2) The gate phrase "all 5 scenarios remain winnable" is unrunnable — js/scenarios.js:91-296 holds exactly four scenarios, and GP7 and GP9 repeat the same wording, so it is a systematic docs error worth fixing across all three entries.

One more baseline correction to carry into the brief: quake/flood/riot/monster are NOT absent from play today — they already spawn from the random ladder at js/sim.js:5484-5487. Any baseline capture for GP8b's coupling gate must therefore be taken against the current seven-kind ladder, never against a fire/tornado/ufo-only assumption.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8a — HONEST ODDS AT THE CALIBRATION POINT vs GP8a — BAND RESPONSE WITHIN ONE ROLLOVER
preflight_gate_problems.problem: These two gates cannot both pass, and the contradiction is forced by GP8a's own BYTE-IDENTICAL SIM gate. Because GP8a provably does not move the sim, the true hazard rate on EVERY city is the constant 1-(1-0.0009)^288 = 22.84%/yr and the true per-kind split is the fixed ladder at js/sim.js:5481-5487, independent of fire coverage, police funding, plant age or coastline. Scope item 3 puts the band chip AND the live per-year odds figure on the same row, derived from the same row score. So either (a) the published odds are constant across cities — the honesty gate passes but it is a single-point identity, the band chip can never move, and BAND RESPONSE fails 0/4; or (b) the odds vary with city state so the bands move — BAND RESPONSE passes, and the honesty gate then fails on every soak city that is not the calibration reference, because four bands spanning Low/Elevated/High/Severe imply an odds spread far wider than ±20% relative. The scope text half-concedes this ('normalised so that a documented REFERENCE CITY sits exactly on those shipped odds') but the gate measures '10 seeded 50-year soaks', not the reference city. This is the same shape as the y=12/y=9/y=15 incident: the fixture cannot produce the measured quantity.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Split the claim in two. (i) CALIBRATION-POINT IDENTITY (GP8a): on the ONE documented reference city, hazardReport().pTick equals 0.0009 to 1e-9 and the seven row weights equal the shipped ladder to 1e-9 — an exact analytic assertion, no soak needed. (ii) MONOTONIC RESPONSE (GP8a): the four scripted interventions each move their own row's SCORE strictly in the documented direction and cross at least one band boundary. Move the empirical ±20% honesty measurement entirely to GP8b, where the sim actually follows the ruler. Additionally: on GP8a the panel must not print a per-year odds figure that varies by city while the sim's rate does not — either print the odds only on the reference calibration, or label the varying number as 'exposure', which is what it actually is on this half.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8a — HONEST ODDS: 'the measured per-kind shares are each within ±20% relative of the panel's per-kind odds'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Statistically unachievable by construction at the specified sample size. 10 soaks x 50 years = 500 city-years; at 22.84%/yr that is ~114 total events. Monster is 1.5% of the ladder => expected 1.7 events across the WHOLE experiment; riot 5.5% => ~6.3; flood 7% => ~8. A Poisson count with mean 1.7 has ~77% relative standard deviation. To hold the monster share inside ±20% relative at 95% confidence you need ~96 monster events, i.e. ~6,400 total events, i.e. ~28,000 city-years — 56x the specified budget. The gate will fail on a perfectly correct implementation on most seed sets, and passing it once would be luck. Only the fire row (~63 events, ~13% rel. sd) is even marginally powered.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Either (a) assert the per-kind split ANALYTICALLY rather than empirically — hazardReport()'s seven normalised weights equal the shipped ladder constants (.55/.13/.10/.08/.07/.055/.015) to 1e-9 — which is exact, free, and actually proves the thing; or (b) keep the empirical form only for the AGGREGATE rate and for kinds whose expected count over the horizon is >= 30, and explicitly exclude kinds below that floor from scoring, reporting their observed counts instead. The same fix is needed on GP8b's 'CALIBRATION BAND + THE RULER STAYS HONEST', which re-runs the identical per-kind ±20% test at the identical 500-city-year budget.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8a — MENU REACHABILITY: 'MENUS.disasters() returns exactly 7 kind rows plus the Random Disasters toggle (length === 8 counting the separator per the live shape)'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Off-by-one against the live shape the gate claims to be counting. js/ui.js:372-379 today is [fire],[tornado],[UFO],"-",[toggle] = 5 elements: 3 kinds + 1 separator + 1 toggle. Going 3->7 kinds gives 7 + 1 separator + 1 toggle = 9, not 8. An implementer who ships the correct menu fails the assertion and will be tempted either to drop the separator (a real UI regression, losing the divider between the destructive rows and the toggle) or to quietly amend the bar — exactly the S6 failure this role exists to prevent.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'MENUS.disasters() returns 9 elements: 7 kind rows, one "-" separator, and the Random Disasters toggle — asserted as (rows.filter(r => Array.isArray(r)).length === 8 && rows.filter(r => r === "-").length === 1), so the count is robust to future separator placement.'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8a — HONEST ODDS: '...within ±20% RELATIVE of the odds the panel publishes for those same cities'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The soak cities are never specified, and the sim makes the choice load-bearing in two ways the gate does not survive. (1) COASTLINE: startDisaster('flood') aborts at js/sim.js:4645 ('if (!front.length) return') without counting on a landlocked map, so the measured flood share is exactly 0 there while the shipped ladder publishes 7% — a relative error of 100%, and the aggregate rate also falls ~7% below the 22.84% analytic. On a coastal map neither is true. (2) POPULATION: the roll is gated on 'pop > 200' (js/sim.js:5477), so any soak that starts from a small town spends its opening years at a rate of 0, dragging the 50-year mean below the analytic reference. Neither 'coastal or landlocked' nor 'pop trajectory' nor 'is the panel expected to publish flood=0 on a waterless map' is pinned, and the answers change whether the gate passes.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Pin the fixture in the gate text: 'over 10 seeded 50-year soaks on the SAME documented coastal 80x80 city script (city = new City(seed,80), funds 1e9, tier 4, pop held above 200 from tick 0 — asserted), ...'. And state the required panel behaviour explicitly: 'on a landlocked city the panel must publish flood odds of exactly 0 and renormalise the remaining six rows to the aggregate — asserted directly, not measured by soak.'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8a — S4 ROTATION + FAILURE-STATE DISTINCTNESS: 'the Risk minimap mode produces an identical per-tile band buffer at cam.r 0/1/2/3 (0 differing tiles after the documented rotation mapping)... verified on screenshots at all 4 rotations'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The minimap does not rotate, by explicit design, so this clause is trivially true for any implementation including a broken one. renderMinimap (js/render.js:2243) never reads cam.r; the code comments say so twice — 'stays north-up like every other minimap mode' at the dist branch, and 'Reads planes only — north-up, never cam.r.' near the end of the function. There is therefore no 'documented rotation mapping' for the minimap to apply, and the phrase invites an implementer to go looking for one that does not exist (the second incident's failure mode). Four screenshots of a north-up buffer prove nothing.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Drop the rotation clause from the minimap gate and state the real invariant instead: 'the Risk minimap is north-up like every other mode — assert renderMinimap's risk branch reads no cam.r (grep: 0 occurrences of cam.r inside the branch) and that the painted buffer is byte-identical at cam.r 0/1/2/3.' Keep the genuinely useful half unchanged: MM_NAMES has 14 entries, updateMapLegend returns a non-empty name+swatch for 'risk' with no stale caption, and the four band colours are 4 distinct hex values distinguishable by lightness as well as hue (the GQ11 deutan rule the other ramps follow). Note the real S4 rotation risk in GP8 lives in GP8b's dispatch sprites, where the gate is already correctly written.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8a — NAMED CONTRIBUTOR IS THE ARGMAX: 'the driver string the panel names equals the argmax of that row's own driver list in 200/200 cases'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: 'argmax of the driver list' is undefined over the drivers the scope actually specifies, because they are in incommensurable units: fire coverage 0..255, police funding 0..100 (percent), plant age in years vs PLANT_WARN_AGE=40, pollution and crime on their own index scales. The declared row shape is {id,label,val,blurb} — an argmax over raw `val` would name 'fire coverage 200' over 'funding 30%' purely because 255 > 100, which is a genuinely wrong claim to the player, and the gate as written would certify it. Separately, in its current form the gate is close to a tautology: it re-derives the same argmax from the same table the panel used, so it can only catch a display-wiring bug, never a modelling error.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'Each driver row carries a NORMALISED contribution field (0..1, its share of the row score, documented per driver) alongside its raw val; the panel names the argmax over that normalised field, ties broken by the documented id order. Across 200 scripted states spanning the ranges, the named string equals that argmax in 200/200. Additionally, on 12 hand-labelled single-cause states (only one driver moved off its healthy value) the panel names THAT driver in 12/12 — the half of the gate that can actually fail.'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8a — BAND RESPONSE: 'and no unrelated row changes band in the same window (0 spurious band changes)'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: A zero-tolerance absolute on a shared census. Every one of the four interventions moves quantities that feed every row: bulldozing fire stations changes deptStrain's fire cap AND its structure count (js/sim.js:4970-4990); setting funding.police to 0 changes polCov and, via recomputeMaps within 14 ticks, the crime plane that the riot row reads and the land-value chain other rows read; zoning 20 coastal tiles changes popLoad/jobLoad the moment any lot develops. Any row already sitting near a band boundary will flip on that shared movement — and the gate gives no rule for how far from a boundary the fixture must start. This is an unbounded-flakiness bar with no relationship to whether the ruler is correct.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Make it directional and comparative rather than absolute: 'each intervention moves its own row's SCORE by >= 2x the largest score change of any other row in the same window (4/4), and no other row's score moves in the direction that would be reported as worsening.' If a band-crossing assertion is wanted, state the fixture precondition: 'the test city is scripted so every row's score starts at least 25% of a band width from its nearest boundary — asserted before the intervention.'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8a — ONE BUGLE PER KIND: '20 launches per kind => exactly 20 entries per kind'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: newsQueue is a consumed queue, not an accumulator. newsFrame (js/ui.js:2097-2102) runs every frame from the main loop and shifts one entry off whenever #dlg-news is not open. Under any harness that lets the render loop run — which is the normal way this repo is driven, and is required by the same gate's 'invoking each row' clause going through the live menu closure — the queue will hold 0 or 1 entries, never 20, and the gate fails on correct code. Nothing in the gate says the loop is stopped or that pushes rather than residents are counted.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'Instrument the push site: wrap city.newsQueue.push and count calls. 20 scripted launches per kind produce exactly 20 push calls per kind (140 total), 7 distinct headline strings, 0 duplicate headlines across kinds, and every pushed entry is an object with non-empty headline/sub/body (never a bare number — newsFrame at js/ui.js:2101 dispatches on typeof ed === "number" to showNewspaper, so a numeric push would render as a tier promotion).'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — DIFFICULTY AXIS IS REAL AND TWISTER-SEASON IS UNMOVED: 'the generalized path fires tornadoes on exactly the same set of elapsed months as the pinned GP8a baseline across 20 seeds (0 differing spawn months, 0 differing medal tiers)'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Unachievable by construction, and it directly contradicts GP8b's own declared re-pin. The shipped schedule at js/scenarios.js:369-371 is guarded by '&& !c.disaster' — whether a scheduled tornado fires in a given month depends on whether a random misfortune happens to be active at that moment. GP8b replaces the probability at js/sim.js:5477 with a coupled pTick and re-weights the kind ladder, which changes both WHICH months carry an active disaster and the rng.hazard cursor position (each startDisaster consumes 4 rh.next() draws; the per-tick gate consumes 1). disastersEnabled defaults to true (js/sim.js:2017) and no scenario disables it, and Twisterton's scnBuildTown population clears the pop>200 gate, so random misfortunes definitely fire during the scenario. Therefore the set of elapsed months on which tornadoes fire MUST differ under any real coupling. Medal tier is downstream of months-left-at-win, which is downstream of how much development the extra/fewer disasters destroyed — so '0 differing medal tiers' is doubly unreachable. This is the exact shape of incident #1: a bar unreachable by construction and unrelated to the work.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Split the semantic claim from the byte claim. (i) SEMANTICS, asserted directly: 'the generalized pressure path, evaluated on twister-season's shipped {type:"tornado", everyMonths:2, months:12} config with the random-misfortune roll suppressed (disastersEnabled=false), fires on exactly the same elapsed-month set as the pinned baseline under the same suppression — 0 differing months — and sc.pressure defaults, medals {gold:18,silver:9} and winTarget 4000 are unchanged by grep.' (ii) OUTCOME, comparative per R1: 'with disasters enabled, twister-season run on this build vs the pinned GP8a baseline across 20 seeds: it still wins on every seed it won on baseline, and no medal tier regresses.' Never assert bit-for-bit month equality across a declared re-pin.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — CALIBRATION BAND: 'arm A's aggregate annual disaster rate is <= 23%/yr'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Trivially satisfied: 23%/yr is the CURRENT uncoupled rate (1-(1-0.0009)^288 = 22.84%/yr), so a build that does nothing whatsoever for arm A passes this clause, as does the GP8a baseline itself. It carries no information about whether the coupling helps a well-run city. The paired '>= 1.5x' clause is doing all the work; this half is a decorative absolute where the meaningful statement is comparative, which is exactly the pattern R1 exists to forbid.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'Arm A's aggregate annual disaster rate is at least 25% BELOW the GP8a baseline arm run on the same seeds and the same build script (i.e. good governance measurably buys safety, not merely the status quo), and arm B's is >= 1.5x arm A's.'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — COUPLING OUTCOME: 'with arm B's rate also re-measured against the GP8a baseline arm to prove the effect is coupling and not a global rate cut'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: No pass/fail criterion is attached. 'Also re-measured' names a measurement but never states what value would fail it. As written the clause can be satisfied by simply reporting a number, which means the anti-global-rate-cut protection — the whole reason the clause exists — is unenforceable.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'arm B's aggregate rate is >= the GP8a baseline arm's rate on the same seeds (a neglected city is never made SAFER by the coupling), and arm B's fire rate is strictly greater than baseline — so a uniform reduction in pTick cannot pass this gate.'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — DETERMINISM + PERF: 'The hazard vector is computed <= 1 time per 24-tick rollover and 0 times per frame (call counter)'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Contradicts GP8a, which this milestone builds on. GP8a's Risk minimap mode and #dlg-civdef panel both consume hazardReport(), and renderMinimap is driven from js/main.js:72 on a per-frame timer ('if (++mmCounter % 15 === 0) renderMinimap(city, UI.mapMode)') — i.e. roughly 4x/second whenever Risk is the selected mode. A naive call counter on hazardReport will therefore show many calls per second while the Risk view is open, failing '0 times per frame' on a correct implementation. The gate never distinguishes the sim-side hazVec computation from UI-side reads of the same pure function.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'Count only the SIM-side consumer: city.hazVec is assigned at most once per 24-tick rollover and never inside tick()'s per-tick body or any render path — asserted by a counter on the assignment site, not on hazardReport() itself. Separately assert that UI-side hazardReport() reads never write city state (serialize() byte-identical across 1000 Risk repaints, per GP8a's ZERO-DRAW gate).'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — SCENARIO WINNABILITY, COMPARATIVE (R1): 'months-left-at-win regresses by <= 2 months on any winning scenario'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: No seed or run count is specified, uniquely among GP8b's gates (every other one names 10, 20 or 100 samples). Since GP8b is a declared re-pin, a single scripted run per scenario is pure seed noise — the same script on the same build with a different seed can easily swing months-left by more than 2. The gate's structure is correct per R1; only its sample size is missing, which is enough to make it either flaky or accidentally lenient depending on the seed the implementer happens to pick.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: '...run the same scripted solutions on this build and on the pinned GP8a baseline across 20 seeds per scenario. No scenario that wins on baseline on a given seed loses on this build on that seed; no medal tier regresses on any seed; and the MEDIAN months-left-at-win across the 20 seeds regresses by <= 2 months on any winning scenario.'

preflight_missing_coverage: GP8a has NO performance gate at all, yet it ships an O(n) census on a per-frame timer. The Risk minimap mode is repainted from js/main.js:72 ('if (++mmCounter % 15 === 0) renderMinimap(city, UI.mapMode)') roughly 4x/second, and the per-tile band buffer needs hazardReport, which per the scope does a full coast-front scan plus City.deptStrain() (both O(map)). Worse, GP8b's perf gate is measured 'within 5% of the GP8a baseline' — so any regression GP8a introduces is baked into the baseline and never caught by either half. Needs a GP8a gate: mean frame time and _jaComp/_jaNC cache-hit rate over a 600-tick soak with the Risk minimap selected are within 5% of the pre-GP8a pin, and the risk band buffer is recomputed at most once per repaint (memoised on a sim revision counter, the terrRev/powerEpoch idiom).

GP8a's new ADVISORY_GATES row (FIRE_RISK_HIGH) has no gate that it ever fires, or that it stays quiet on a healthy city. A predicate that is never true is vacuously byte-neutral and passes every gate in the GP8a list — the byte-identity gate cannot tell a correct advisory from dead code. The GP5a precedent (POLICE_THIN / FIRE_THIN, js/sim.js:1758-1774) is the model. Needs: on a scripted thin-coverage city, diagnoseTile(i).advisories contains FIRE_RISK_HIGH on >= 1 tile with the documented evid rows populated; on a scripted healthy city it appears on 0 tiles.

GP8a's item 8 — 'optional auto-pause + camera jump on disaster start, behind a UI.prefs flag' — has no gate whatsoever, and it is the ONE item in GP8a that changes what the running game does when a disaster lands. It also adds new persisted state outside the save file (UI.prefs via savePrefs) with no round-trip gate. Needs: with the flag off, disaster start leaves UI.paused and cam.x/y/z/r unchanged (byte-neutral to the running session); with it on, exactly one pause and one camera jump per disaster start, not per tick; the pref survives a savePrefs/reload round-trip and defaults to the documented value when absent from localStorage.

GP8a adds four new Snd voices (quake/flood/riot/monster, js/audio.js:60-67 today holds only siren/boom/ufo) with no distinctness gate. S4's 'every failure state must be visually distinct from its working state' has an obvious audio analogue here — seven disasters sharing three voices is exactly the failure the milestone is fixing. The ZERO CONSOLE ERRORS gate only proves the four new voices do not throw. Needs at minimum: the 7 kind rows map to 7 distinct Snd functions (asserted by identity, not by ear), and each new voice's documented waveform/envelope parameters differ from all six others.

GP8a's Civil Defense 'Show me' buttons have no gate that they land on the right thing. The gate list covers the mode switch machinery (setMapMode / MM_NAMES / no stale caption) but nothing asserts that a row's focus function returns a tile that actually carries the named driver — and unlike GP6's survey, all seven focus functions are NEW here. Needs: for each of the 7 rows on a scripted city, focus() returns an in-map index, and for the rows with a spatial driver (fire coverage, police coverage, plant age, coastline) that tile is in the documented worst decile of the corresponding plane.

GP8b: the history-series double-key-list rule has no gate. The scope correctly names both sites (normaliseHistory js/sim.js:31 and its mirror in the >240 trim loop at js/sim.js:5274) and the substrate notes flag it as a repeat failure, but the requirement is stated conditionally ('If a monthly risk/disaster-rate history series ships') and no quality gate enforces it. Needs, conditional on shipping a series: the new key appears in BOTH hardcoded lists (grep asserts 2 occurrences); a save/load round-trip preserves the series (normaliseHistory does not drop it); and after >240 months the series is trimmed to the same length as every sibling series.

GP8b has no S4 gate on the coupled RATE itself — only on dispatch sprites. The player is told a band moved, but nothing gates that the world visibly reflects the changed exposure, and every visibility gate in the milestone sits on GP8a's panel, which was calibrated against a DIFFERENT (uncoupled) model. Needs: after GP8b lands, the Risk minimap and the panel band chips on a neglected city read materially worse than on a well-run city of comparable size — asserted on screenshots at the two arms — so the S4 expression tracks the coupling rather than the frozen GP8a calibration.

GP8b: the flood O(n^2) cost that the scope explicitly warns about (item 6: d.flooded.indexOf(ni) at js/sim.js:4768/4779) is not gated. The perf gate measures 'mean frame time over a 600-tick soak', which at even an elevated hazard rate will rarely contain a large flood at all, and mean frame time hides a spike anyway. Needs: worst-case tick time during a scripted maximum-extent flood is within a documented bound of the GP8a baseline's equivalent flood, and peak serialize() size during that same scripted flood grows by <= 5% (the existing clause, but paired to a SCRIPTED flood rather than to whichever flood the coupled model happens to produce, which is not a paired comparison).

GP8b: the M29 'no phantom count on a waterless map' invariant is named in scope item 7 but never gated against the coupled model. The coupled vector changes how often flood is picked, and the abort path at js/sim.js:4645 returns before recCur.disasters++ — so a re-weighting that routes more rolls to flood on a landlocked city silently changes the Almanac's 'Disasters Survived' column relative to the number of events the player actually experienced. Needs: on a landlocked 80x80 soak, recCur.disasters equals the count of disasters that actually started (0 phantom counts), and the panel's published flood odds on that city are 0.

milestones.title: Coupled hazard, scenario difficulty & emergency dispatch (behaviour, re-pinned, save v18)
milestones.scope:
BEHAVIOUR HALF, measured by the GP8a instrumentation.

1. COUPLE THE ROLL. Replace only the probability ARGUMENT at js/sim.js:5477 — `this.rng.hazard.chance(0.0009)` becomes `this.rng.hazard.chance(this.hazVec.pTick)` — keeping the `&&` short-circuit order and the `pop > 200` gate EXACTLY where they are (the GP1b comment at js/sim.js:5475-5476 records why), and keeping the kind pick at js/sim.js:5480 as ONE `rng.hazard.next()` draw whose ladder thresholds now come from the vector's per-kind weights instead of the constants at js/sim.js:5481-5487. Draw COUNT and ORDER at this site are unchanged (2 draws max, same positions) — this is what protects the shared hazard cursor from desynchronising roadWearTick's crumble draws at js/sim.js:3609/3614. `this.hazVec` is computed by the GP8a-certified pure hazardReport ONCE per rollover, in tick()'s %24 block alongside eduTick/approvalTick (js/sim.js:5498-5499), spending ZERO RNG; it is DERIVED, recomputed at load like GP6's megaOk, and NOT serialized.

2. PHASE-1 DEFECT #2 — scenario pressure + difficulty axis. Generalize js/scenarios.js:367-374 off `sc.pressure.type === "tornado"` to any of the 7 kinds, with explicit frequency/severity fields. The default MUST reproduce twister-season's shipped semantics exactly (js/scenarios.js:147 `{type:"tornado", everyMonths:2, months:12}`) or its pop>=4000 win and its gold-18/silver-9 medal cutoffs (js/scenarios.js:149) silently recalibrate.

3. EMERGENCY DISPATCH. A TOOLS entry (js/ui.js:62-124) with an availability predicate, refused through the existing toolLocked branch (js/ui.js:320-325) when no disaster is active and fire[] is empty; place() tool-string mapping at js/sim.js:6005. Allowance = City.deptStrain() (js/sim.js:4962-4996) — powered anchors x SVC_DEF.cap x funding/100, already computed in ONE O(n) scan; NEVER re-census. Engines SCALE the terms that already exist in fireTick — the coverage burn-down at js/sim.js:4534 and the spread chance at js/sim.js:4563 — they do not add a parallel mechanism. Police squads MULTIPLY the polCov riot drain that already exists at js/sim.js:4811. A Metropolis-tier (TIERS index 4, js/sim.js:561-568) Guard unit decrements d.ticks for the moving kinds only — quake terminates on its ring counter (`d.r > QUAKE_MAX || d.ticks <= 0`, js/sim.js:4750) and flood on depth/frontier (js/sim.js:4787), so d.ticks is NOT the universal clock.

4. NO NEW over[] ID. Dispatch units are plain-JSON roster objects on `city.dispatch` ({kind,x,y,ticks,cost}) drawn render-only from world-space state with rotation applied at draw time — the certified GP4b trains precedent — NOT new OV ids. This deliberately keeps the milestone out of the `t >= OV.ZR` crosstalk web (power conduction js/sim.js:2341, demand 2371, brownout 2395, y2k 2411, pump feed 2435, fire candidacy 4596-4602) and out of ui.js's index-keyed ovName. A firebreak is expressed as fire[i]=0 plus a roster marker, never a tile id.

5. SAVE v18. Append `dispatch` AFTER recallDone (js/sim.js:5744-5745) so the whole v17 key sequence stays a character-stable prefix; bump `v: 17` at js/sim.js:5652 to 18. Defensive Array.isArray guard on load, defaulting to []; NO version-equality test anywhere in deserialize (js/sim.js:5749-5990). fire[] IS ALREADY SERIALIZED — packU8 at js/sim.js:5734, unpackU8 at js/sim.js:5917, fixed by GP1b at v12; DO NOT rebuild it (substrate rule). If a monthly risk/disaster-rate history series ships, extend BOTH hardcoded key lists — normaliseHistory (js/sim.js:31) and the >240 trim loop at js/sim.js:5274.

6. Watch flood's O(n^2) `d.flooded.indexOf(ni)` membership test (js/sim.js:4768, 4779): a vector that makes flood more common raises both its per-tick cost and its serialized size, and d.flooded rides inside this.disaster.

7. recCur.disasters (bumped per SUCCESSFUL branch, js/sim.js:4589-4591; rendered at js/ui.js:1456) is the Almanac's 'Disasters Survived' column — a rate change rewrites it, and the M29 'no phantom count on a waterless map' invariant must survive. LAUNCH CONDITION (preflight, non-negotiable): the gate problems recorded in preflight_gate_problems below were found by an adversarial reviewer that read the LIVE source and MEASURED the unchanged build. The design phase MUST resolve every one before implementation, and each resolution must be reported in the ship verdict with its measurement. Rules for resolving: an IMPOSSIBILITY (unachievable/self-contradictory/vacuous — the sim arithmetic or the fixture cannot produce the quantity) is corrected by re-specifying the gate so it measures the intended property with a reachable bar, and the correction is recorded with the measurement proving the original was impossible. An ABSOLUTE-SHOULD-BE-COMPARATIVE bar is restated per the R1 protocol (this build vs baseline on identical scripted inputs). An AMBIGUOUS-THRESHOLD gate is pinned to a named city, seed, sample count and reference quantity. An UNMEASURABLE gate is either given a concrete headless observable or reported to the user as needing a design decision. A resolution that changes what the milestone is TRYING TO ACHIEVE (rather than how it is measured) is a DESIGN decision — surface it to the user, never decide it (S6). Also close every missing_coverage item or justify its omission.
milestones.player_facing_win: Disasters become the itemized bill for decisions the player could already see coming on the Civil Defense panel — a neglected fire department measurably burns more often than a funded one — and when something lands, the dispatch allowance is always smaller than the fire front, so the player has to choose what to let burn.
quality_gates: FLAG-OFF BYTE-IDENTITY + DECLARED RE-PIN: with disastersEnabled=false, 20 seeds x 600 ticks Math.random UNSTUBBED are byte-identical to the pinned GP8a build (0 differing serialize bytes at ticks 200/400/600) and rng.hazard.s is unchanged from its tick-0 value except for the pre-existing roadWearTick draws — asserted by an instrumented draw counter showing exactly 0 hazard draws attributable to the vector, and roadWear[] byte-identical. With the flag ON, the counter shows exactly 2 hazard draws per triggered misfortune (gate + kind), the same as the GP8a baseline; the re-pin is declared in the commit.

COUPLING OUTCOME OVER A HORIZON vs A CONTROL: 10 seeded 50-year headless runs per arm at matched population (within ±5%) — arm A has fireCov >= SVC_OK over >=90% of zoned tiles and police funding 100%, arm B is neglected. Measured as counts of successful startDisaster('fire') and ('riot') over the horizon, arm A suffers >=50% fewer fires and >=70% fewer riots than arm B, with arm B's rate also re-measured against the GP8a baseline arm to prove the effect is coupling and not a global rate cut.

CALIBRATION BAND + THE RULER STAYS HONEST: over the same 10 x 50-year runs, arm A's aggregate annual disaster rate is <= 23%/yr and arm B's is >= 1.5x arm A's; and the GP8a honesty gate re-runs green against the now-coupled model — the panel's published per-year odds match the measured empirical rate within ±20% relative, per-kind and aggregate.

DIFFICULTY AXIS IS REAL AND TWISTER-SEASON IS UNMOVED: every one of the 7 kinds is accepted as sc.pressure.type and fires that kind; two documented difficulty settings produce measured event counts differing by >= 2.0x over 10 seeded 120-month scenario runs (ratio computed on totals, both >= 5 events so the ratio is not noise); and the shipped twister-season schedule is bit-for-bit unchanged — the generalized path fires tornadoes on exactly the same set of elapsed months as the pinned GP8a baseline across 20 seeds (0 differing spawn months, 0 differing medal tiers).

DISPATCH AGENCY, § AND EXPIRY: on 20 paired seeded fires (identical seed, identical ignition tile, dispatch vs no dispatch) the median reduction in total tiles lost — rubble plus burnt FOREST at burnout — is >= 35% and >= 15 of 20 individual pairs clear 35%; across 100 sampled fires the allowance computed from deptStrain is strictly smaller than the burning front at its peak in >= 90 of 100; § charged equals unitCount x the documented per-unit cost to the exact §  in 100/100 dispatches; and city.dispatch.length === 0 within one tick of this.disaster becoming null or fire[] emptying, in 100/100 sampled events.

SAVE v18 LADDER + MID-EVENT PERSISTENCE: the payload declares v:18 and the entire v17 key sequence is a character-identical prefix; pinned v17, v16, v14 and v12 saves all load with dispatch defaulting to [] under Array.isArray guards and no version-equality test anywhere in deserialize (grep asserts 0 occurrences of a v===N test). For each of the 7 kinds: start -> tick 5 -> serialize -> deserialize -> serialize is byte-identical (7/7), and continuing 100 ticks from the reloaded city produces a serialize byte-identical to continuing the original (7/7). A mid-fire save with >=10 burning tiles and >=1 dispatched engine restores fire[] and the roster exactly and burns to an identical final rubble count.

ANTI-CROSSTALK, ASSERTED AS A BOOLEAN: Object.keys(OV).length and every OV id value are identical to the GP8a baseline (true), and a grep confirms 0 new `>= OV.ZR` comparison sites — so power conduction (js/sim.js:2341), demand (2371), brownout (2395), y2k flicker (2411), pump feed (2435) and fire candidacy (4596-4602) are provably untouched. Dispatch units render from world-space roster state at all 4 rotations: 20 sampled unit screen positions match the analytic rotation transform within 1px at cam.r 0/1/2/3, and an expired/spent unit is a visually distinct sprite from an active one (S4).

SCENARIO WINNABILITY, COMPARATIVE (R1): all FOUR scenarios — gridlock-97, twister-season, blackout-summer-97, y2k-ready (js/scenarios.js:93/139/183/233; there are four, not five) — run the same scripted solutions on this build and on the pinned GP8a baseline. No scenario that wins on baseline loses on this build, no medal tier regresses, and months-left-at-win regresses by <= 2 months on any winning scenario. Any scenario the reference script never wins on EITHER build is excluded and reported, never scored as a failure.

DETERMINISM + PERF: same seed + same script reproduces identical serialize() and identical history series over 600 ticks across 3 consecutive runs with Math.random UNSTUBBED, in both flag states (6/6, 0 differing bytes). The hazard vector is computed <= 1 time per 24-tick rollover and 0 times per frame (call counter); recomputeJobAccess's _jaComp/_jaNC cache-hit rate and mean frame time over a 600-tick soak are within 5% of the GP8a baseline; peak save size during an active flood grows by <= 5% vs baseline. Zero console errors across boot, soak, all 7 kinds, dispatch, and save/load.
milestones.split_rationale: Every gate here is measured by instrumentation GP8a already proved honest: the coupling gate reads the same startDisaster counts the panel's odds are calibrated against, and the calibration gate is literally GP8a's honesty gate re-run against the changed model — if the sim moves and the ruler does not follow, this half fails. The drift report's two biggest traps are designed out rather than gated around: the shared rng.hazard cursor (consumed by roadWearTick at js/sim.js:3609/3614 as well as the three disaster sites) is protected by holding the draw count and order at js/sim.js:5477-5480 constant and computing the vector with zero RNG, so road crumbling in a 0%-roads-funding city cannot desynchronise; and the anti-crosstalk web is avoided entirely by shipping dispatch as GP4b-style render-only roster objects instead of new over[] ids, which turns an eight-site predicate audit into a single boolean assertion. Three shipped-work landmines are explicitly fenced: fire[] serialization already exists at v12 (js/sim.js:5734/5917) and must not be rebuilt; the polCov riot drain already exists at js/sim.js:4811 and is multiplied, not introduced; and fireTick's coverage burn-down (4534) and spread suppression (4563) already exist and are scaled, not paralleled. The scenario gate is comparative per R1 and names four scenarios, because the milestone's 'all 5' is unrunnable as written.
milestones.save_version_plan:
GP8a takes NO version bump and adds NO save key and NO history series. It stays at v17 (js/sim.js:5652) with a character-identical payload — that is what makes its byte-identical gate a real proof rather than a diff-tolerance. Nothing it ships is persistent state: hazardReport is derived-on-demand, newsQueue is never serialized (init js/sim.js:2031, reset to [] on load at js/sim.js:5948), the ADVISORY_GATES row is a pure read, and MENUS/minimap/dialog work is UI-only.

GP8b OWNS SAVE v18 — the next ladder integer after GP6's v17. Exactly one new key: `dispatch`, the emergency-unit roster, a plain JSON array of {kind,x,y,ticks,cost} objects appended AFTER recallDone (js/sim.js:5744-5745) so the entire v17 key sequence remains a character-stable prefix. Loaded with `Array.isArray(d.dispatch) ? ... : []`, no version-equality test anywhere in deserialize (js/sim.js:5749-5990); v17/v16/v14/v12 saves all load with an empty roster.

DO NOT re-add fire[] — GP1b already serializes it as a packU8 base64 plane at js/sim.js:5734 and restores it via unpackU8 at js/sim.js:5917 (the fix comment is at js/sim.js:5717-5719), and the mid-fire round-trip passes on HEAD today. The milestone spec's claim that "fire[] is not in serialize() at all" is stale by two ladder rungs; re-adding it would duplicate the key and break the character-stable-prefix rule. this.disaster is likewise already conditionally serialized (js/sim.js:5701) and restored (js/sim.js:5967) — the roster rides beside it, not inside it, precisely because startDisaster('fire') returns at js/sim.js:4607 without ever setting this.disaster, which is the 55%-likeliest kind.

hazVec is DERIVED and deliberately NOT serialized — recomputed at load from restored state, the GP6 megaOk precedent. If GP8b ships a monthly risk or disaster-rate history series, BOTH hardcoded key lists must be extended in the same commit: normaliseHistory (js/sim.js:31) and its mirror in the >240 trim loop at js/sim.js:5274 — the warning comments sit at js/sim.js:23-27 and js/sim.js:5270-5272.
milestones.launch_order_note:
Launch GP8a first, alone, and certify it before GP8b starts — the whole value of the split is that GP8b's coupling and calibration gates are measured by a ruler already proven honest against the shipped 22.84%/yr model.

SPLIT-BOUNDARY DECISION (the drift report flagged this as unwinnable-by-construction if left ambiguous): the milestone's Phase 1 is DIVIDED across the two halves. Menu registration of the four orphaned kinds (js/ui.js:372-379) goes in GP8a because a menu closure only fires on click and is therefore draw-neutral. Scenario-pressure generalization (js/scenarios.js:367-374) goes in GP8b because its own gate — ">=2 difficulty settings whose measured event frequency differs by >=2x" — is a behavioural measurement and cannot live under a byte-identical sim gate. GP8a's byte-identity gate must be run in BOTH disastersEnabled states, because the flag-off zero-draw property is already green on HEAD by GP1b's short-circuit design (js/sim.js:5477) and the real risk is regressing it, not achieving it.

Both halves are independently shippable per S8: GP8a alone delivers the Civil Defense panel, all seven kinds reachable from the menu, seven Bugle front pages, the Risk minimap mode and the first disaster advisor lines, with zero sim risk and no save bump. If the session caps after GP8a, the game is coherent and certified.

TWO ITEMS NEED A USER DECISION BEFORE GP8b IS BRIEFED (S6 — reported, not silently reinterpreted): (1) MELTDOWN appears in the spec's seven-row vector but exists nowhere in the tree (the only 'meltdown' string is a transit joke at js/advisors.js:97) while TORNADO — built, menu-listed and the sole scenario pressure type — is absent from it; shipping MELTDOWN is an unpriced 8th disaster kind requiring a new sim branch, rotation-aware art, a sound voice and a Bugle page, well beyond the 4->5 re-rate. The split assumes, pending the user's call, that the vector's seven rows are the seven BUILT kinds and that the plantYear/OV.NUKE age driver becomes a named contributor to the FIRE row. (2) The gate phrase "all 5 scenarios remain winnable" is unrunnable — js/scenarios.js:91-296 holds exactly four scenarios, and GP7 and GP9 repeat the same wording, so it is a systematic docs error worth fixing across all three entries.

One more baseline correction to carry into the brief: quake/flood/riot/monster are NOT absent from play today — they already spawn from the random ladder at js/sim.js:5484-5487. Any baseline capture for GP8b's coupling gate must therefore be taken against the current seven-kind ladder, never against a fire/tornado/ufo-only assumption.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8a — HONEST ODDS AT THE CALIBRATION POINT vs GP8a — BAND RESPONSE WITHIN ONE ROLLOVER
preflight_gate_problems.problem: These two gates cannot both pass, and the contradiction is forced by GP8a's own BYTE-IDENTICAL SIM gate. Because GP8a provably does not move the sim, the true hazard rate on EVERY city is the constant 1-(1-0.0009)^288 = 22.84%/yr and the true per-kind split is the fixed ladder at js/sim.js:5481-5487, independent of fire coverage, police funding, plant age or coastline. Scope item 3 puts the band chip AND the live per-year odds figure on the same row, derived from the same row score. So either (a) the published odds are constant across cities — the honesty gate passes but it is a single-point identity, the band chip can never move, and BAND RESPONSE fails 0/4; or (b) the odds vary with city state so the bands move — BAND RESPONSE passes, and the honesty gate then fails on every soak city that is not the calibration reference, because four bands spanning Low/Elevated/High/Severe imply an odds spread far wider than ±20% relative. The scope text half-concedes this ('normalised so that a documented REFERENCE CITY sits exactly on those shipped odds') but the gate measures '10 seeded 50-year soaks', not the reference city. This is the same shape as the y=12/y=9/y=15 incident: the fixture cannot produce the measured quantity.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Split the claim in two. (i) CALIBRATION-POINT IDENTITY (GP8a): on the ONE documented reference city, hazardReport().pTick equals 0.0009 to 1e-9 and the seven row weights equal the shipped ladder to 1e-9 — an exact analytic assertion, no soak needed. (ii) MONOTONIC RESPONSE (GP8a): the four scripted interventions each move their own row's SCORE strictly in the documented direction and cross at least one band boundary. Move the empirical ±20% honesty measurement entirely to GP8b, where the sim actually follows the ruler. Additionally: on GP8a the panel must not print a per-year odds figure that varies by city while the sim's rate does not — either print the odds only on the reference calibration, or label the varying number as 'exposure', which is what it actually is on this half.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8a — HONEST ODDS: 'the measured per-kind shares are each within ±20% relative of the panel's per-kind odds'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Statistically unachievable by construction at the specified sample size. 10 soaks x 50 years = 500 city-years; at 22.84%/yr that is ~114 total events. Monster is 1.5% of the ladder => expected 1.7 events across the WHOLE experiment; riot 5.5% => ~6.3; flood 7% => ~8. A Poisson count with mean 1.7 has ~77% relative standard deviation. To hold the monster share inside ±20% relative at 95% confidence you need ~96 monster events, i.e. ~6,400 total events, i.e. ~28,000 city-years — 56x the specified budget. The gate will fail on a perfectly correct implementation on most seed sets, and passing it once would be luck. Only the fire row (~63 events, ~13% rel. sd) is even marginally powered.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Either (a) assert the per-kind split ANALYTICALLY rather than empirically — hazardReport()'s seven normalised weights equal the shipped ladder constants (.55/.13/.10/.08/.07/.055/.015) to 1e-9 — which is exact, free, and actually proves the thing; or (b) keep the empirical form only for the AGGREGATE rate and for kinds whose expected count over the horizon is >= 30, and explicitly exclude kinds below that floor from scoring, reporting their observed counts instead. The same fix is needed on GP8b's 'CALIBRATION BAND + THE RULER STAYS HONEST', which re-runs the identical per-kind ±20% test at the identical 500-city-year budget.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8a — S4 ROTATION + FAILURE-STATE DISTINCTNESS: 'the Risk minimap mode produces an identical per-tile band buffer at cam.r 0/1/2/3 (0 differing tiles after the documented rotation mapping)... verified on screenshots at all 4 rotations'
