preflight_gate_problems.problem: The minimap does not rotate, by explicit design, so this clause is trivially true for any implementation including a broken one. renderMinimap (js/render.js:2243) never reads cam.r; the code comments say so twice — 'stays north-up like every other minimap mode' at the dist branch, and 'Reads planes only — north-up, never cam.r.' near the end of the function. There is therefore no 'documented rotation mapping' for the minimap to apply, and the phrase invites an implementer to go looking for one that does not exist (the second incident's failure mode). Four screenshots of a north-up buffer prove nothing.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Drop the rotation clause from the minimap gate and state the real invariant instead: 'the Risk minimap is north-up like every other mode — assert renderMinimap's risk branch reads no cam.r (grep: 0 occurrences of cam.r inside the branch) and that the painted buffer is byte-identical at cam.r 0/1/2/3.' Keep the genuinely useful half unchanged: MM_NAMES has 14 entries, updateMapLegend returns a non-empty name+swatch for 'risk' with no stale caption, and the four band colours are 4 distinct hex values distinguishable by lightness as well as hue (the GQ11 deutan rule the other ramps follow). Note the real S4 rotation risk in GP8 lives in GP8b's dispatch sprites, where the gate is already correctly written.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — DIFFICULTY AXIS IS REAL AND TWISTER-SEASON IS UNMOVED: 'the generalized path fires tornadoes on exactly the same set of elapsed months as the pinned GP8a baseline across 20 seeds (0 differing spawn months, 0 differing medal tiers)'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Unachievable by construction, and it directly contradicts GP8b's own declared re-pin. The shipped schedule at js/scenarios.js:369-371 is guarded by '&& !c.disaster' — whether a scheduled tornado fires in a given month depends on whether a random misfortune happens to be active at that moment. GP8b replaces the probability at js/sim.js:5477 with a coupled pTick and re-weights the kind ladder, which changes both WHICH months carry an active disaster and the rng.hazard cursor position (each startDisaster consumes 4 rh.next() draws; the per-tick gate consumes 1). disastersEnabled defaults to true (js/sim.js:2017) and no scenario disables it, and Twisterton's scnBuildTown population clears the pop>200 gate, so random misfortunes definitely fire during the scenario. Therefore the set of elapsed months on which tornadoes fire MUST differ under any real coupling. Medal tier is downstream of months-left-at-win, which is downstream of how much development the extra/fewer disasters destroyed — so '0 differing medal tiers' is doubly unreachable. This is the exact shape of incident #1: a bar unreachable by construction and unrelated to the work.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Split the semantic claim from the byte claim. (i) SEMANTICS, asserted directly: 'the generalized pressure path, evaluated on twister-season's shipped {type:"tornado", everyMonths:2, months:12} config with the random-misfortune roll suppressed (disastersEnabled=false), fires on exactly the same elapsed-month set as the pinned baseline under the same suppression — 0 differing months — and sc.pressure defaults, medals {gold:18,silver:9} and winTarget 4000 are unchanged by grep.' (ii) OUTCOME, comparative per R1: 'with disasters enabled, twister-season run on this build vs the pinned GP8a baseline across 20 seeds: it still wins on every seed it won on baseline, and no medal tier regresses.' Never assert bit-for-bit month equality across a declared re-pin.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — DISPATCH AGENCY: 'the allowance computed from deptStrain is strictly smaller than the burning front at its peak in >= 90 of 100'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Unit mismatch — the two sides of the comparison are not the same kind of quantity, and no conversion is documented anywhere in the spec. deptStrain's cap (js/sim.js:4986) is powered_fire_anchors x SVC_DEF[OV.FIRESTA].cap x funding/100, and SVC_DEF fire cap is 240 STRUCTURES COVERED (js/sim.js:1405). A modest city with 5 powered stations at 100% funding yields cap = 1200. The 'burning front at its peak' is a count of tiles with fire[i] > 0 — typically tens, since fireTick decrements by up to 3/tick with the cov>40 bonus (js/sim.js:4534) and fire[] is seeded at 8-17. So 'allowance strictly smaller than the front' is systematically FALSE by two orders of magnitude, in essentially 0 of 100 samples rather than 90. The gate is only measurable once the spec documents the mapping from deptStrain's structure-capacity number to a dispatch UNIT COUNT — and that mapping is the actual design decision this gate is supposed to be policing.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Document the derivation in the scope and gate it as one formula: 'units = floor(deptStrain().fire.cap / DISPATCH_UNIT_LOAD) with DISPATCH_UNIT_LOAD a named frozen constant; the gate asserts units < (count of tiles with fire[i] > 0 at the fire's peak) in >= 90 of 100 sampled fires, and that DISPATCH_UNIT_LOAD is chosen so this holds — i.e. the scarcity is a designed constant, stated, not an emergent hope.' Also reconcile the player_facing_win, which promises the allowance is ALWAYS smaller, with the gate's 90/100.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — DISPATCH AGENCY: 'city.dispatch.length === 0 within one tick of this.disaster becoming null or fire[] emptying, in 100/100 sampled events'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Read as the disjunction it is literally written as, this gate forbids dispatch from ever existing during a fire — which is the milestone's headline mechanic. startDisaster('fire') sets fire[] and returns at js/sim.js:4607 WITHOUT ever assigning this.disaster; the split spec itself notes this fact in its save_version_plan. So during every fire, this.disaster is already null, the first disjunct is permanently satisfied, and the assertion demands city.dispatch.length === 0 at all times. Fire is 55% of the ladder, so this covers the majority case. The intent is obviously a conjunction, but an implementer running the gate as written fails on correct code — the second incident's failure mode verbatim.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'city.dispatch.length === 0 within one tick of the city becoming quiet, where quiet is defined as (this.disaster === null AND no i with fire[i] > 0) — asserted in 100/100 sampled events. Separately, dispatch units targeted at a disaster that ends while units are still alive are cleared in the same tick the disaster clears (100/100), and a unit whose ticks reach 0 is removed on that tick regardless of city state.'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — COUPLING OUTCOME OVER A HORIZON vs A CONTROL: 'at matched population (within ±5%)'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Circular and unstated as to when it is measured. Arm B is deliberately neglected — no fire coverage, 0% police funding — which in this sim suppresses growth through the certified GP5a/GP5b chain (svcStrain multiplies stampCoverage potency, crime suppresses land value) AND, under the very coupling this gate is measuring, destroys developed tiles to fire and riot. So the intervention under test is precisely what breaks the matching condition, and the tighter the coupling works the further apart the populations drift. The gate does not say whether ±5% is checked at tick 0, at the end, or as a horizon mean, and the three give different verdicts. Left as written this becomes either an unsatisfiable precondition or a silently-reinterpreted one.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Normalise instead of matching: 'measured as successful startDisaster(kind) counts PER 1000 POPULATION-YEARS, integrating population over the horizon rather than requiring the two arms to end at the same size. Report both arms' population trajectories. Arm A's fire rate per 1000 pop-years is >= 50% below arm B's, and arm A's riot rate >= 70% below arm B's.' If a matched-population design is genuinely wanted, pin it as a scripted-and-frozen footprint: both arms build the identical zoned footprint from the same script and growth is not the variable under test.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — COUPLING OUTCOME: 'arm A suffers ... >= 70% fewer riots than arm B'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Noise-dominated at the specified horizon, and — unlike the difficulty-axis gate in the same list — it carries no minimum-event floor. Riot is 5.5% of the ladder; at the baseline 22.84%/yr that is ~1.26%/yr, i.e. ~0.63 riots per 50-year run and ~6 riots for arm B across all 10 runs. Coupling will raise arm B's number, but plausibly only into the teens. Requiring a >= 70% reduction against a denominator of order 10 means one or two lucky events flips the verdict. The very next gate in the same list gets this right ('both >= 5 events so the ratio is not noise'), so the omission here is inconsistent within the milestone.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Add the same floor and widen the horizon for the rare kinds: 'arm B accumulates >= 20 riots over the horizon (extend the number of seeded runs until it does, reporting the count) before the ratio is scored; then arm A's riot rate is >= 70% below arm B's.' Or drop riot from the numeric bar and gate it directionally — 'arm A's riot rate is strictly below arm B's in >= 8 of 10 paired seeds' — which is measurable at this sample size.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — CALIBRATION BAND: 'arm A's aggregate annual disaster rate is <= 23%/yr'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Trivially satisfied: 23%/yr is the CURRENT uncoupled rate (1-(1-0.0009)^288 = 22.84%/yr), so a build that does nothing whatsoever for arm A passes this clause, as does the GP8a baseline itself. It carries no information about whether the coupling helps a well-run city. The paired '>= 1.5x' clause is doing all the work; this half is a decorative absolute where the meaningful statement is comparative, which is exactly the pattern R1 exists to forbid.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'Arm A's aggregate annual disaster rate is at least 25% BELOW the GP8a baseline arm run on the same seeds and the same build script (i.e. good governance measurably buys safety, not merely the status quo), and arm B's is >= 1.5x arm A's.'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — COUPLING OUTCOME: 'with arm B's rate also re-measured against the GP8a baseline arm to prove the effect is coupling and not a global rate cut'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: No pass/fail criterion is attached. 'Also re-measured' names a measurement but never states what value would fail it. As written the clause can be satisfied by simply reporting a number, which means the anti-global-rate-cut protection — the whole reason the clause exists — is unenforceable.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'arm B's aggregate rate is >= the GP8a baseline arm's rate on the same seeds (a neglected city is never made SAFER by the coupling), and arm B's fire rate is strictly greater than baseline — so a uniform reduction in pTick cannot pass this gate.'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — DETERMINISM + PERF: 'The hazard vector is computed <= 1 time per 24-tick rollover and 0 times per frame (call counter)'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Contradicts GP8a, which this milestone builds on. GP8a's Risk minimap mode and #dlg-civdef panel both consume hazardReport(), and renderMinimap is driven from js/main.js:72 on a per-frame timer ('if (++mmCounter % 15 === 0) renderMinimap(city, UI.mapMode)') — i.e. roughly 4x/second whenever Risk is the selected mode. A naive call counter on hazardReport will therefore show many calls per second while the Risk view is open, failing '0 times per frame' on a correct implementation. The gate never distinguishes the sim-side hazVec computation from UI-side reads of the same pure function.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: 'Count only the SIM-side consumer: city.hazVec is assigned at most once per 24-tick rollover and never inside tick()'s per-tick body or any render path — asserted by a counter on the assignment site, not on hazardReport() itself. Separately assert that UI-side hazardReport() reads never write city state (serialize() byte-identical across 1000 Risk repaints, per GP8a's ZERO-DRAW gate).'

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP8b — SCENARIO WINNABILITY, COMPARATIVE (R1): 'months-left-at-win regresses by <= 2 months on any winning scenario'
preflight_gate_problems.problem: No seed or run count is specified, uniquely among GP8b's gates (every other one names 10, 20 or 100 samples). Since GP8b is a declared re-pin, a single scripted run per scenario is pure seed noise — the same script on the same build with a different seed can easily swing months-left by more than 2. The gate's structure is correct per R1; only its sample size is missing, which is enough to make it either flaky or accidentally lenient depending on the seed the implementer happens to pick.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: '...run the same scripted solutions on this build and on the pinned GP8a baseline across 20 seeds per scenario. No scenario that wins on baseline on a given seed loses on this build on that seed; no medal tier regresses on any seed; and the MEDIAN months-left-at-win across the 20 seeds regresses by <= 2 months on any winning scenario.'

preflight_missing_coverage: GP8a has NO performance gate at all, yet it ships an O(n) census on a per-frame timer. The Risk minimap mode is repainted from js/main.js:72 ('if (++mmCounter % 15 === 0) renderMinimap(city, UI.mapMode)') roughly 4x/second, and the per-tile band buffer needs hazardReport, which per the scope does a full coast-front scan plus City.deptStrain() (both O(map)). Worse, GP8b's perf gate is measured 'within 5% of the GP8a baseline' — so any regression GP8a introduces is baked into the baseline and never caught by either half. Needs a GP8a gate: mean frame time and _jaComp/_jaNC cache-hit rate over a 600-tick soak with the Risk minimap selected are within 5% of the pre-GP8a pin, and the risk band buffer is recomputed at most once per repaint (memoised on a sim revision counter, the terrRev/powerEpoch idiom).

GP8a's new ADVISORY_GATES row (FIRE_RISK_HIGH) has no gate that it ever fires, or that it stays quiet on a healthy city. A predicate that is never true is vacuously byte-neutral and passes every gate in the GP8a list — the byte-identity gate cannot tell a correct advisory from dead code. The GP5a precedent (POLICE_THIN / FIRE_THIN, js/sim.js:1758-1774) is the model. Needs: on a scripted thin-coverage city, diagnoseTile(i).advisories contains FIRE_RISK_HIGH on >= 1 tile with the documented evid rows populated; on a scripted healthy city it appears on 0 tiles.

GP8a's item 8 — 'optional auto-pause + camera jump on disaster start, behind a UI.prefs flag' — has no gate whatsoever, and it is the ONE item in GP8a that changes what the running game does when a disaster lands. It also adds new persisted state outside the save file (UI.prefs via savePrefs) with no round-trip gate. Needs: with the flag off, disaster start leaves UI.paused and cam.x/y/z/r unchanged (byte-neutral to the running session); with it on, exactly one pause and one camera jump per disaster start, not per tick; the pref survives a savePrefs/reload round-trip and defaults to the documented value when absent from localStorage.

GP8a adds four new Snd voices (quake/flood/riot/monster, js/audio.js:60-67 today holds only siren/boom/ufo) with no distinctness gate. S4's 'every failure state must be visually distinct from its working state' has an obvious audio analogue here — seven disasters sharing three voices is exactly the failure the milestone is fixing. The ZERO CONSOLE ERRORS gate only proves the four new voices do not throw. Needs at minimum: the 7 kind rows map to 7 distinct Snd functions (asserted by identity, not by ear), and each new voice's documented waveform/envelope parameters differ from all six others.

GP8a's Civil Defense 'Show me' buttons have no gate that they land on the right thing. The gate list covers the mode switch machinery (setMapMode / MM_NAMES / no stale caption) but nothing asserts that a row's focus function returns a tile that actually carries the named driver — and unlike GP6's survey, all seven focus functions are NEW here. Needs: for each of the 7 rows on a scripted city, focus() returns an in-map index, and for the rows with a spatial driver (fire coverage, police coverage, plant age, coastline) that tile is in the documented worst decile of the corresponding plane.

GP8b: the history-series double-key-list rule has no gate. The scope correctly names both sites (normaliseHistory js/sim.js:31 and its mirror in the >240 trim loop at js/sim.js:5274) and the substrate notes flag it as a repeat failure, but the requirement is stated conditionally ('If a monthly risk/disaster-rate history series ships') and no quality gate enforces it. Needs, conditional on shipping a series: the new key appears in BOTH hardcoded lists (grep asserts 2 occurrences); a save/load round-trip preserves the series (normaliseHistory does not drop it); and after >240 months the series is trimmed to the same length as every sibling series.

GP8b has no S4 gate on the coupled RATE itself — only on dispatch sprites. The player is told a band moved, but nothing gates that the world visibly reflects the changed exposure, and every visibility gate in the milestone sits on GP8a's panel, which was calibrated against a DIFFERENT (uncoupled) model. Needs: after GP8b lands, the Risk minimap and the panel band chips on a neglected city read materially worse than on a well-run city of comparable size — asserted on screenshots at the two arms — so the S4 expression tracks the coupling rather than the frozen GP8a calibration.

GP8b: the flood O(n^2) cost that the scope explicitly warns about (item 6: d.flooded.indexOf(ni) at js/sim.js:4768/4779) is not gated. The perf gate measures 'mean frame time over a 600-tick soak', which at even an elevated hazard rate will rarely contain a large flood at all, and mean frame time hides a spike anyway. Needs: worst-case tick time during a scripted maximum-extent flood is within a documented bound of the GP8a baseline's equivalent flood, and peak serialize() size during that same scripted flood grows by <= 5% (the existing clause, but paired to a SCRIPTED flood rather than to whichever flood the coupled model happens to produce, which is not a paired comparison).

GP8b: the M29 'no phantom count on a waterless map' invariant is named in scope item 7 but never gated against the coupled model. The coupled vector changes how often flood is picked, and the abort path at js/sim.js:4645 returns before recCur.disasters++ — so a re-weighting that routes more rolls to flood on a landlocked city silently changes the Almanac's 'Disasters Survived' column relative to the number of events the player actually experienced. Needs: on a landlocked 80x80 soak, recCur.disasters equals the count of disasters that actually started (0 phantom counts), and the panel's published flood odds on that city are 0.
milestones.split_of: GP8 (preflight-authored S3 split, grounded against the live source 2026-07-30)

milestones.title: The Waste Ledger — the garbage number, the honest power pie, and the crosstalk audit (read-first)
milestones.scope:
NO new over[] ids, NO tools, NO disposal, NO pollution/land-value coupling. Six deliverables, all pure reads over state that already exists.

(1) WASTE_RATE + the tonnage ruler. New frozen per-zone-type x per-level rate table sited beside RES_POP/COM_JOB/IND_JOB (js/sim.js:365-367), industry heaviest per the M31 design. Two readers: `City.wasteRateAt(i)` — O(1), pure, from over[i]+lvl[i] (+ ordMods.wasteMul, see 3) — and `City.wasteCensus()` returning {total, res, com, ind, byLevel[]}, one O(n) scan following the deptStrain() purity contract documented at js/sim.js:4948-4961. PERF: wasteCensus is called ONLY from collectBudget's monthly rollover and from UI fills — never from tick/growthPass/recomputeMaps — so it does NOT add a scan to the per-14-tick sim path the hazard forbids. The minimap paints wasteRateAt(i) per tile directly (the `mode==="poll"` idiom at js/render.js:2262-2266), allocating no plane.

(2) history.waste — the certified series GP9b's overflow curve is measured against. SIX sites: normaliseHistory's hardcoded key list (js/sim.js:31), its mirror in collectBudget's >240 trim loop (js/sim.js:5274-5276 — BOTH carry SECOND LIST WARNING comments), the ctor history literal (js/sim.js:2009), the push in collectBudget after `approv` (js/sim.js:5267), UI.graphSeries (js/ui.js:33, `on: false` per the GP3a/GP6 default-off policy so the shipped default graph render is pixel-unchanged, `idx: true` for the 100yr monthly-tail fallback at js/ui.js:1529), and the graph checkbox in index.html.

(3) Ordinance plumbing, front-loaded and inert. EXTEND the EXISTING `recycle` row (js/sim.js:611-613 — a Recycling ordinance has shipped since M22; adding a 7th row would double-charge the player and give the environment advisor two champions) with `wasteMul`. recomputeOrdinances folds via an EXPLICIT key list (js/sim.js:4302-4310), so it needs its own line `if (d.wasteMul != null) m.wasteMul *= d.wasteMul;` plus a floor clamp mirroring js/sim.js:4312-4313, and identityOrdMods (js/sim.js:632-634) gains `wasteMul: 1` or a nothing-enacted city gets `undefined` in the arithmetic. wasteMul is consumed by wasteRateAt ONLY — zero sim paths read it — so the ordinance's simulated effect is unchanged.

(4) Garbage minimap mode — FOUR sites, not the one the spec names: index.html:100 (14th `.mm` button; the strip is genuinely 13-mode/two-row today, so 14 makes it exactly 7x2 inside `grid-template-rows: repeat(2,auto)` at css/style.css:220-225), MM_LEGENDS (js/ui.js:741-770), **MM_NAMES (js/ui.js:772-776)** — read unconditionally at js/ui.js:781, so a mode with a legend row but no name row renders the literal string `undefined` — and the renderMinimap mode chain (js/render.js:2254-2345). Ramp follows the GQ11 deutan-safe discipline (lightness monotone).

(5) Power-mix honesty — repairing the ruler GP9b's Σ gate depends on. powerMix (js/sim.js:2528-2541) sums plantEffectiveCap = PRE-trade plant supply, while this.powerSupply is assigned POST-trade at js/sim.js:2382-2383; fillPowerMix (js/ui.js:1064-1102) then labels the mix sum "Total supply". Any open M27 deal makes that displayed number WRONG on today's build, with zero GP9 code. Fix: correct the stale doc comment at js/sim.js:2525-2526 (it still says "four values" over a five-key object); add `City.powerLedger()` -> {mix, plantSupply, tradeIn, tradeOut, supply} where supply === this.powerSupply by construction; fillPowerMix renders trade as its own SIGNED legend row (an export is negative and cannot be a pie slice) and relabels the total to city.powerSupply. Read-only — powerMix and fillPowerMix have no sim consumers.

(6) The crosstalk audit — hoist only, zero semantic change. The eight >= OV.ZR membership tests that a new id joins SILENTLY become named module-scope predicates, each the single source of truth the file already demands at js/sim.js:344-345: ovConducts (js/sim.js:2339-2341), ovDrawsPower (2370-2371), ovBrownoutEligible (2394-2395), ovFlickerEligible (2410-2412), ovFeedsPump (2435), ovFireCandidate (4599-4602), ovIsStructure (SVC_LINEAR js/sim.js:1421-1422, consumed at 4978-4979), ovWireJoins (js/sprites.js:4305 — already resolves isWaterOv/isXp from sim.js module scope). Expose `City.ovCrosstalk(t)` returning all eight booleans for any id. This converts the highest-risk hazard — SVC_LINEAR/deptStrain fire-load, which the original spec omits entirely — from "hope the implementer remembers the site" into a table assertion.

S6 REPORTED, NOT AMENDED: (a) parent gate 3's "powerMix's buckets still sum EXACTLY to powerSupply" is FALSE on the current build with any open regional power-trade deal, independent of GP9 — GP9a makes it true and restates it; (b) parent gate 6's "a city with no waste buildings is byte-identical to the GP8 baseline" cannot coexist with gate 1's zero-disposal overflow requirement — see GP9b's rationale; (c) parent gate 6 names a GP8 baseline that does not exist (ledger certified_through = GP5b, GP6 live-but-uncertified). LAUNCH CONDITION (preflight, non-negotiable): the gate problems recorded in preflight_gate_problems below were found by an adversarial reviewer that read the LIVE source and MEASURED the unchanged build. The design phase MUST resolve every one before implementation, and each resolution must be reported in the ship verdict with its measurement. Rules for resolving: an IMPOSSIBILITY (unachievable/self-contradictory/vacuous — the sim arithmetic or the fixture cannot produce the quantity) is corrected by re-specifying the gate so it measures the intended property with a reachable bar, and the correction is recorded with the measurement proving the original was impossible. An ABSOLUTE-SHOULD-BE-COMPARATIVE bar is restated per the R1 protocol (this build vs baseline on identical scripted inputs). An AMBIGUOUS-THRESHOLD gate is pinned to a named city, seed, sample count and reference quantity. An UNMEASURABLE gate is either given a concrete headless observable or reported to the user as needing a design decision. A resolution that changes what the milestone is TRYING TO ACHIEVE (rather than how it is measured) is a DESIGN decision — surface it to the user, never decide it (S6). Also close every missing_coverage item or justify its omission.
milestones.player_facing_win: Before you can build a single landfill, the city already tells you exactly how much garbage it makes, which zones make it, how that number has moved every month you have played — and the budget's power pie finally adds up to the supply figure on the HUD instead of quietly disagreeing with it whenever a regional deal is open.
quality_gates: BYTE-IDENTICAL SIM (the S3 gate). 20 seeds x 600 ticks, Math.random UNSTUBBED, identical scripted build order, GP9a vs the pinned pre-GP9a commit served on :8902. Measurement: per seed, SHA-256 of the concatenation of over[], lvl[], poll[], crime[], landv[], traffic[], powered[], watered[], jobAccess[], anc[] plus the scalars pop/funds/approval/avgCommute/strandedShare/eduLevel/powerSupply/powerDemand, sampled every 25 ticks. Bar: 0 differing bytes across all 20 seeds x 24 samples, and all TEN pre-existing history series element-identical; history.waste is the only new key.

THE RULER IS HONEST AND MONOTONE. Measurement: city.wasteCensus().total on 5 scripted cities at 0 / 40 / 120 / 300 / 600 developed zone tiles, and on one city held at fixed tile count while its ZR tiles are forced lvl 1 -> 3. Bars: total is strictly monotone non-decreasing across the five (4/4 pairwise), and rises by >= 2.0x under the level sweep. Cross-check bar: Σ over all i of city.wasteRateAt(i) === city.wasteCensus().total EXACTLY (integer equality) — the per-tile number the minimap paints and the citywide number the graph plots can never disagree.

RECYCLING IS MEASURABLE BEFORE IT IS LOAD-BEARING, AND CHANGED NOTHING. Measurement: toggle the shipped `recycle` ordinance OFF then ON on an identical city at the same tick. Bars: (i) wasteCensus().total falls by the designed percentage +/-2% (the exact bar GP9b's saturation/ordinance gate reuses); (ii) across that same toggle, over[], lvl[], poll[], crime[], landv[], traffic[] and pop are byte-identical to the pre-GP9a build's same toggle over 200 ticks — proving that adding wasteMul to the ORDINANCES `recycle` row, to identityOrdMods() and to recomputeOrdinances' fold changed the ordinance's simulated effect by exactly zero.

THE POWER PIE STOPS LYING. Measurement: 6 configurations = trade mode {none, sell, buy} x grid state {surplus, deficit}. Bars: mix.coal+mix.solar+mix.gas+mix.wind+mix.nuke + ledger.tradeIn − ledger.tradeOut === city.powerSupply EXACTLY (integer equality) in all 6/6, and the rendered legend total string equals String(city.powerSupply) + " MW" in all 6/6. S6 finding recorded, not fixed silently: the count of those 6 in which the PRE-GP9a build's displayed total differs from city.powerSupply (expected 4 — every configuration with a live deal).

CROSSTALK AUDIT IS A TRUE MIRROR. Measurement: for every existing overlay id t in 0..33 (34 ids, confirmed contiguous at js/sim.js:274 and OV_NAMES js/ui.js:1682-1695), compare City.ovCrosstalk(t)'s eight booleans against the value the pre-GP9a build's inline expression produced for that id at each of the eight sites. Bar: 34 x 8 = 272 boolean comparisons, 272/272 identical, 0 mismatches. Plus a live probe: powered[], powerDemand, deptStrain().fire.load and the ignition index of 200 startDisaster('fire') calls are all identical to the pre-GP9a build on the same seeded city.

SAVE ROUND-TRIP AT THE NEW LADDER INTEGER. The integer is READ OFF THE TREE at implement time (live is v:17 at js/sim.js:5652, but GP7a/GP7b/GP8a/GP8b all precede GP9 in execution_order and GP7+GP8 both declare touches_save_format — never pin v18 from the spec). Bars: a pre-GP9a save loads with history.waste === [] and 0 console errors; City.deserialize(city.serialize()).serialize() is CHARACTER-IDENTICAL to city.serialize() (idempotent); a loaded city's next 120 rollovers produce a history.waste array element-identical to a natively-run equivalent; and a save whose history.waste holds 250 entries survives load AND is trimmed in lockstep — all ELEVEN history arrays equal length after the next rollover (proving BOTH normaliseHistory copies, js/sim.js:31 and js/sim.js:5274-5276, were extended). No `v ===` equality test introduced anywhere in deserialize.

S4 VISIBILITY OF THE NEW READOUT, ALL 4 ROTATIONS. Measurement: on a city with >= 100 developed zone tiles, capture the minimap canvas at cam.rot 0/1/2/3 in Garbage mode. Bars: the image is non-black and non-uniform (>= 8 distinct pixel values); the four captures are PIXEL-IDENTICAL to each other (the minimap is north-up by contract, js/render.js:2249); the legend caption text starts with exactly "Garbage" and the string "undefined" appears nowhere in #mm-legend.innerHTML (the MM_NAMES omission the spec would have caused); #mapmodes contains exactly 14 `.mm` buttons and #mapmodes.scrollWidth <= #mapmodes.clientWidth (no horizontal overflow at the 160px cap, css/style.css:220-225).

PERF: NO REGRESSION ON EITHER PATH. Measurement: median of 5 runs on a saturated 80x80 city. Bars: 200 x deptStrain() wall time within 5% of the pre-GP9a build's 200 x deptStrain() (the predicate hoist must not cost the fire-load census); 200 x recomputePower() within 5% of baseline (the hoist touches the conducts() flood, the demand scan and both hash-domain cuts); a full 600-tick run within 3% of baseline total wall time. Zero console errors or warnings across the entire suite.
milestones.split_rationale: The read half is emphatically not vacuous here, for four independent reasons. First, the tonnage stream is FULLY derivable from state that already exists (over[] + lvl[] + the shipped recycle ordinance) with zero disposal, zero pollution coupling and zero new over[] ids — so the number GP9b's overflow curve is measured against can be built, plotted and certified while the sim is provably frozen. Second, one of the parent milestone's own rulers is currently broken: fillPowerMix labels the pre-trade plant sum "Total supply" while city.powerSupply is post-trade, so parent gate 3's Σ contract is already false on today's build with any open M27 deal — the behavior half literally cannot be measured with that instrument until it is repaired, which is the exact failure mode S3 exists to prevent. Third, the drift report identifies the SVC_LINEAR/deptStrain fire-load census (js/sim.js:1421-1422 -> 4978-4979) as the highest-risk site and notes the original spec omits it entirely, along with three more of the same class (demand scan, pump feed, wireMask); hoisting all eight into named predicates under a byte-identity gate turns "did we remember every site?" into a 272-assertion table, and a silent citywide fire-coverage collapse into a caught regression. Fourth, all of this is genuinely player-facing — a minimap mode, a query row, a graph series and a budget pie that stops disagreeing with the HUD — so the half is shippable and coherent on its own under S8. Nothing in this half can change behavior: every new consumer is a pure read, wasteMul is read by exactly one pure function, the predicate work is a hoist, and the only serialized addition is an output series.
milestones.save_version_plan: TWO integers, both READ OFF THE TREE at implement time — never pinned from the spec. Live today is `v: 17` (js/sim.js:5652, GP6) and baseline_ledger.current.save_version = 17, but execution_order places GP7a/GP7b/GP8a/GP8b before GP9 and BOTH GP7 and GP8 declare touches_save_format:true, so GP9a realistically lands at v19-v21 and GP9b at that +1. GP9a takes integer N for ONE new key: the `history.waste` series — which requires normaliseHistory's hardcoded key list (js/sim.js:31) AND its mirror in collectBudget's >240 trim loop (js/sim.js:5274-5276) to be extended TOGETHER (both carry explicit SECOND LIST WARNING comments; extending only one silently drops the series on load and drifts it out of month-alignment with the other ten), plus the ctor history literal (js/sim.js:2009) and the push after `approv` (js/sim.js:5267). GP9b takes N+1 for TWO keys: `fill` (per-cell landfill fill, Uint8Array) and `garbageBacklog` (scalar). The spec's 'landfill fill levels are the one new serialized array' is wrong — the backlog is path-dependent STOCK state, the approval/eduLevel precedent at js/sim.js:5641-5650, and derived-and-rebuilt is legal only for pure functions of restored state (the powered[]/svcStrain/megaOk policy). Both halves: all new keys append AFTER every existing key so the prior version's serialized prefix stays character-stable; backward-compatible load rides the existing defensive typeof/Array.isArray guards; NO `v ===` equality test is introduced anywhere in deserialize (there is none today); round-trip must be idempotent (deserialize(serialize()).serialize() character-identical). If a save-neutral read half is preferred, `history.waste` can be deferred to GP9b — but then GP9b's overflow curve has no independently certified series behind it, which is exactly the coupling S3 exists to break, so the recommendation is to keep it in GP9a.
milestones.launch_order_note: Strictly GP9a then GP9b; GP9a itself launches only after GP8b ships, because it claims the next save-ladder integer and both GP7 and GP8 touch the save format. GP9a's baseline for its byte-identity gate is the pinned commit immediately preceding it (git worktree on :8902 per the harness facts) — NOT 'the GP8 baseline' the parent spec names, which does not exist as a certified commit: baseline_ledger.current.certified_through is GP5b, and GP6 is live-in-tree but uncertified at v17 with its own workflow owning the promotion. GP9b's comparison commit is GP9a's SHIP commit, pinned at GP9b launch per R1, and GP9b must not start until GP9a is independently certified — its gates 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 all consume GP9a's instrumentation (history.waste, wasteCensus/wasteRateAt, powerLedger, ovCrosstalk), so an uncertified read half would leave the behavior half measuring itself with a ruler nobody checked, which is precisely the failure S3 was written to stop. Two scope decisions are made in the split and should be confirmed before GP9b implementation rather than discovered in it: the incinerator does NOT join isPlant() and instead takes a sixth powerMix bucket with its own upkeep and its MW injected BEFORE powerTradeDelta (so it is exportable); and landfill is EXCLUDED from fire candidacy while the incinerator is INCLUDED. Three gates of the parent milestone are reported under S6 and need a user decision, not a worker amendment: parent gate 3's Σ === powerSupply (already false on the current build under any open M27 trade deal), parent gate 6's byte-identity-vs-overflow contradiction (restated in GP9b as the WASTE_RATE-zero attribution gate), and parent gate 6's non-existent GP8 baseline.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 7 (S4 VISIBILITY): "#mapmodes.scrollWidth <= #mapmodes.clientWidth (no horizontal overflow at the 160px cap, css/style.css:220-225)"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: MEASURED FALSE ON THE PRE-GP9a BUILD, with zero GP9 code. I served the repo on :8901 and read the live box: #mapmodes has 13 .mm buttons, gridTemplateColumns resolves to "34px 34px 34px 34px 34px 34px 34px" (7 tracks), scrollWidth = 244, clientWidth = 160. The strip ALREADY overflows by 84px. It is designed to: css/style.css:220-225 sets grid-auto-columns: minmax(34px,1fr) with a hard width:160px and overflow-x:auto, and the shipped comment on that rule says in terms "width: 160px; /* hard cap = minimap width: the strip scrolls, never grows */". The gate demands the opposite of the shipped design contract, and no correct GP9a implementation can satisfy it — this is incident #1 repeating exactly (an absolute bar the baseline already fails, unrelated to the work).
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Replace with the comparative form that actually expresses the intent (the 14th button must fill the existing 7th column's empty second-row cell rather than open an 8th column): "#mapmodes contains exactly 14 .mm buttons; #mapmodes.scrollWidth is UNCHANGED from the pre-GP9a build (measured 244 today) and #mapmodes.offsetHeight is unchanged (still exactly two rows); getComputedStyle(#mapmodes).gridTemplateColumns still resolves to 7 tracks."

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 7 (S4 VISIBILITY): "the four captures are PIXEL-IDENTICAL to each other (the minimap is north-up by contract, js/render.js:2249)"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: MEASURED FALSE ON THE PRE-GP9a BUILD at every non-degenerate camera position. renderMinimap paints the tiles north-up, but then strokes a camera-viewport rectangle over the same canvas (js/render.js:2362-2381) whose bounds come from screenToTileF at the four screen corners — and the shipped comment there says explicitly "route the four screen corners through the rotation-aware FLOAT inverse ... so the box bounds the ROTATED visible region in tile space at every rotation". I hashed the full 160x160 minimap ImageData at cam.r 0/1/2/3 on four camera configs (z=1 centred, z=2 at 20,20, z=2 at 60,15, z=4 centred): all four configs produced FOUR DIFFERENT hashes. (The bar passes only at a degenerate clamped camera — cam.x=0, cam.y=1280 — which is why it looks plausible.) The cited authority, js/render.js:2249, is the `dist`-mode comment "stays north-up like every other minimap mode", which covers the TILE PAINT only and says nothing about the overlay stroke the gate's measurement includes. This is incident #2's shape: the gate's own justification does not cover the quantity it measures, and the implementer would burn a full cycle proving the gate wrong.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Measure the tile paint, not the whole canvas: "the four captures are PIXEL-IDENTICAL to each other after masking the camera-viewport stroke (compare ImageData with pure-white #ffffff pixels excluded), OR capture with the camera pinned to a fully-zoomed-out, map-clamped position where the projected box is rotation-invariant by construction — state which, and pin cam.x/cam.y/cam.z in the harness."

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 1: "history.waste (the series GP9a certified) is non-decreasing over all 24 [rollovers]" — in the ZERO-DISPOSAL arm
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The same gate requires this arm to be poisoned by its own garbage (rising pollution) while simultaneously requiring its waste OUTPUT never to dip — but waste output is a pure function of over[]/lvl[], and the sim de-levels developed tiles under exactly the conditions this gate is trying to induce. The decline paths: applyDecline at js/sim.js:1121-1123 (`c.lvl[i]--` on a demand-driven draw), the UNPOWERED decay at 1135, and the gridlock decay at 4464 (`if (this.lvl[i] > 1 && gCong(...) > 0.8 ...) this.lvl[i]--`). Rising poll[] drives landv[] down (js/sim.js:3731, `- this.poll[i] * 0.7`), which drives gFit down, which drives demand down, which drives applyDecline. Over 24 rollovers a genuinely overflowing city can lose levels and its tonnage can fall — the gate then fails BECAUSE the feature worked. Monotonicity of the stock (garbageBacklog) is safe; monotonicity of the flow (history.waste) is not.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Keep the strictly-increasing backlog bar (that one is sound — with zero disposal the stock only accumulates) and restate the flow bar comparatively and with slack: "history.waste at rollover 24 is >= its value at rollover 1, and the zero-disposal arm's history.waste is element-wise >= the drained control's at every rollover" — or drop it entirely, since garbageBacklog strictly increasing already proves the stream is live.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 5 (CROSSTALK AUDIT IS A TRUE MIRROR): "34 x 8 = 272 boolean comparisons, 272/272 identical, 0 mismatches"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Seven of the eight hoisted predicates are pure functions of the overlay byte and mirror cleanly. The eighth, ovIsStructure, is NOT — so for 4 of the 34 ids the "value the pre-GP9a build's inline expression produced for that id" does not exist, and the gate cannot be evaluated. At the census (js/sim.js:4966-4981) the control flow is: `if (t === OV.NONE) continue;` (NONE is not a structure, but NONE is not in SVC_LINEAR, so the natural hoist `!SVC_LINEAR.has(t)` returns TRUE for it — a guaranteed mismatch); then `if (t === OV.ZR || t === OV.ZC || t === OV.ZI) { const l = this.lvl[i]; if (!l) continue; structures++; }` — for the three zone ids the site's answer depends on lvl[i], not on t, so there is no single boolean to compare against. 4 of the 272 cells are ill-defined and will read as failures on a correct hoist.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Either carve the ambiguity out explicitly — "ovIsStructure(t) is defined as `t !== OV.NONE && !SVC_LINEAR.has(t)`, and the comparison is run over the 30 NON-ZONE ids only (30 x 8 = 240 assertions); the three zone ids' structure membership is lvl-dependent and is asserted separately as `lvl > 0` at both a lvl-0 and a lvl-2 tile" — or split the site into ovIsStructure(t) for non-zone ids plus an explicit ovZoneIsStructure(t, lvl). Restate the total (240 + 6, or whatever the split yields) so the arithmetic in the bar matches the assertions actually run.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 4 (THE POWER PIE STOPS LYING), the S6 finding: "the count of those 6 in which the PRE-GP9a build's displayed total differs from city.powerSupply (expected 4 — every configuration with a live deal)"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The expected count is 3, not 4, and the reasoning behind "every configuration with a live deal" is wrong for one cell of the matrix. powerTradeDelta (js/sim.js:4373-4384) computes `const sold = Math.min(sellCommit, Math.max(0, plantSupply - demand)); return buys - sold;`. In the sell x DEFICIT configuration, plantSupply < demand by definition, so `Math.max(0, plantSupply - demand)` is 0, sold is 0, buys is 0, and the delta is EXACTLY 0 — powerSupply equals the plant sum and the pre-GP9a displayed total does NOT differ. Only sell x surplus, buy x surplus and buy x deficit produce a nonzero delta. A worker who dutifully records "3" against a gate that says "expected 4" is forced either to escalate or to quietly amend the bar.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: "...the count of those 6 in which the PRE-GP9a build's displayed total differs from city.powerSupply (expected 3: sell x surplus, buy x surplus, buy x deficit — sell x deficit is provably delta-0 because powerTradeDelta caps sold at max(0, plantSupply - demand), js/sim.js:4381)." Note the 6/6 exact-equality bars themselves are sound: the Math.max(0, ...) clamp at js/sim.js:2382 is unreachable, since sold <= plantSupply always.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 8 (PERF: NO REGRESSION ON EITHER PATH): "200 x deptStrain() within 5% ... 200 x recomputePower() within 5% ... a full 600-tick run within 3%", median of 5 runs
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The tolerances are tighter than the instrument. I measured the noise floor on a saturated 76x76 city in the harness Chromium: 200 x deptStrain() = 5.2 ms median, raw runs 4.9 / 5.0 / 5.1 / 5.1 / 5.2 / 5.2 / 5.2 / 5.6 / 5.8 — an 17.3% spread and ±9% around the median. 200 x recomputePower() = 8.9 ms median, raw runs 8.9 ... 12.0 — a 34.8% spread. Both timed blocks are single-digit milliseconds, so timer granularity and JIT tiering dominate; a median-of-5 does not shrink that to 5%. The 3% bar on a full 600-tick run is worse, because it compares across two separate browser contexts against two separate servers (:8901 vs :8902). This gate will pass or fail on scheduler luck, which is exactly the state that invites a worker to re-run until it passes.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Size each timed block above the noise floor and widen the tolerance to something the instrument can resolve: "20,000 x deptStrain() and 5,000 x recomputePower() (each block >= 200 ms), median of 9 runs, within 10% of baseline; a full 600-tick run, median of 9, within 8%." Better still, add a noise-floor control: run the SAME build against itself first and require the observed self-vs-self spread to be below the tolerance before the cross-build comparison is admitted as evidence.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 6 (SAVE ROUND-TRIP): "a save whose history.waste holds 250 entries survives load AND is trimmed in lockstep — all ELEVEN history arrays equal length after the next rollover"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: As written the fixture cannot produce the measured quantity. The trim (js/sim.js:5273-5276) is `if (this.history.pop.length > 240) for (const k of [...]) this.history[k].shift();` — a single shift per rollover, guarded on POP's length, not on each key's. A save in which only history.waste holds 250 entries loads with pop at whatever the other ten hold; if that is <= 240 the guard never fires, nothing is trimmed, and waste stays at 250+1 while the others sit at N+1 — the eleven are unequal on a perfectly correct implementation. Even with all eleven at 250, one rollover pushes one and shifts one, so they end at 250 each, equal but not "trimmed" to 240. The bar's intent (both key lists were extended) is right; its fixture and its success condition are not.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the fixture and split the two claims: "(a) a save in which ALL ELEVEN history arrays hold 250 entries loads, and after the next rollover all eleven are still equal in length and all eleven shrank by exactly the same amount — proving the collectBudget trim list at js/sim.js:5274-5276 was extended; (b) a save whose history object contains a `waste` key loads with that key preserved and non-empty — proving normaliseHistory's list at js/sim.js:31 was extended (an unextended list silently drops it to [])."

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 3(i) and GP9b gate 5: "toggling `recycle` cuts wasteCensus().total by the DESIGNED PERCENTAGE +/-2%"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: "The designed percentage" is not a number in the spec — it is whatever value the implementer assigns to the recycle row's wasteMul at implement time. The bar therefore cannot fail in its design dimension: an implementer who picks wasteMul 0.95 passes the gate exactly as easily as one who picks 0.70, and the gate certifies nothing about whether Recycling is a meaningful player choice. The ±2% slop is doing real work (it catches per-tile vs total rounding drift in the fold at js/sim.js:4302-4313), but the percentage itself is self-referential.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Pin the constant in the spec before launch so the bar is falsifiable: "the recycle row carries wasteMul: 0.75; toggling it cuts wasteCensus().total by 25% +/-2%." S6 note: the constant is a tuning knob and may be re-argued at launch, but it must be a NUMBER in the gate, not a forward reference to the implementation.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 7 (S4 VISIBILITY): "the image is non-black and non-uniform (>= 8 distinct pixel values)"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: WASTE_RATE is declared as a FROZEN per-zone-type x per-level table (3 types x 3 levels = 9 possible non-zero rates), and the minimap is declared to paint wasteRateAt(i) per tile directly. The number of distinct colours the canvas can carry is therefore bounded by the number of distinct (type, level) pairs actually PRESENT in the fixture, plus the background/water/dim-context colours and the white viewport stroke. A city with ">= 100 developed zone tiles" — the only fixture condition the gate states — will typically be mostly lvl 1-2 residential with some commercial and light industry, i.e. 3-5 distinct rates. 3 rates + background + water + white stroke = 6 distinct values on a completely correct build. The bar assumes a continuous ramp over a plane; it is being applied to a 9-valued lookup.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Tie the threshold to the fixture instead of guessing at it: "the count of distinct non-background pixel values equals the count of distinct (zone type, level) pairs present in the fixture, and that count is >= 4 — pin the fixture to contain at least ZR lvl 1, ZR lvl 3, ZC lvl 2 and ZI lvl 2 so the bar has something to count." Keep the non-black / non-uniform bars as-is.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 2 (THE RULER IS HONEST AND MONOTONE): "total is strictly monotone non-decreasing across the five (4/4 pairwise)"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Two issues. First, "strictly monotone non-decreasing" is internally contradictory — strict monotonicity and non-decreasing are different predicates and the gate does not say which is being asserted. Second, whichever is meant, the bar cannot fail on any correct implementation: WASTE_RATE is a frozen table of non-negative rates, wasteCensus is a plain sum over tiles, and the five cities are a nested sequence (0 / 40 / 120 / 300 / 600 developed tiles from the same script). More tiles of non-negative rate means more total, by construction. It certifies nothing the Sigma cross-check bar in the same gate does not already certify. The level-sweep bar (>= 2.0x) in the same gate IS real — it constrains the table's shape — and should be kept.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Either drop the monotonicity bar as vacuous, or replace it with something that constrains the design: "total per developed tile stays within a 3x band across the five cities (the ruler must not be dominated by one zone type), AND the ind:res ratio of wasteCensus() exceeds 1.5 at every one of the five (industry heaviest, per the M31 design the scope cites)." Also fix the wording to a single predicate.

preflight_missing_coverage: S4 VISIBILITY — the garbage GRAPH SERIES is ungated. GP9a ships history.waste plus a UI.graphSeries entry (js/ui.js:33) plus a checkbox in index.html, and GP9b gate 1 measures its whole overflow curve against that series, but NO gate opens the graph dialog, ticks the checkbox and asserts a plotted line appears. Gate 7 covers only the minimap and gate 4 only the pie. Because the series ships `on: false` per the GP3a/GP6 default-off policy, a broken checkbox wiring or a missing seriesData path (js/ui.js:1522-1534) is invisible to every gate in the split — the exact 'nothing invisible ever bills the player' failure S4 exists to catch. Suggested bar: with the checkbox ticked at all three graph ranges (1yr/10yr/100yr), the garbage line renders non-empty and its final plotted value equals the last element of city.history.waste.

S4 VISIBILITY — the PER-TILE garbage readout in the query panel is ungated and arguably undelivered. GP9a's rationale claims 'a query row' as one of four player-facing wins, but the six numbered deliverables in scope do not include a query-panel waste row, and no gate asserts one. GP9b gate 5 asserts only the literal string 'full' for a saturated landfill cell. If the minimap is the sole per-tile expression, wasteRateAt has no numeric surface anywhere.

GP9b's new COMPLAINT kind `garbage` has NO gate of any kind — not that it fires, not its text, not the tile it targets, and not the scope's own claim that 'it changes which x,y the ticker jumps to ONLY in cities carrying a backlog'. This matters concretely: the declared score is `40 + backlogPressure` where backlogPressure is a CITYWIDE scalar, so every tile scores identically, and scanComplaints picks the winner with a strict `score > bestScore` (js/sim.js:5328) — meaning the garbage complaint always resolves to the LOWEST map index that qualifies, and the ticker's 'Show me' camera jump lands on the same corner tile every single time. Nothing in the split would detect that. Suggested bars: the complaint fires within COMPLAINT_EVERY*2 rollovers of the backlog crossing its threshold; its (x,y) is a landfill/high-waste tile rather than index 0; and on a zero-backlog city the complaint kind and target are byte-identical to the GP9a build's.

GP9b's ADVISORY_GATES WASTE_OVERFLOW row is ungated. The scope adds it 'so diagnoseTile explains the stall', which is the GP1a substrate contract, but no bar asserts city.diagnoseTile(i) actually emits the row on a stalled tile in a backlogged city, nor that it stays absent on a clean one. Draw-neutrality is covered (gate 8(ii)); presence and correctness are not.

The REPAIRED POWER PIE has no rendering gate. GP9a gate 4 checks the legend TOTAL string only. Nothing asserts the new SIGNED trade row renders correctly when the value is negative (an export), that fillPowerMix's arc loop at js/ui.js:1080-1085 does not emit a negative or NaN sweep when a trade row is folded in, or that the pie still draws when total <= 0. GP9b adds a SIXTH `waste` slice with the same gap — gate 4 checks mix.waste numerically but nothing checks the slice renders or that POWERMIX_TYPES was extended (the scope itself warns 'omit the row and the pie silently under-sums').

GP9b gate 5 measures with `city.wasteCapacity()`, an instrument that neither half's scope declares or ships. Under S3 the behavior half must be measured by instruments the read half certified; wasteCapacity() cannot live in GP9a (fill[] does not exist yet), so it must at minimum be named as a GP9b deliverable with its own definition, or the gate is measuring with a ruler that appears for the first time inside the gate that uses it.

GP9b gate 8(ii)'s attribution claim overreaches, and the residue is ungated. With WASTE_RATE zeroed and a GP9a-era scripted build order (which by definition cannot place a landfill or incinerator — those tools do not exist in GP9a), the two new over[] ids never appear in over[], so the eight predicate edits, the five tool registries (COST/TOOL_TIER/OV_SIZE/toolOverlay/TOOLS), the budget line and the complaint kind are NEVER EXERCISED by that run. Byte-identity therefore cannot 'prove' they contribute no drift — it proves only that dormant code is dormant. Gate 3 part 2's live probes do cover the eight predicates with a real landfill field; the tool registries, the deptCosts/collectBudget/lastBudget-ctor budget line and the complaint kind have no equivalent probe. Suggested addition: a WASTE_RATE-zeroed run that DOES place landfills and an incinerator, byte-identical to itself across load/save and asserting funds delta equals exactly the placement cost plus upkeep.

No save-compat bar covers the GP9a ordinance plumbing on a LEGACY save. GP9a adds `wasteMul: 1` to identityOrdMods (js/sim.js:632-634) and a fold line to recomputeOrdinances (4302-4310). A pre-GP9a save with `recycle` already enacted must reload with ordMods.wasteMul defined rather than undefined — recomputeOrdinances is documented as running on load, so this is probably safe, but gate 6 asserts nothing about ordMods at all. One bar: 'a pre-GP9a save with recycle enacted loads with typeof city.ordMods.wasteMul === "number" and wasteCensus().total finite and non-NaN.'

GP9b determinism gate 8(i) reproduces history.waste, garbageBacklog and history.poll across 20 seeds but omits fill[] — the other new serialized array. Gate 7 compares fill[] on a load-vs-native run, but the 20-seed determinism sweep does not, so a seed-dependent divergence in landfill fill ordering would only be caught if it happened to perturb the backlog.
milestones.split_of: GP9 (preflight-authored S3 split, grounded against the live source 2026-07-30)

milestones.title: Somewhere To Put It — landfill, waste-to-energy incinerator, overflow (behavior, re-pinned against GP9a)
milestones.scope:
Ships the two disposal routes and the overflow consequence, measured throughout by GP9a's certified instrumentation.

IDS + PREDICATE. OV.LANDFILL / OV.INCIN take the next two free ids (34/35 today — READ OFF THE TREE, GP7/GP8 may have consumed ids), appended never renumbered; over[] is a Uint8Array serialized via plain Array.from at js/sim.js:5668, so they round-trip with no loader change. `isWaste(t)` goes in the documented family slot at js/sim.js:353-358 — immediately after isMega, before the GP2 isPort block — carrying the doctrine comment the family states at js/sim.js:344-345.

ONE LINE AT EACH OF GP9a's EIGHT HOISTED PREDICATES, with the membership DECLARED per id, not inherited by accident: conducts (js/sim.js:2339-2341) excludes both — a paint-style landfill sprayed over hundreds of tiles would otherwise bridge wires the player never laid; demand (2370-2371) excludes both — landfill is not a consumer, the incinerator is a generator; brownout (2394-2395) and y2k (2410-2412) exclude both — a landfill has no systems to flicker, and both cuts are hash-domain walks over i, so widening the eligible set would change WHICH tiles a given cutRatio lands on; pump-feed (2435) excludes both — the GP4a !isXp symmetry; fire candidacy (4599-4602) EXCLUDES landfill and INCLUDES the incinerator — `cand[rh.pick(cand.length)]` uses the array LENGTH as the RNG argument, so hundreds of landfill tiles would both swamp the candidate array and re-pin every fire location on every seed; SVC_LINEAR (js/sim.js:1421-1422) GAINS OV.LANDFILL and NOT OV.INCIN — the spec-omitted highest-risk site, where every non-SVC_LINEAR overlay increments `structures` at js/sim.js:4978-4979, which IS deptStrain's fire `load`, which drives svcStrain.fire, which multiplies stampCoverage potency for EVERY fire station citywide (GP5b substrate); wireMask (js/sprites.js:4305) excludes both, or drawn wires autotile into tiles carrying no current (S4 violation — art contradicting sim).

NAMES. OV_NAMES (js/ui.js:1682-1695) gains two entries at 34/35, and BOTH consumers must resolve: the query panel (js/ui.js:1746) and the hover memo (js/ui.js:2231) — the spec names only one.

TOOLS, FIVE REGISTRIES. `landfill` 1x1 drag-paint (the PIPE precedent) and `incin` 2x2 anchor (the PUMP precedent at OV_SIZE js/sim.js:296, which also proves the 2x2 anchor + power-receiver pattern): COST (js/sim.js:523-540), TOOL_TIER (578-584, gated — nuke:4 / airport:3 precedent), OV_SIZE (292-304), toolOverlay (5993-6015), TOOLS (js/ui.js:62-130), sprites in js/sprites.js.

SERIALIZED STATE — TWO ITEMS, NOT ONE. `fill` (per-cell landfill fill, Uint8Array) AND `garbageBacklog` (the uncollected-garbage scalar). The spec's "the one new serialized array" understates it: the backlog is PATH-DEPENDENT STOCK state, exactly the approval/eduLevel precedent at js/sim.js:5641-5650; derived-and-rebuilt is legal only for pure functions of restored state (the powered[]/svcStrain/megaOk policy). Both keys append AFTER every existing key so GP9a's prefix stays character-stable (ladder rule, js/sim.js:5615-5651). Next ladder integer, read off the tree.

MONTHLY WASTE TICK at the rollover: GP9a's wasteCensus().total -> incinerator fixed tonnage first, then landfill cells in ascending index order (deterministic, RNG-free), saturating per cell; remainder accrues into garbageBacklog.

POLLUTION at js/sim.js:3663-3681: a saturated cell's persistent emission (it keeps stinking after it is full) plus a backlog-scaled citywide source, both behind a `const wasteAny = this._wasteAny` hoist mirroring the shipped `noisy` fast-path at js/sim.js:3728, so a waste-free city pays no per-tile compare for a term that is identically 0. DO NOT scale by `pm` (ordMods.pollMul, js/sim.js:3662): that already discounts curbside industry/road pollution when Recycling is on, and routing garbage pollution through it too would let one ordinance discount the same smog twice. Recycling's effect on garbage is already carried by GP9a's wasteMul on the stream.

LAND VALUE at js/sim.js:3730-3741: the landfill scar plus the backlog penalty, behind the same wasteAny hoist (the GP2 targeted-penalty precedent at js/sim.js:3738-3739).

INCINERATOR MW — the COLLISION 2 decision, made in scope. It does NOT join isPlant(), which would drag in plantYear stamping (js/sim.js:2276), the aging curve (2517-2522), PLANT_WARN_AGE nagging (2550-2562) + the INFRA_GATES PLANT_AGING row (1298-1303), and the flat `plants * 40` upkeep (4936). Instead: a SIXTH `waste` bucket in powerMix (js/sim.js:2528-2541) plus a sixth POWERMIX_TYPES row (js/ui.js:1057-1063) — omit the row and the pie silently under-sums. The MW is summed into `supply` BEFORE the powerTradeDelta(supply, demand) call at js/sim.js:2382, so incinerator power is indistinguishable from plant generation on the grid and IS exportable through the M27 sell cap min(sellCommit, max(0, plantSupply − demand)) at js/sim.js:4381. Upkeep rides the new waste budget line, never plants*40.

BUDGET LINE, FOUR COORDINATED SITES: deptCosts scan + return object (js/sim.js:4902-4944), collectBudget net + lastBudget (5240-5253), the lastBudget CTOR shape (js/sim.js:2011-2015 — fillBudgetTable reads city.lastBudget before the first rollover on a fresh city), and fillBudgetTable rows (js/ui.js:1133-1150).

COMPLAINT KIND `garbage`: COMPLAINT_T (js/sim.js:763), COMPLAINT_TEXT (777-783), scanComplaints (5316-5333). The scoring chain is ORDER-SENSITIVE — rubble(130)/traffic/unpowered(150) are an else-if ladder followed by two unconditional overrides (crime, poll). Declared placement: garbage is a THIRD unconditional override after poll, scored 40 + backlogPressure, so it wins only when the backlog genuinely dominates; it changes which x,y the ticker jumps to ONLY in cities carrying a backlog. The name draw is a stateless HZ.FX_NAME hash on tickCount (5339-5341), so it cannot re-pin the sim.

TRUCK TRAFFIC (S4 / launch_note). `load[]` is not a plane and not addressable from outside recomputeTraffic — it is this._trafficLoad, a lazily-allocated scratch Float32Array (js/sim.js:2955) never serialized. The exact shipped precedent is spreadPortTrips(load, gate, trips) at js/sim.js:4097-4125: a deterministic, RNG-FREE, token-stamped BFS deposit taking `load` as a PARAMETER from recomputeTraffic. Ship spreadWasteTrips on that identical shape. This IS a re-pin (load -> traffic at js/sim.js:3305/3314 -> landv -> gFit -> growth draws) and is declared as such; it is covered by the WASTE_RATE-zero attribution gate below.

GATE TABLES: NO new GROWTH_GATES row (that shifts draws and would need its own declared re-pin under the GP1a substrate rule) — garbage acts through poll[]/landv[], which already feed gFit. ADD one ADVISORY_GATES row, WASTE_OVERFLOW, which is draw-neutral (walked only by _attachAdvisories, js/sim.js:4514) so diagnoseTile explains the stall. LAUNCH CONDITION (preflight, non-negotiable): the gate problems recorded in preflight_gate_problems below were found by an adversarial reviewer that read the LIVE source and MEASURED the unchanged build. The design phase MUST resolve every one before implementation, and each resolution must be reported in the ship verdict with its measurement. Rules for resolving: an IMPOSSIBILITY (unachievable/self-contradictory/vacuous — the sim arithmetic or the fixture cannot produce the quantity) is corrected by re-specifying the gate so it measures the intended property with a reachable bar, and the correction is recorded with the measurement proving the original was impossible. An ABSOLUTE-SHOULD-BE-COMPARATIVE bar is restated per the R1 protocol (this build vs baseline on identical scripted inputs). An AMBIGUOUS-THRESHOLD gate is pinned to a named city, seed, sample count and reference quantity. An UNMEASURABLE gate is either given a concrete headless observable or reported to the user as needing a design decision. A resolution that changes what the milestone is TRYING TO ACHIEVE (rather than how it is measured) is a DESIGN decision — surface it to the user, never decide it (S6). Also close every missing_coverage item or justify its omission.
milestones.player_facing_win: Growth now produces something you must physically put somewhere — cheap landfill that poisons the ground it sits on and keeps stinking after it is full, or an expensive incinerator that turns the problem into a trickle of sellable power and a cloud over its own neighbourhood — and ignoring both fills the city with faxes and smog you can watch climbing on the garbage graph GP9a shipped.
quality_gates: STREAM -> OVERFLOW, MEASURED BY THE GP9a RULER, AGAINST A CONTROL. Measurement: one 300-developed-zone city with ZERO disposal vs a control identical in every way except its backlog is drained each month, 24 rollovers, same seed and script. Bars: history.waste (the series GP9a certified) is non-decreasing over all 24; city.garbageBacklog strictly increases at every one of the 24 rollovers; city.cityIndex(city.poll) rises by >= 20 from tick 0 while the control's drifts by < 3.

THE TWO ROUTES GENUINELY DIFFER. Measurement: three arms, same seed, same script, 120 rollovers — (A) no disposal, (B) landfill sized to zero the backlog, (C) incinerator of equal rated tonnage. Bars: B and C both hold garbageBacklog === 0 for the final 24 rollovers; mean landv over the ring within 4 tiles of a saturated landfill cell in B is >= 20 LOWER than the same ring in C; that same ring in C is < 5 lower than in a no-waste control; mean city.poll within 3 tiles of the incinerator in C is >= 25 HIGHER than over the same footprint in B; and city.powerSupply in C exceeds A by EXACTLY the incinerator's rated MW (integer equality).

ANTI-CROSSTALK AUDIT — EVERY SITE ASSERTED INDIVIDUALLY VIA GP9a's ovCrosstalk(). Measurement, part 1: for t = OV.LANDFILL and t = OV.INCIN separately, compare all eight memberships against the declared design table — conducts (js/sim.js:2339-2341), demand (2370-2371), brownout (2394-2395), y2k (2410-2412), pump-feed (2435), fire candidacy (4599-4602), SVC_LINEAR structure census (1421-1422 / 4978-4979), wireMask (js/sprites.js:4305). Bar: 16/16 individual boolean assertions match. Part 2, live probes on a 400-tile (20x20) landfill field laid between two disconnected wire runs. Bars: (i) city.powered[] is byte-identical to the same city with the field absent (0 bridged tiles); (ii) city.powerDemand rises by EXACTLY 0; (iii) city.deptStrain().fire.load rises by EXACTLY 0 and city.svcStrain.fire changes by EXACTLY 0 — the spec-omitted site whose failure mode is a silent citywide fire-coverage collapse; (iv) over 200 startDisaster('fire') calls, ZERO ignitions land on a landfill tile AND the 200-element ignition index sequence is IDENTICAL to the same 200 calls with the landfill absent; (v) both ids resolve to a non-empty name in OV_NAMES at BOTH consumers (query panel js/ui.js:1746 and hover memo js/ui.js:2231) — the string "undefined" appears in neither.

Σ CONTRACT, RESTATED AGAINST THE INVARIANT GP9a MADE TRUE (the parent's gate 3 as written is false on the current build — see rationale). Measurement: with an incinerator on the grid, the same 6 trade configurations GP9a gated. Bars: mix.coal+solar+gas+wind+nuke+waste + ledger.tradeIn − ledger.tradeOut === city.powerSupply EXACTLY in 6/6; mix.waste equals the summed rated MW of powered incinerator anchors EXACTLY; with a sell deal open on a city whose ONLY generation is incinerators, city._tradeSold > 0 (proving the MW is injected before powerTradeDelta at js/sim.js:2382 and is genuinely exportable). Isolation bars: placing an incinerator leaves city.deptCosts().plants UNCHANGED and city.plantYear at its anchor === 0 (it is provably outside isPlant), and no PLANT_WARN_AGE message is ever emitted for it over 60 game years.

SATURATION + ORDINANCE. Measurement: a landfill cell driven to max fill, then 24 further rollovers. Bars: its fill byte is constant across all 24 and citywide accepted tonnage attributable to it is 0; city.wasteCapacity() equals EXACTLY the summed remaining capacity over unsaturated cells (integer equality); the query panel row for that cell contains the literal string "full"; and toggling `recycle` cuts wasteCensus().total by the designed percentage +/-2% (the identical bar GP9a already certified) while posting a NON-ZERO §/mo in the ordinance row and a non-zero waste line in fillBudgetTable.

S4 SIM-ART COHERENCE AT ALL 4 ROTATIONS, FAILURE DISTINCT FROM WORKING. Measurement: rendered main-view tile bounding boxes captured at cam.rot 0/1/2/3. Bars: empty / half-full / saturated landfill cells are mutually distinct — pixel-diff > 5% for all 3 pairs at all 4 rotations (12/12); a powered incinerator (plume + lit) vs an unpowered idle one is > 5% distinct at all 4 rotations (4/4); the incinerator plume centroid sits within 4 px of its anchor's screen position at all 4 rotations (the shipped lesson: a noise cone perpendicular to the drawn runway); truck load is visible as non-zero city.traffic[] on the road tiles serving a landfill (>= 1 tile above its no-waste value). Zero console errors.

SAVE-COMPAT AT THE NEXT LADDER INTEGER (read off the tree, not pinned from the spec). Bars: a GP9a save loads with fill[] all-zero, garbageBacklog === 0, and NO retroactive overflow penalty — its landv[] and poll[] after one recomputeMaps are element-identical to the GP9a build's; City.deserialize(serialize()).serialize() is CHARACTER-IDENTICAL to serialize() on a city with a half-filled landfill field AND a non-zero backlog (idempotent round-trip); a loaded city's next 120 rollovers match a native equivalent BYTE-FOR-BYTE over over[], lvl[], poll[], landv[], fill[], garbageBacklog and all 11 history series; and no `v ===` equality test exists anywhere in deserialize.

DETERMINISM + A FULLY ATTRIBUTED, BOUNDED RE-PIN + COMPARATIVE SCENARIOS. Bars: (i) same seed + same script reproduces identical history.waste, garbageBacklog and history.poll series over 600 ticks with Math.random UNSTUBBED, across 20 seeds — 0 differing values; (ii) ATTRIBUTION — with WASTE_RATE set to all zeros (a one-table knob), a 20-seed x 600-tick run is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the GP9a baseline across over[], lvl[], poll[], crime[], landv[], traffic[], pop and funds (0 differing bytes), proving every byte of drift comes from the waste stream itself and none from the two new ids, the eight predicate edits, the tool registries, the budget line, the complaint kind or the truck deposit; (iii) R1 COMPARATIVE — all 5 scenarios in js/scenarios.js (gridlock-97, twister-season, blackout-summer-97, y2k-ready, +1) run on THIS build vs the pinned GP9a SHIP commit on IDENTICAL scripted solutions, and the 5-element pass/fail vector is identical or strictly better — no scenario the baseline script wins may be lost. Never an absolute wins-N-of-10 bar.
milestones.split_rationale: Every claim this half makes is now measured by an instrument the read half already proved honest under a byte-identity gate: the tonnage series, the per-tile rate, the recycling percentage, the Σ ledger and the eight-site crosstalk table all shipped and were certified while the sim was frozen. That is what lets gate 3 assert sixteen individual memberships instead of hand-probing five idioms the original spec mislocated, and what lets gate 4 state a Σ contract that is actually true. Two of the parent milestone's gates are reported as MIS-SPECIFIED under S6 rather than amended to fit: parent gate 3's Σ === powerSupply fails on today's build with any open M27 power-trade deal, with zero GP9 code, because powerMix sums pre-trade plant capacity while powerSupply is assigned post-trade — GP9a repairs the instrument and this half restates the gate against the repaired invariant; and parent gate 6's 'a city with no waste buildings is byte-identical to the GP8 baseline' is mutually exclusive with parent gate 1's 'a city with zero disposal accumulates overflow', because no-waste-buildings IS zero-disposal, and the overflow feeds a pollution source whose poll[] feeds landv[] feeds gFit feeds the growth draws. Byte-identity is unrecoverable unless the whole stream sits behind an opt-in the scope does not describe. The attainable and strictly stronger form is shipped as gate 8(ii): with WASTE_RATE zeroed, the build is byte-identical to the GP9a baseline over 20 seeds x 600 ticks — which proves every byte of divergence is attributable to the waste stream and none to the plumbing, and is only possible because the plumbing landed in a separately certified half. Parent gate 6 also names a GP8 baseline that does not exist (the ledger's certified_through is GP5b, GP6 is live-but-uncertified); the comparison commit is GP9a's SHIP commit, pinned at launch per R1.
milestones.save_version_plan: TWO integers, both READ OFF THE TREE at implement time — never pinned from the spec. Live today is `v: 17` (js/sim.js:5652, GP6) and baseline_ledger.current.save_version = 17, but execution_order places GP7a/GP7b/GP8a/GP8b before GP9 and BOTH GP7 and GP8 declare touches_save_format:true, so GP9a realistically lands at v19-v21 and GP9b at that +1. GP9a takes integer N for ONE new key: the `history.waste` series — which requires normaliseHistory's hardcoded key list (js/sim.js:31) AND its mirror in collectBudget's >240 trim loop (js/sim.js:5274-5276) to be extended TOGETHER (both carry explicit SECOND LIST WARNING comments; extending only one silently drops the series on load and drifts it out of month-alignment with the other ten), plus the ctor history literal (js/sim.js:2009) and the push after `approv` (js/sim.js:5267). GP9b takes N+1 for TWO keys: `fill` (per-cell landfill fill, Uint8Array) and `garbageBacklog` (scalar). The spec's 'landfill fill levels are the one new serialized array' is wrong — the backlog is path-dependent STOCK state, the approval/eduLevel precedent at js/sim.js:5641-5650, and derived-and-rebuilt is legal only for pure functions of restored state (the powered[]/svcStrain/megaOk policy). Both halves: all new keys append AFTER every existing key so the prior version's serialized prefix stays character-stable; backward-compatible load rides the existing defensive typeof/Array.isArray guards; NO `v ===` equality test is introduced anywhere in deserialize (there is none today); round-trip must be idempotent (deserialize(serialize()).serialize() character-identical). If a save-neutral read half is preferred, `history.waste` can be deferred to GP9b — but then GP9b's overflow curve has no independently certified series behind it, which is exactly the coupling S3 exists to break, so the recommendation is to keep it in GP9a.
milestones.launch_order_note: Strictly GP9a then GP9b; GP9a itself launches only after GP8b ships, because it claims the next save-ladder integer and both GP7 and GP8 touch the save format. GP9a's baseline for its byte-identity gate is the pinned commit immediately preceding it (git worktree on :8902 per the harness facts) — NOT 'the GP8 baseline' the parent spec names, which does not exist as a certified commit: baseline_ledger.current.certified_through is GP5b, and GP6 is live-in-tree but uncertified at v17 with its own workflow owning the promotion. GP9b's comparison commit is GP9a's SHIP commit, pinned at GP9b launch per R1, and GP9b must not start until GP9a is independently certified — its gates 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 all consume GP9a's instrumentation (history.waste, wasteCensus/wasteRateAt, powerLedger, ovCrosstalk), so an uncertified read half would leave the behavior half measuring itself with a ruler nobody checked, which is precisely the failure S3 was written to stop. Two scope decisions are made in the split and should be confirmed before GP9b implementation rather than discovered in it: the incinerator does NOT join isPlant() and instead takes a sixth powerMix bucket with its own upkeep and its MW injected BEFORE powerTradeDelta (so it is exportable); and landfill is EXCLUDED from fire candidacy while the incinerator is INCLUDED. Three gates of the parent milestone are reported under S6 and need a user decision, not a worker amendment: parent gate 3's Σ === powerSupply (already false on the current build under any open M27 trade deal), parent gate 6's byte-identity-vs-overflow contradiction (restated in GP9b as the WASTE_RATE-zero attribution gate), and parent gate 6's non-existent GP8 baseline.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 8(iii): "all 5 scenarios in js/scenarios.js (gridlock-97, twister-season, blackout-summer-97, y2k-ready, +1) ... the 5-element pass/fail vector is identical or strictly better"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: js/scenarios.js contains exactly FOUR scenarios. SCENARIOS = [ at line 91, closing ]; at line 286, with ids at lines 93 (gridlock-97), 139 (twister-season), 183 (blackout-summer-97) and 233 (y2k-ready). There is no fifth. The gate's "+1" placeholder and its "5-element pass/fail vector" cannot be produced by the fixture. Everything else about this gate is correct and is the right R1 comparative construction — the count is the only defect, but it makes the bar literally unmeasurable as written.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: "all FOUR scenarios in js/scenarios.js (gridlock-97, twister-season, blackout-summer-97, y2k-ready) ... the 4-element pass/fail vector is identical or strictly better." Re-read the array at launch rather than pinning the count from the spec, since GP7/GP8 precede GP9 and may add rows.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 4 (Σ CONTRACT) and GP9b gate 6 (S4): "mix.waste equals the summed rated MW of POWERED incinerator anchors EXACTLY" / "a POWERED incinerator (plume + lit) vs an UNPOWERED idle one is > 5% distinct at all 4 rotations"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Nothing in the declared design can ever set powered[] on an incinerator tile, so both bars are pinned at the failing value by construction. Three mechanisms light a tile in recomputePower: isPlant() self-lights and seeds the flood (js/sim.js:2381-2383); isMega() self-lights as a power island (2394); and the flood enters a neighbour only if conducts(j) (2367-2369, 2402). GP9b's declaration table explicitly EXCLUDES OV.INCIN from conducts() and states it does NOT join isPlant() (the COLLISION 2 decision), and it is not isMega. The only remaining precedent — the PUMP terminal-receiver loop at js/sim.js:2435-2450 — is gated on `this.over[i] !== OV.PUMP` and GP9b declares the incinerator EXCLUDED at that site too ("pump-feed (2435) excludes both"). Result: powered[incinAnchor] === 0 forever, mix.waste === 0 forever, and there is no reachable "powered incinerator" art state.
