The scope gestures at this once — "the PUMP precedent ... which also proves the 2x2 anchor + power-receiver pattern" — but the eight-site membership table, which is what gate 3's 16/16 asserts, never declares a receiver rule, and gate 3 conflates the two senses of the 2435 site (which tiles may FEED a pump vs which tiles are ENERGIZED as receivers).
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Add a NINTH declared site and gate it: "OV.INCIN is energized by a terminal-receiver pass mirroring the PUMP loop at js/sim.js:2435-2450 — non-propagating, run after the brownout/y2k cuts, anchor lit iff any tile orthogonally touching its 2x2 footprint is powered and is itself a real conductor." Then gate 3 becomes 18/18 (9 sites x 2 ids) and gate 4 should add: "an incinerator with no wire run to it reads powered[anchor] === 0 and contributes 0 to mix.waste; the same incinerator with a wire run reads 1 and contributes its full rated MW." If instead the incinerator is meant to generate unconditionally, delete the word "powered" from gate 4 and drop gate 6's powered/unpowered pair.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 1 (STREAM -> OVERFLOW): "city.cityIndex(city.poll) rises by >= 20 from tick 0"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: cityIndex is a whole-MAP mean (js/sim.js:5283-5287: sum over all 6400 tiles / 6400, wilderness included), and the project has already MEASURED and DOCUMENTED its reachable ceiling. js/sim.js:1516-1517 states, in the GP6 fix-pass block that exists precisely because someone else made this mistake: "measured ceiling of cityIndex(poll) with the ENTIRE map converted to coal plants is 40, and cityIndex(crime) sat at 5 with every patrol defunded ... 12 + 8 points of weight were dead." A rise of >= 20 on that index therefore demands that garbage overflow from a 300-tile city (4.7% of the map) generate HALF the citywide pollution of a map paved wall-to-wall with coal plants. No sane calibration of a backlog-scaled source reaches that, and pushing a constant until it does would wreck every other pollution-coupled bar. This is the same class of failure GP6 already had to repair, one file over.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Two independent fixes, either or both: (a) measure over the INHABITED footprint the way GP6's approvalCensus does rather than the whole-map mean, and (b) make it comparative against the control instead of absolute — e.g. "the zero-disposal arm's mean poll over the zoned footprint exceeds the drained control's by >= 15 at rollover 24, and the gap widens monotonically over the final 12 rollovers." Pin the threshold against a measured reachable range, not against the 0..255 type range.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 1 (STREAM -> OVERFLOW): "while the control's [cityIndex(poll)] drifts by < 3"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: This is an absolute bar on the CONTROL arm's own behaviour over 24 rollovers, and the control is a living, growing city — it develops zones, its industry levels up (js/sim.js:3669 emits (30 + lvl*35) per ZI tile), its roads accumulate traffic and its plants load up (coalSmog scales 40 -> 160 with powerDemand/powerSupply at js/sim.js:3718-3721). None of that has anything to do with waste. A control that simply grows can easily drift more than 3 index points and fail a gate about garbage. Same defect as the first incident: a bar that measures something other than the work.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Delete the control-side absolute and state the whole thing as one difference: "the zero-disposal arm's pollution index exceeds the drained control's by >= X at rollover 24, where both arms ran the identical seed and script." The control's own drift then cancels out of the measurement instead of becoming a failure mode.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 1: "history.waste (the series GP9a certified) is non-decreasing over all 24 [rollovers]" — in the ZERO-DISPOSAL arm
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The same gate requires this arm to be poisoned by its own garbage (rising pollution) while simultaneously requiring its waste OUTPUT never to dip — but waste output is a pure function of over[]/lvl[], and the sim de-levels developed tiles under exactly the conditions this gate is trying to induce. The decline paths: applyDecline at js/sim.js:1121-1123 (`c.lvl[i]--` on a demand-driven draw), the UNPOWERED decay at 1135, and the gridlock decay at 4464 (`if (this.lvl[i] > 1 && gCong(...) > 0.8 ...) this.lvl[i]--`). Rising poll[] drives landv[] down (js/sim.js:3731, `- this.poll[i] * 0.7`), which drives gFit down, which drives demand down, which drives applyDecline. Over 24 rollovers a genuinely overflowing city can lose levels and its tonnage can fall — the gate then fails BECAUSE the feature worked. Monotonicity of the stock (garbageBacklog) is safe; monotonicity of the flow (history.waste) is not.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Keep the strictly-increasing backlog bar (that one is sound — with zero disposal the stock only accumulates) and restate the flow bar comparatively and with slack: "history.waste at rollover 24 is >= its value at rollover 1, and the zero-disposal arm's history.waste is element-wise >= the drained control's at every rollover" — or drop it entirely, since garbageBacklog strictly increasing already proves the stream is live.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 2 (THE TWO ROUTES GENUINELY DIFFER): arm "(B) landfill sized to zero the backlog" vs arm "(C) incinerator of equal rated tonnage", both required to "hold garbageBacklog === 0 for the final 24 rollovers" of 120
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The two arms are sized in incommensurable units, so "equal rated tonnage" cannot be satisfied for both. The incinerator is a FLOW (fixed tonnage consumed per rollover, per the scope's monthly waste tick) and needs only rate >= monthly tonnage. The landfill is a STOCK (per-cell `fill`, saturating, per GP9b gate 5's own saturation bar) and to hold backlog at 0 through rollover 120 it must have capacity >= the CUMULATIVE 120 months of tonnage in a city that is also growing. A landfill "of equal rated tonnage" to the incinerator saturates and arm B fails; a landfill sized to survive 120 rollovers is not "equal" to the incinerator by any reading. The gate as written guarantees one arm fails, and the failure is about the fixture, not the build.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Name the two sizings separately and drop "equal": "(B) a landfill field whose TOTAL capacity exceeds the cumulative 120-rollover tonnage by >= 20%; (C) an incinerator bank whose per-rollover RATED TONNAGE exceeds peak monthly tonnage by >= 20%." Keep the backlog === 0 bar on both. If a like-for-like comparison is wanted, add a separate short-horizon arm (24 rollovers) where the landfill is genuinely rate-matched, and gate on the saturation date instead.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9a gate 3(i) and GP9b gate 5: "toggling `recycle` cuts wasteCensus().total by the DESIGNED PERCENTAGE +/-2%"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: "The designed percentage" is not a number in the spec — it is whatever value the implementer assigns to the recycle row's wasteMul at implement time. The bar therefore cannot fail in its design dimension: an implementer who picks wasteMul 0.95 passes the gate exactly as easily as one who picks 0.70, and the gate certifies nothing about whether Recycling is a meaningful player choice. The ±2% slop is doing real work (it catches per-tile vs total rounding drift in the fold at js/sim.js:4302-4313), but the percentage itself is self-referential.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Pin the constant in the spec before launch so the bar is falsifiable: "the recycle row carries wasteMul: 0.75; toggling it cuts wasteCensus().total by 25% +/-2%." S6 note: the constant is a tuning knob and may be re-argued at launch, but it must be a NUMBER in the gate, not a forward reference to the implementation.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP9b gate 4 (Σ CONTRACT): "with a sell deal open on a city whose ONLY generation is incinerators, city._tradeSold > 0"
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The fixture is under-specified in a way that can fail a correct build. js/sim.js:4381 computes `sold = Math.min(sellCommit, Math.max(0, plantSupply - demand))`. On a city whose only generation is incinerators, the quantity passed as plantSupply is the incinerator MW (that is the point of injecting it before the call at js/sim.js:2382) — so _tradeSold is 0 whenever the city's own demand meets or exceeds the incinerator output, no matter how correctly the injection was implemented. The gate states no relation between incinerator MW and demand.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: "...on a city whose ONLY generation is incinerators AND whose powerDemand is strictly less than the incinerator bank's rated MW, with sellCommit <= (ratedMW - demand): city._tradeSold === sellCommit exactly." The exact-equality form is strictly stronger than "> 0" and pins the injection point unambiguously.

preflight_missing_coverage: S4 VISIBILITY — the garbage GRAPH SERIES is ungated. GP9a ships history.waste plus a UI.graphSeries entry (js/ui.js:33) plus a checkbox in index.html, and GP9b gate 1 measures its whole overflow curve against that series, but NO gate opens the graph dialog, ticks the checkbox and asserts a plotted line appears. Gate 7 covers only the minimap and gate 4 only the pie. Because the series ships `on: false` per the GP3a/GP6 default-off policy, a broken checkbox wiring or a missing seriesData path (js/ui.js:1522-1534) is invisible to every gate in the split — the exact 'nothing invisible ever bills the player' failure S4 exists to catch. Suggested bar: with the checkbox ticked at all three graph ranges (1yr/10yr/100yr), the garbage line renders non-empty and its final plotted value equals the last element of city.history.waste.

S4 VISIBILITY — the PER-TILE garbage readout in the query panel is ungated and arguably undelivered. GP9a's rationale claims 'a query row' as one of four player-facing wins, but the six numbered deliverables in scope do not include a query-panel waste row, and no gate asserts one. GP9b gate 5 asserts only the literal string 'full' for a saturated landfill cell. If the minimap is the sole per-tile expression, wasteRateAt has no numeric surface anywhere.

GP9b's new COMPLAINT kind `garbage` has NO gate of any kind — not that it fires, not its text, not the tile it targets, and not the scope's own claim that 'it changes which x,y the ticker jumps to ONLY in cities carrying a backlog'. This matters concretely: the declared score is `40 + backlogPressure` where backlogPressure is a CITYWIDE scalar, so every tile scores identically, and scanComplaints picks the winner with a strict `score > bestScore` (js/sim.js:5328) — meaning the garbage complaint always resolves to the LOWEST map index that qualifies, and the ticker's 'Show me' camera jump lands on the same corner tile every single time. Nothing in the split would detect that. Suggested bars: the complaint fires within COMPLAINT_EVERY*2 rollovers of the backlog crossing its threshold; its (x,y) is a landfill/high-waste tile rather than index 0; and on a zero-backlog city the complaint kind and target are byte-identical to the GP9a build's.

GP9b's ADVISORY_GATES WASTE_OVERFLOW row is ungated. The scope adds it 'so diagnoseTile explains the stall', which is the GP1a substrate contract, but no bar asserts city.diagnoseTile(i) actually emits the row on a stalled tile in a backlogged city, nor that it stays absent on a clean one. Draw-neutrality is covered (gate 8(ii)); presence and correctness are not.

The REPAIRED POWER PIE has no rendering gate. GP9a gate 4 checks the legend TOTAL string only. Nothing asserts the new SIGNED trade row renders correctly when the value is negative (an export), that fillPowerMix's arc loop at js/ui.js:1080-1085 does not emit a negative or NaN sweep when a trade row is folded in, or that the pie still draws when total <= 0. GP9b adds a SIXTH `waste` slice with the same gap — gate 4 checks mix.waste numerically but nothing checks the slice renders or that POWERMIX_TYPES was extended (the scope itself warns 'omit the row and the pie silently under-sums').

GP9b gate 5 measures with `city.wasteCapacity()`, an instrument that neither half's scope declares or ships. Under S3 the behavior half must be measured by instruments the read half certified; wasteCapacity() cannot live in GP9a (fill[] does not exist yet), so it must at minimum be named as a GP9b deliverable with its own definition, or the gate is measuring with a ruler that appears for the first time inside the gate that uses it.

GP9b gate 8(ii)'s attribution claim overreaches, and the residue is ungated. With WASTE_RATE zeroed and a GP9a-era scripted build order (which by definition cannot place a landfill or incinerator — those tools do not exist in GP9a), the two new over[] ids never appear in over[], so the eight predicate edits, the five tool registries (COST/TOOL_TIER/OV_SIZE/toolOverlay/TOOLS), the budget line and the complaint kind are NEVER EXERCISED by that run. Byte-identity therefore cannot 'prove' they contribute no drift — it proves only that dormant code is dormant. Gate 3 part 2's live probes do cover the eight predicates with a real landfill field; the tool registries, the deptCosts/collectBudget/lastBudget-ctor budget line and the complaint kind have no equivalent probe. Suggested addition: a WASTE_RATE-zeroed run that DOES place landfills and an incinerator, byte-identical to itself across load/save and asserting funds delta equals exactly the placement cost plus upkeep.

No save-compat bar covers the GP9a ordinance plumbing on a LEGACY save. GP9a adds `wasteMul: 1` to identityOrdMods (js/sim.js:632-634) and a fold line to recomputeOrdinances (4302-4310). A pre-GP9a save with `recycle` already enacted must reload with ordMods.wasteMul defined rather than undefined — recomputeOrdinances is documented as running on load, so this is probably safe, but gate 6 asserts nothing about ordMods at all. One bar: 'a pre-GP9a save with recycle enacted loads with typeof city.ordMods.wasteMul === "number" and wasteCensus().total finite and non-NaN.'

GP9b determinism gate 8(i) reproduces history.waste, garbageBacklog and history.poll across 20 seeds but omits fill[] — the other new serialized array. Gate 7 compares fill[] on a load-vs-native run, but the 20-seed determinism sweep does not, so a seed-dependent divergence in landfill fill ordering would only be caught if it happened to perturb the backlog.
milestones.split_of: GP9 (preflight-authored S3 split, grounded against the live source 2026-07-30)

milestones.title: The Distress Ledger — a Deterministic Monthly Sweep That Counts Decline and Changes Nothing
milestones.scope:
Ships the RULER: the deterministic O(n) monthly sweep GP10's own scope demands, its per-tile counter, and every player-facing readout of decline — with zero sim consequence, so it carries a byte-identical gate.

1. NEW PLANES, declared beside unpow at sim.js:1838 (`this.unpow = new Uint8Array(n)`): `this.distress` (Uint8, 0..250 consecutive FAILING month rollovers) and `this.distressCause` (Uint8, index+1 of the DISTRESS_CAUSES row that bound last sweep, 0 = none). Mostly-zero small-valued Uint8 is exactly packU8's sparse mode-3 workload (sim.js:36-60): serialize alongside sim.js:5734 `traffic: packU8(this.traffic), unpow: packU8(this.unpow), fire: packU8(this.fire)`, restore beside sim.js:5916 `unpackU8(d.unpow, c.unpow);`.

2. NEW FROZEN TABLE `DISTRESS_CAUSES` — ordered, first-match, {code, label, test, text, evid}, in the SVC_DEF/APPROVAL_TERMS house style. Rows: DARK (`!c.powered[i]`), CRIME (`c.crime[i] >= DISTRESS_T.crime`), SLUMP (sector demand below threshold for the tile's zone, read off the committed `c.demand`), GRIDLOCK (`gCong` above the eviction line). It MUST NOT be inserted into GROWTH_GATES (sim.js:1125+): firstGate (sim.js:1269-1273) is the unfiltered walk growthPass uses to pick the row whose apply spends `this.rng.growth`, and the discipline comment at sim.js:1737-1744 forbids it. This table is walked ONLY by distressTick and by one new ADVISORY_GATES row.

3. `distressTick()` — zero RNG, O(n), touches every tile exactly once. Slot is FIXED HERE AND NEVER MOVED AGAIN: in tick()'s %24 block at sim.js:5492-5512, immediately after `approvalTick()` (sim.js:5499) and BEFORE `collectBudget()` (sim.js:5500), the slot GP10b needs so abandonment can affect the same month's taxes. On a ZR/ZC/ZI tile it walks DISTRESS_CAUSES; first match => `distress[i] = min(250, distress[i]+1)`, `distressCause[i] = row+1`; no match => both 0. Publishes `this.distressCensus` computed over the ZONED footprint at ANY level — the exact denominator approvalCensus uses (sim.js:5082-5099) for the reason documented at sim.js:5049-5059 (the measured self-healing bug: unpowShare 0.309→0.000 with the wire still cut). Also publishes `this.distressVisits` for the sweep-honesty gate.

4. TEN-SITE CLEAR AUDIT (the read half owns it, byte-cheap): reset both planes at sim.js:2249 (waterfill), 2266 (place footprint), 2315-2316 (bulldoze — already clears fire/unpow), 3615 (road crumble→RUBBLE), 4542 (fire burnout→RUBBLE), 4718, 4744, 4778, 4806, 4829 (the five disaster destruction loops).

5. READOUTS, all rebuilt on open/hover from live state: one ADVISORY_GATES row `BLOCK_DISTRESS` (sim.js:1745+, draw-neutral, attaches via _attachAdvisories at sim.js:4512-4522) → free in the query verdict box (ui.js:1710-1719) and the memoized hover line (ui.js:2228-2239); a 'Distressed lots' row in districtStats (sim.js:5580-5611) + fillDistrictStats (ui.js:1327-1355); a live blight line in buildAlmanacRows (ui.js:1451-1467, the GP3b commute line at ui.js:1464 is the exact precedent); a `distress` complaint kind — one COMPLAINT_T threshold, one scoring branch in scanComplaints (sim.js:5314-5347), one COMPLAINT_TEXT line (sim.js:777-783) — landing on the shipped click-to-jump path (ui.js:2118-2127); a 14th 'Blight' minimap mode (MM_NAMES ui.js:773-776, setMapMode ui.js:820, render.js:2244+); `history.blight` added to BOTH hardcoded key lists (sim.js:31 and the mirror at sim.js:5274).

6. S4 tile expression: a draw-time distress treatment keyed off distress[i] — the drawChar precedent at render.js:1074 (per-tile overlay over an UNMODIFIED sprite), three bands, no new sprite bake. Night glow at render.js:1043 is NOT touched here; full suppression is reserved for GP10b's abandoned state so the states stay distinct.

HONESTY CONSTRAINT: no copy in this half may promise abandonment — it does not exist yet. The advisory states the observed cause and the month count only. GP10b amends the copy to add the countdown. LAUNCH CONDITION (preflight, non-negotiable): the gate problems recorded in preflight_gate_problems below were found by an adversarial reviewer that read the LIVE source and MEASURED the unchanged build. The design phase MUST resolve every one before implementation, and each resolution must be reported in the ship verdict with its measurement. Rules for resolving: an IMPOSSIBILITY (unachievable/self-contradictory/vacuous — the sim arithmetic or the fixture cannot produce the quantity) is corrected by re-specifying the gate so it measures the intended property with a reachable bar, and the correction is recorded with the measurement proving the original was impossible. An ABSOLUTE-SHOULD-BE-COMPARATIVE bar is restated per the R1 protocol (this build vs baseline on identical scripted inputs). An AMBIGUOUS-THRESHOLD gate is pinned to a named city, seed, sample count and reference quantity. An UNMEASURABLE gate is either given a concrete headless observable or reported to the user as needing a design decision. A resolution that changes what the milestone is TRYING TO ACHIEVE (rather than how it is measured) is a DESIGN decision — surface it to the user, never decide it (S6). Also close every missing_coverage item or justify its omission.
milestones.player_facing_win: The mayor can finally see a neighbourhood dying: every failing block names WHY it is failing and how many months it has been failing, on the tile, in the neighbourhood report, on a Blight minimap, in the almanac, and in an angry fax that jumps the camera there — before anything actually collapses.
quality_gates: BYTE-IDENTICAL SIM (the S3 contract). 20 seeds x 600 ticks, scripted build, Math.random UNSTUBBED, against a pinned pre-GP10a worktree served on :8902. SHA-256 over the concatenation of over/lvl/anc/varnt/terr/rail/district/unpow/fire/traffic/poll/crime/landv plus the scalars (funds, pop, jobs, tickCount, month, year, tier, approval) plus the four rng cursor indices (growth/fire/hazard/build): 0 differing bytes on 20 of 20 seeds. The growth cursor's total draw count is EQUAL on every seed. distress[]/distressCause[]/history.blight are excluded from the hash by construction (they are the new state).

SWEEP HONESTY (spec gate 1, read half). An instrumented per-tile visit counter over 120 consecutive rollovers shows min visits == max visits == 1 for all MAP*MAP tiles on every rollover (exactly one visit per tile per rollover, 120 of 120). A Math.random call-count spy plus the four rng cursor indices are UNCHANGED across every distressTick() invocation: exactly 0 draws, 120 of 120.

COUNTER EXACTNESS + THE GP6 SELF-HEALING REGRESSION TEST. On a scripted city, cutting power to a zoned sub-district makes distress[i] == k on exactly the k-th rollover after the cut for 100% of tiles in that footprint, k = 1..18 (exact integer equality, no tolerance). Restoring power sets distress[i] == 0 on the very next rollover for 100% of those tiles. Measured over the ZONED footprint denominator, distressShare holds constant at 168/544 = 0.309 for 24 consecutive rollovers with the wire still cut (the numbers the sim.js:5049-5059 comment recorded) — it must NOT decay toward 0.000.

CAUSE ATTRIBUTION IS EXACT. For each of the 4 DISTRESS_CAUSES rows, a scripted single-cause city reports that row as distressCause on >= 95% of its distressed tiles and reports each of the other 3 rows on 0 tiles. Across 120 rollovers of a mixed city, distressCause[i] === 0 for 100% of tiles with distress[i] === 0 (no orphan cause bytes).

LEGIBILITY AT EVERY SHIPPED SURFACE. Over 200 sampled distressed tiles: diagnoseTile(i).advisories contains BLOCK_DISTRESS with the month count AND the cause label in evidence, 200 of 200; the hover status line and the query verdict box both render that label. districtStats returns distressed/zoned counts that equal a fresh independent recount, exact integers, on 10 sampled districts. The almanac blight line's numbers equal city.distressCensus field-for-field. A `distress` complaint fires within 2*COMPLAINT_EVERY rollovers of a district reaching >= 10 distressed tiles, and its ticker click lands the camera on a tile with distress > 0 (boolean, 10 of 10 trials).

S4 VISIBILITY AT ALL 4 ROTATIONS. Screenshot pixel-diff at cam.r = 0,1,2,3 of a distressed block against a pixel-identical healthy block: >= 2% of the tile's pixels differ at EACH of the 4 rotations. The three bands (healthy, at-risk distress >= 6, critical distress >= 12) are PAIRWISE distinct by >= 2% pixel diff at each of the 4 rotations (3 pairs x 4 rotations = 12 assertions, 12 pass). The 'Blight' minimap chip is the 14th mode, renders a non-uniform image on a distressed city, and its legend names it.

TEN-SITE CLEAR DISCIPLINE. For each of the 10 tile-clearing sites (sim.js:2249, 2266, 2315, 3615, 4542, 4718, 4744, 4778, 4806, 4829), fire that site on a tile carrying distress >= 5 and assert distress[i] === 0 AND distressCause[i] === 0 immediately after: 10 of 10 sites pass, asserted individually and named in the report.

SAVE-COMPAT + DETERMINISM. The ladder integer is read from the live `v:` literal at sim.js:5652 AT LAUNCH and is LIVE+1 — never hardcoded, no version-equality test anywhere in deserialize, new keys APPENDED after the last existing key (today sim.js:5745 `recallDone`). A pre-GP10a save loads with sum(distress) === 0 and sum(distressCause) === 0 and no retroactive blight. serialize→deserialize→serialize is character-identical (idempotent round-trip). history.blight survives a load of a 250-entry save with length exactly equal to history.pop after the >240 trim (proves BOTH lists at sim.js:31 and sim.js:5274 were extended). Same seed + script reproduces byte-identical distress[] over 600 ticks across 3 runs with Math.random UNSTUBBED. Zero console errors.
milestones.split_rationale: The read half is emphatically NOT vacuous. Nothing in the tree today counts consecutive months of neglect: unpow[] is written in exactly two places, both inside growthPass's 340-random-tile sampler (increment at sim.js:1134, reset at sim.js:4461), so at 340*24/6400 = 1.275 Poisson samples per tile per month it is a 'dark checks' tally, not a calendar — the drift report's confirmed claim. There is no crime/demand/gridlock distress accounting at all, no district distress readout, no blight minimap mode, no blight history series, and no blight substrate anywhere in the tree (the repo-wide grep returns four prose comments and one scenario string, zero code). Every one of GP10's own quality gates is a MEASUREMENT taken with this ruler — '>= 60% of its developed tiles abandoned', 'a visit counter proves the sweep touches every tile exactly once', 'diagnoseTile returns the verdict with its countdown'. Shipping the ruler first, provably behavior-free, is what lets GP10b's numbers be trusted. The half is cheap to prove honest precisely because it can only write its own two planes: the byte-identical gate is decidable rather than argued. It also front-loads the three things most likely to be got wrong under implementation pressure — the zoned-footprint denominator (the GP6 self-healing bug, already measured once), the ten-site clear audit (nine of ten sites do not currently clear unpow, so copying the existing pattern produces phantom blight), and the BOTH-history-lists rule — into the half where a mistake costs nothing but a re-run. Per S8 this half is independently shippable: a mayor who stops here gets a real diagnostic layer.
milestones.save_version_plan: DO NOT HARDCODE. The ladder reads v17 TODAY (sim.js:5652 `v: 17`), but GP10 is LAST in .execution_order behind GP7b, GP8b and GP9 — and the roadmap marks all three touches_save_format:true. GP10 is only v18 if all three slip. RULE FOR BOTH HALVES: at launch, read the live `v:` integer literal at sim.js:5652 and take LIVE+1; GP10b then takes GP10a's shipped version +1. Two halves = two ladder integers (GP10a adds distress[]/distressCause[]/history.blight; GP10b adds aband[] and the per-district renewal flag). Mechanics, identical in both halves: (1) APPEND new keys strictly after the last existing key — today sim.js:5745 `recallDone` — so the earlier-version prefix stays character-stable; (2) guard every read with typeof / Array.isArray and NEVER a version-equality test anywhere in deserialize (the shipped GP3b/GP5b/GP6 comments at sim.js:5736-5746 and 5916-5926 are the pattern); (3) the two Uint8 planes go through packU8/unpackU8 (sim.js:36-60) alongside sim.js:5734 `traffic/unpow/fire` and restore beside sim.js:5916 `unpackU8(d.unpow, c.unpow);` — unpackU8 already rejects malformed packs and leaves `out` untouched, so an older save lands all-zero with no retroactive blight; (4) the per-district renewal designation needs NO new array and NO new save key — it rides the districts[] object round-trip (serialize sim.js:5683, field-preserving Object.assign restore sim.js:5785-5786) and needs only a defensive default; (5) `history.blight` is added ONCE, in GP10a, to BOTH hardcoded key lists — normaliseHistory at sim.js:31 AND its mirror in collectBudget's >240 trim loop at sim.js:5274 — so GP10b adds no history series at all. Both halves gate on an idempotent serialize→deserialize→serialize round-trip and on every earlier version loading clean.
milestones.launch_order_note: GP10a ships FIRST and alone. It is independently shippable per S8 (a mayor who stops there gets a real diagnostic layer: causes, month counts, a Blight minimap, district and almanac readouts, and a complaint that jumps the camera), and it is decidably safe because it can only write its own two planes — the byte-identical gate is a hash comparison, not an argument. GP10a must land the FIXED SWEEP SLOT (tick()'s %24 block, after approvalTick at sim.js:5499, before collectBudget at sim.js:5500), the ZONED-FOOTPRINT DENOMINATOR (the approvalCensus discipline at sim.js:5082-5099 that the measured self-healing bug at sim.js:5049-5059 forced), the TEN-SITE CLEAR AUDIT, and the BOTH-HISTORY-LISTS extension — every one of those is a known-expensive mistake, and in the read half a mistake costs a re-run rather than a re-pin. GP10b then re-pins against GP10a's pinned hash and is measured entirely by GP10a's counter. GP10a has NO dependency on GP7b/GP8b/GP9 and can launch the moment those three either land or are deferred — it only needs the live ladder integer at launch. GP10b has one real sequencing question and it is already resolved in its gates: the original spiral gate's dependence on GP7's assessed-value floor is DROPPED (the floor does not exist — sim.js:5187 is the headcount formula, sim.js:4927-4943 is eight fixed dept lines, sim.js:1992 is six funding levers, and GP7 status is still 'todo'), replaced by a comparative-vs-baseline survivability gate. If GP7b ships a real assessed-value floor before GP10b launches, ADD the floor clause back as a separate gate — do not fold it into the survivability gate, and never let the implementing worker amend it (S6). Two items to escalate to the user at GP10b launch rather than resolve in implementation: the declared re-pin (authorized here, bounded by gate 1) and the fire-candidacy decision for abandoned tiles (declare it in design; it is a crosstalk assertion, not an implementation detail).

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 5 (BLIGHT RADIATES) — crime clause
preflight_gate_problems.problem: "mean crime in the 4-tile annulus is >= 10 HIGHER than control" is unreachable under the scope's own design. Crime is NEVER diffused: the only diffuse() calls in recomputeMaps are poll (sim.js:3681), land value (3694) and traffic (3700). Crime is a pure per-tile formula, `density - polCov - landv*0.2 - ordMods.crimeCut` (sim.js:3746-3748). The scope puts the blight crime term inside that per-tile loop gated on aband[i], so a NON-abandoned annulus tile receives blight crime only through the landv channel at coefficient 0.2 — a +10 crime annulus requires a -50 landv annulus, i.e. more than three times the gate's own -15 landv bar. No constant choice fixes this; the term simply does not reach the annulus.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Split the measurement to match where each term actually applies: measure crime ON the abandoned cluster tiles (where the added term lives) and landv on the annulus (which the diffused pollution channel does reach). If crime is genuinely meant to radiate, that is a SCOPE change — seed a diffused blight source in the source loop at sim.js:3663-3681 (the `if (this.fire[i]) src[i] += 100` idiom) feeding a diffused plane, and re-derive the annulus bar from the diffusion kernel rather than asserting a number.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 3 (COUNTER EXACTNESS) — the 168/544 = 0.309 clause
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The gate hardcodes "distressShare holds constant at 168/544 = 0.309", citing sim.js:5049-5059. Two problems. (1) WRONG METRIC: those numbers are unpowShare (zoned tiles that are dark), recorded in prose at sim.js:1590-1592 and 5054-5057. distressShare counts ALL FOUR causes, so it is >= unpowShare by construction — cutting power to a third of the city also crashes sector demand, so SLUMP fires on tiles DARK does not cover and the share cannot equal 0.309. (2) NO FIXTURE: repo-wide, 544/168/0.309 appear ONLY inside those two comments. There is no committed script or save that reproduces that city, and it was measured on a build that HAD abandonment (that is the bug the comment describes) — a build GP10a by definition is not. The literal is not reproducible.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Make it a co-measurement instead of a literal. (a) distressShare must be NON-DECREASING across 24 consecutive rollovers with the wire still cut — the actual anti-self-healing property. (b) The DARK-cause subset count (tiles with distressCause === DARK+1) must equal approvalCensus's live zUnpow on the same city at the same rollover, exact integer equality, every rollover — this proves the shared denominator without importing a number. (c) If a fixed number is wanted, commit the scripted city as a fixture and re-measure it on the GP10a build first.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 3 (HYSTERESIS)
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Scope §6 defines revival as "an abandoned tile needs REVIVE_W consecutive rollovers at distress == 0 before the ABANDONED row stops matching." The gate then measures revival latency against REVIVE_W with a ±2 tolerance on >= 18 of 20 runs, plus "EXACTLY 0 tiles revive before rollover REVIVE_W - 2". Both clauses are true by construction — the latency IS REVIVE_W, exactly, because a counter is being compared to its own constant. The gate tests that a decrement works, and the ±2/18-of-20 statistics create the false impression that something stochastic is being measured. It cannot fail without the feature being outright broken.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Replace with the exact identity (latency === REVIVE_W on 20 of 20, zero tolerance — cheaper and strictly stronger), and move the real content into a comparative assertion the constant does NOT trivially satisfy: a DESIGNATED renewal district's revival latency is shorter than an undesignated one by exactly the designed reduction, on the same seed and the same cluster, 10 of 10 pairs. Also assert the distress counter is genuinely re-armed — a tile that hits distress > 0 mid-window restarts at 0, it does not resume.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 4 (CAUSE ATTRIBUTION IS EXACT)
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The two clauses cannot both be met with the stated tolerance. Every tile with distress[i] > 0 got there because SOME DISTRESS_CAUSES row matched (first-match, scope §3), so its distressCause is necessarily one of the four rows. If "each of the other 3 rows [is reported] on 0 tiles", then the target row is on 100% of distressed tiles — the ">= 95%" allowance is unusable. An implementer who measures 96% has already failed the second clause, and will not know which clause is the real bar. This is the same shape as the y=12/y=9/y=15 incident: the fixture described cannot produce the quantity measured.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Pick one bar. Either: "100% of distressed tiles report the target row and the other 3 rows appear on 0 tiles" (clean, and what the fixture actually implies); or, if the single-cause city cannot be made that clean, ">= 95% report the target row, and the report ENUMERATES the residual <= 5% by cause with a stated reason" — dropping the 0-tiles clause. Do not ship both.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 7 (CROSSTALK PREDICATES) assertion 1
preflight_gate_problems.problem: "Abandoning N tiles drops this.powerDemand by exactly N at sim.js:2367-2372" is false in the scenario that produces abandonment. The loop counts `if (this.powered[i] && t >= OV.ZR && ...) demand++` — a tile only contributes when it is POWERED. The primary abandonment path in this milestone is DARK (unpowered for ABAND_W rollovers), and those tiles already contribute 0, so the drop is 0, not N. The assertion is additionally perturbed by the `pdMult` activeMods multiplier and `powerTradeDelta` immediately below (sim.js:2374-2382), either of which breaks exact-N.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the precondition in the gate: run the assertion on a POWERED abandonment path (a CRIME- or SLUMP-caused cluster), with no `powerDemand` activeMod (pdMult === 1) and no regional power trade open, then assert the exact -N drop. Separately assert the DARK case explicitly reads -0 so the null result is recorded rather than mistaken for a bug.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 9 (SPIRAL SURVIVABLE)
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The re-specification correctly drops the GP7 floor clause and adds a comparative clause, but it LEAVES an absolute bar in front of it: "returns the city to positive monthly net AND rising pop within 60 rollovers on THIS build in >= 8 of 10 seeded runs". That is the exact shape of incident 1 ("wins the medal in >= 8 of 10"). It is also the clause most likely to fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the work: GP10b ADDS decline pressure (ABAND_SMOG pollution, blight crime, a landv subtraction, and the census exclusion removing taxable pop), so the absolute success count can legitimately fall below 8 while the comparative clause — the one that actually tests for regression — passes cleanly. Secondly, "rising pop" has no definition: rising measured over what window, against what point?
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Keep only the comparative clause: this build's success count >= the pinned pre-GP10 baseline's on the SAME script and seeds, with the per-seed outcomes tabulated. Report the absolute count as an OBSERVATION, not a bar. Define the success predicate concretely, e.g. "monthly net > 0 at rollover 60 AND pop at rollover 60 > pop at the trough rollover" — a single unambiguous headless read.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 1 (BOUNDED DECLARED RE-PIN)
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The gate's interesting half will almost certainly never execute. 600 ticks is 25 month rollovers (tick()'s %24 block, sim.js:5492). Reaching aband requires ABAND_W CONSECUTIVE distressed rollovers on top of the time to develop the city, so a normal scripted build on 20 seeds will very likely produce ZERO abandoning seeds. The gate then reads 20/20 byte-identical and PASSES, with the "first differing byte >= first aband[i]=1" clause — the entire point of the bounded re-pin — never exercised on a single seed. Nothing in the gate requires that any seed abandon.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Add a coverage precondition and make it a failure condition: the 20-seed script must include a deliberately sabotaged arm (power cut / service collapse) such that >= 6 of 20 seeds actually reach aband, and the gate FAILS if fewer than that number exercise the divergence clause. Report the abandoning-seed count in the results. Consider extending the horizon past 600 ticks for the sabotaged arm so ABAND_W + development time fits.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 2 (CAUSATION) — the 18-rollover / 60% bar
preflight_gate_problems.problem: ABAND_W is never given a value anywhere in the split spec, yet the gate hardcodes 18 rollovers and 60%. If ABAND_W > 18 the result is 0% by construction and the gate is unreachable. Worse, the denominator is ambiguous in a way that swings the answer from ~0% to ~100%: scope §1 says "a zoned tile with distress[i] >= ABAND_W flips to aband=1" with NO lvl guard, and scope §3 walks DISTRESS_CAUSES on any ZR/ZC/ZI tile regardless of level — so EMPTY zoned lots accumulate distress and abandon too, making >= 60% of the zoned footprint trivial. That directly contradicts two other statements: §1's "the tile KEEPS lvl[] so the derelict sprite has a size" (a lvl-0 abandoned tile has no size), and this gate's own separation clause "separates aband===1 from merely-decayed (lvl===0 && aband===0)", which presumes lvl-0 tiles do NOT abandon.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Declare ABAND_W in the scope and require 18 > ABAND_W with stated margin. Declare explicitly whether abandonment requires lvl > 0 (the derelict-sprite and separation clauses both imply it does). Then re-express the bar over the subset the answer is actually about: >= 60% of tiles that were DEVELOPED (lvl > 0) in the pre-cut snapshot, with the zoned footprint reported alongside as the stable denominator.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 6 (THE CAMPAIGN BEATS WAITING) — the 40%-fewer-rollovers clause
preflight_gate_problems.problem: "returns the cluster to within 5% of control mean landv at least 40% FEWER rollovers than the do-nothing arm" has no horizon and no censoring rule. The do-nothing arm is a blighted cluster with an abandonment feedback loop — the expected outcome is that it NEVER returns to within 5% of control. When the denominator is infinite/undefined the ratio is undefined and the gate can be neither passed nor failed honestly, which is precisely the condition under which an implementer quietly reinterprets the bar. (The second clause, ">= 25% more developed non-abandoned zoned tiles at rollover 60", is sound — it has a horizon.)
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Fix a horizon H (rollover 120 is consistent with the rest of the split) and define non-recovery as censored-at-H. Score the pair as a success when EITHER the renewal arm recovers by H and the do-nothing arm does not, OR both recover and the renewal arm's rollover count is <= 60% of the do-nothing arm's. Require >= 9 of 10 pairs and report the censoring split so "9 of 10 by censoring alone" is visible rather than hidden.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 5 (LEGIBILITY) — the distress complaint clause
preflight_gate_problems.problem: scanComplaints (sim.js:5314-5347) is a CITYWIDE winner-take-all argmax that emits at most one complaint per COMPLAINT_EVERY (= 3) rollovers. The shipped scores are flat: rubble 130, unpowered 150, traffic 60+excess, crime 40+excess, poll 40+excess. The natural way to produce "a district reaching >= 10 distressed tiles" is the DARK cause — which means >= 10 developed unpowered tiles, each scoring a flat 150. Unless the new distress kind scores ABOVE 150, no distress complaint can ever fire in that scenario, and the "within 2*COMPLAINT_EVERY rollovers" window contains at most two emission opportunities. If the implementer does score it above 150, the shipped unpowered and rubble complaints are starved — a regression the gate does not measure.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the distress kind's score RANK relative to the five existing kinds explicitly in the scope (it is a design decision, not an implementation detail). Run the timing assertion on a CRIME- or SLUMP-caused fixture where no higher-scoring kind co-occurs. Add a companion anti-crosstalk assertion: on a pinned pre-GP10a fixture, each of the five existing complaint kinds fires at its pre-GP10a rate over 120 rollovers.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 4 (CENSUS INTEGRITY) — the pop/jobs identity
preflight_gate_problems.problem: "city.pop === Σ RES_POP[lvl] over non-abandoned ZR and city.jobs === Σ COM_JOB/IND_JOB over non-abandoned ZC/ZI" is not the identity the code implements. computeDemandParts (sim.js:4163) also folds arcology contributions into the SAME totals: `else if (isArco(this.over[i]) && this.anc[i] === i) { pop += ARCO_POP[...]; iJobs += ARCO_JOB[...]; }` — a single Launch Arco adds 3000 pop. The stated identity therefore holds only on a city with no arcologies, i.e. it is an identity that passes on the toy fixture and silently stops being true on a real Megalopolis-tier city — exactly the failure mode this review is meant to catch. As written it could also produce a false FAIL if the harness happens to build one.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the full identity: pop === Σ RES_POP[lvl] over non-abandoned ZR + Σ ARCO_POP over arco anchors (anc === i), and the matching jobs form including ARCO_JOB. Then run it on a fixture that DOES contain at least one arcology, so the arco term is actually exercised rather than assumed absent.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 6 (S4 VISIBILITY) — the reference block
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The gate diffs a distressed block "against a pixel-identical healthy block". No such reference block can be constructed. Sprite variants are seeded per tile at growth time (`c.varnt[i] = rg.pick(5)` at sim.js:1115 and 1119) and at build time (sim.js:2270), terrain variants are seeded at generation (sim.js:2131-2132), and tiles are further differentiated by land value, pollution and neighbour context. Two distinct blocks on the same map are essentially never pixel-identical, so the gate has no constructible control and the implementer has no way to know whether a 2% diff came from the distress treatment or from varnt.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Diff the SAME tile against itself: capture at distress[i] = 0, then write the band value directly into the plane, re-render with camera, tick, funds and every other input held fixed, and diff. Repeat at cam.r = 0,1,2,3. That isolates the treatment exactly and needs no reference block. Keep the >= 2% threshold and the pairwise-band structure unchanged.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 7 (TEN-SITE CLEAR DISCIPLINE)
preflight_gate_problems.problem: "fire that site on a tile carrying distress >= 5" cannot be satisfied naturally at the road-crumble site (sim.js:3615). roadWearTick only touches OV.ROAD / OV.WIREROAD tiles, and distress is written ONLY on ZR/ZC/ZI (scope §3). The only route from a zoned tile to a road tile is place(), which passes through the footprint site at sim.js:2266 — a site this same gate requires to clear the planes. So no road tile can ever carry distress >= 5, and the precondition for that site is unconstructible. The gate reads as though all ten preconditions are naturally reachable, which will send an implementer hunting for a state that does not exist.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Say plainly that the harness WRITES distress[i] = 5 and distressCause[i] = k directly into the planes immediately before firing each site — this is a defence-in-depth clear test, not a reachability test. Additionally mark which of the ten sites are naturally reachable from a distressed zoned tile (2266, 2315, 4542, 4718, 4744, 4778, 4806, 4829, 2249) and which are defensive-only (3615), so a future reader does not mistake the defensive ones for live paths.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10a scope §6 band thresholds (>= 6 / >= 12) vs GP10b gate 8
preflight_gate_problems.problem: GP10a pins the three visual bands at healthy / >= 6 / >= 12 and gates on them. ABAND_W is never assigned a value anywhere in the split. If ABAND_W <= 12, a tile flips to aband before it can be observed in the "critical" band, so once GP10b lands the critical band is unreachable state — and GP10b gate 8's requirement that abandoned tiles be "pairwise visually distinct from healthy AND from all three GP10a distress bands" contains a term that cannot be instantiated on a live city. The two halves' constants are coupled but only one of them is written down.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Pin ABAND_W in GP10a's scope (not GP10b's) with ABAND_W > 12 and stated margin, OR define the bands as fractions of ABAND_W (e.g. >= ABAND_W/3 and >= 2*ABAND_W/3) so the two halves cannot drift apart. Then GP10b gate 8 can name the exact distress value it forces to observe each band.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 5 (BLIGHT RADIATES) — the -15 landv magnitude
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The -15 annulus landv bar is an absolute magnitude that was not derived from the code path that has to produce it. Scope §3 deliberately forbids seeding the blight penalty into lv[] (correctly — diffuse() clamps into a Uint8Array at sim.js:3768), so the fold term at 3730-3741 applies only to the abandoned tile itself. The ONLY radiating channel left into the annulus is `- this.poll[i] * 0.7` in the fold, meaning a -15 annulus mean requires roughly +21 diffused pollution there. Given diffuse(src, poll, 3, 0.24) over a 16-tile cluster, that implies an ABAND_SMOG well above the fire term's `src[i] += 100` (sim.js:3679). No pilot measurement is cited, so the bar may be reachable only with a constant that visibly outweighs an active fire.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Run a one-off pilot (place a 16-tile abandoned cluster, sweep ABAND_SMOG, read the annulus mean at +42 ticks) and PIN the bar to what the kernel actually yields at a defensible constant. Until then state it comparatively and directionally — "annulus mean landv is strictly lower than the matched control on >= 9 of 10 pairs, with the measured delta reported" — and add the magnitude bar once the pilot number exists.

preflight_missing_coverage: GP10b: the >= OV.ZR auto-join list is only PARTIALLY discharged. sim.js:347 enumerates the idiom sites as conducts / seed / demand / BROWNOUT / Y2K, and the live sites are demand (2370), brownout (2394), y2k (2410) and fire candidacy (4599). Scope §4 declares only demand + fire candidacy, and gate 7 asserts only those two. Nothing declares or asserts whether an abandoned tile is a brownout victim or a y2k victim — both read `this.powered[i] && t >= OV.ZR` and both will silently include abandoned tiles by default.

GP10a: no anti-crosstalk gate on the new `distress` complaint kind. scanComplaints (sim.js:5314-5347) is a single-winner citywide argmax with one emission per COMPLAINT_EVERY, so adding a kind can starve the five shipped kinds (rubble/traffic/unpowered/crime/poll) with no test noticing. Needs a pre/post firing-rate comparison on a pinned fixture over 120 rollovers.

GP10b: the ABANDONED row is placed in GROWTH_GATES after BURNING, i.e. BEFORE the shipped UNPOWERED row (sim.js:1131-1136). firstGate is first-match, so on an abandoned dark tile UNPOWERED's apply() no longer runs — the `c.unpow[i]` increment at 1134 stops and the `chance(0.35)` lvl-decay draw at 1135 stops. That is a behavior change to a shipped mechanic, and neither the scope's re-pin note (which mentions only sim.js:4461/4464) nor any gate covers it.

GP10b: the per-district `renewal` boolean is new PERSISTED state (it rides the districts[] round-trip at sim.js:5683 / 5785-5786). Gate 10 asserts sum(aband) === 0 on old saves but never asserts that a pre-GP10b districts[] record loads with the designation defaulting to false, nor that a DESIGNATED district survives serialize -> deserialize -> serialize with the flag and its § charge intact.

GP10a: gate 8 requires serialize -> deserialize -> serialize to be character-identical, but nothing establishes that this property holds on the PRE-GP10a tree. If the shipped round-trip is not already idempotent (key ordering through the Object.assign district restore, float formatting), the gate fails for reasons unrelated to GP10a and will burn a fix cycle. Measure the baseline first and record it.

GP10a: no cost gate on the new O(n) per-rollover sweep, despite distressTick calling trafficNear(i) per tile for the GRIDLOCK cause. The project precedent (recomputeJobAccess's _jaComp/_jaNC caching, explicitly flagged perf-critical) says per-tile rollover passes are cost-sensitive. Gate 2 counts visits but bounds no time.

GP10b: no S4/copy gate on the distress -> abandoned handoff. GP10a ships under an explicit HONESTY CONSTRAINT (no copy may promise abandonment) and GP10b's scope says it 'amends the copy to add the countdown', but no gate asserts the amended advisory text actually renders with the recovery countdown at the shipped surfaces (hover line, query verdict box, almanac) — gate 4 only checks v.evidence on diagnoseTile.
milestones.split_of: GP10 (preflight-authored S3 split, grounded against the live source 2026-07-30)

milestones.title: Abandonment & the Renewal Campaign — the Behavior, Re-Pinned and Measured by GP10a's Ledger
milestones.scope:
Turns GP10a's counter into consequence, and ships the campaign against it in the same half so decline is a decision rather than a punishment.

1. ABANDONMENT. New `this.aband` Uint8 flag plane beside distress (sim.js:1838 idiom, packU8 at sim.js:5734, unpackU8 at sim.js:5916). A zoned tile with `distress[i] >= ABAND_W` flips to aband=1. RESOLVING THE CRIME/CENSUS CONTRADICTION (drift report, mandatory): the tile KEEPS lvl[] — so the derelict sprite has a size and crime does not perversely FALL — and is excluded EXPLICITLY. Census exclusion is ONE predicate in the computeDemandParts loop at sim.js:4152-4166 (the ZR/ZC/ZI arms at 4153-4155); taxes at sim.js:5187 are a pure function of the committed pop/jobs, so that single predicate satisfies census integrity at every downstream surface (HUD, tiers, and the ordinance § bases comJobs/resTiles at sim.js:4206) with no second copy.

2. THE DECLARED RE-PIN. A stopping ABANDONED row in GROWTH_GATES (sim.js:1125+, after BURNING). This is the ONLY way diagnoseTile returns the abandonment verdict as the PRIMARY verdict (an ADVISORY_GATES row can only attach alongside — sim.js:4512-4522), and it is what refuses redevelopment until the recovery window is clear. It necessarily changes which apply() spends this.rng.growth (sim.js:4459-4464) and skips the unpow reset at 4461 and the gridlock draw at 4464. Declared, bounded, and gated: a city that never abandons must still be byte-identical to GP10a.

3. EMISSIONS, all inside recomputeMaps so renewal reverts them free (rebuilt every 14 ticks, sim.js:5444). Pollution: an `if (this.aband[i]) src[i] += ABAND_SMOG;` term in the source loop at sim.js:3663-3681, the exact shape of `if (this.fire[i]) src[i] += 100;` at 3679. Crime: an added blight term in the loop at sim.js:3744-3751 ON TOP of the lvl-derived density at 3746. Land value: a SUBTRACTED term in the FOLD at sim.js:3730-3741 — never a negative seed in the lv[] loop at 3685-3692, because diffuse() clamps into a Uint8Array at sim.js:3768 and erases it. Follow the noiseCov pattern at 3739 exactly, behind an `_abandAny` one-bit memo (the `_noiseAny` idiom at sim.js:1887 / 3724-3728) so a blight-free city pays zero and stays bit-identical.

4. ANTI-CROSSTALK BY EXPLICIT PREDICATE. No new OV id is introduced (abandonment is a flag plane), so the >= OV.ZR auto-join list is discharged by construction — but power demand is NOT: an abandoned tile still matches `t >= OV.ZR` at sim.js:2367-2372 and must be excluded there explicitly, and the fire-candidacy decision must be declared, not defaulted.

5. THE CAMPAIGN — three levers, all priced against real sinks. (a) Per-district renewal designation: a boolean on the districts[] record (newDistrict sim.js:5536-5548), which rides the wholesale serialize at sim.js:5683 and the field-preserving Object.assign restore at sim.js:5785-5786 for FREE — no new plane, only a defensive default for pre-GP10b saves. Charged §/mo as a new `renewal` line on lastBudget (sim.js:5231-5241) and shortens the recovery window inside distressTick's slot. (b) Mass clear-and-rezone: priced against the §100/tile REZONE (COST.zr/zc/zi at sim.js:524), NOT against bulldozing — COST.bulldoze is §1 charged ONCE PER CALL for a whole footprint (sim.js:2313-2323), i.e. effectively free, so 'below individual bulldozing' is not a lever. Must respect anc[] (sim.js:2310-2312) and the M25 peel rule (sim.js:2286-2298). (c) A redevelopment ordinance joining ORDINANCES (sim.js:607-626) — this needs a NEW key in identityOrdMods (sim.js:631-634) AND a new fold branch in recomputeOrdinances (sim.js:4299-4313), because the effect cache is a CLOSED key set and a row with an unknown mods key is silently ignored today.

6. RECOVERY/HYSTERESIS: an abandoned tile needs REVIVE_W consecutive rollovers at distress == 0 (GP10a's counter, already proven honest) before the ABANDONED row stops matching. The designation cuts REVIVE_W.

7. S4: aband tiles suppress night glow via the one-condition change at render.js:1043 and take a boarded draw-time treatment (drawChar precedent, render.js:1074) — NOT a new 9-family x 4-facing x season bake (sprites.js:3965-3981, 4012-4016). A designated renewal district paints visibly back.

8. TEN-SITE AUDIT extended to aband[] at the same ten sites GP10a proved for distress[]. LAUNCH CONDITION (preflight, non-negotiable): the gate problems recorded in preflight_gate_problems below were found by an adversarial reviewer that read the LIVE source and MEASURED the unchanged build. The design phase MUST resolve every one before implementation, and each resolution must be reported in the ship verdict with its measurement. Rules for resolving: an IMPOSSIBILITY (unachievable/self-contradictory/vacuous — the sim arithmetic or the fixture cannot produce the quantity) is corrected by re-specifying the gate so it measures the intended property with a reachable bar, and the correction is recorded with the measurement proving the original was impossible. An ABSOLUTE-SHOULD-BE-COMPARATIVE bar is restated per the R1 protocol (this build vs baseline on identical scripted inputs). An AMBIGUOUS-THRESHOLD gate is pinned to a named city, seed, sample count and reference quantity. An UNMEASURABLE gate is either given a concrete headless observable or reported to the user as needing a design decision. A resolution that changes what the milestone is TRYING TO ACHIEVE (rather than how it is measured) is a DESIGN decision — surface it to the user, never decide it (S6). Also close every missing_coverage item or justify its omission.
milestones.player_facing_win: Neglect finally costs something — a neighbourhood can die and sit as a blighted hole dragging its neighbours down — but the mayor has a renewal campaign to run against it: designate the district, pay the §/mo, mass-rezone the dead blocks, enact the redevelopment ordinance, and watch it paint back faster than waiting ever would.
quality_gates: BOUNDED DECLARED RE-PIN. Against the GP10a baseline, 20 seeds x 600 ticks, Math.random UNSTUBBED: on every seed whose run NEVER reaches ABAND_W, the sim hash (same plane+scalar+cursor definition as GP10a's gate 1) is 0 differing bytes — 100% of non-abandoning seeds. On every seed that DOES abandon, the tick index of the first differing byte is >= the tick index of the first aband[i]=1, asserted per seed. The re-pin is thus provably confined to cities that actually blight; a diff before the first abandonment is a FAIL, not a tolerance.

CAUSATION, MEASURED BY GP10a's LEDGER (spec gate 1, re-grounded). A district cut off from power for 18 consecutive month rollovers has >= 60% of its ZONED footprint abandoned — denominator snapshotted BEFORE the cut, using GP10a's zoned-footprint census, never the developed count (which the existing unpow decay at sim.js:1134-1135 shrinks for unrelated reasons). An identical powered control has EXACTLY 0 abandoned tiles. The report separates aband===1 from merely-decayed (lvl===0 && aband===0) and counts only the former.

HYSTERESIS. Across 20 seeded runs, after power is restored the measured revival latency (first rollover at which aband flips 1→0) is within ±2 rollovers of the designed window REVIVE_W on >= 18 of 20 runs, and EXACTLY 0 tiles revive before rollover REVIVE_W - 2.

CENSUS INTEGRITY. At >= 120 sampled rollovers: city.pop === Σ RES_POP[lvl] over non-abandoned ZR and city.jobs === Σ COM_JOB/IND_JOB over non-abandoned ZC/ZI, exact integer equality, 120 of 120. Flipping ONE developed tile to aband=1 changes pop by exactly -RES_POP[lvl] and the next month's `taxes` by exactly the recomputed value at sim.js:5187 (exact, no tolerance). diagnoseTile returns ABANDONED as the PRIMARY verdict (v.code, not v.advisories) for 100% of 200 sampled abandoned tiles, with the recovery countdown present in v.evidence.

BLIGHT RADIATES. Measured >= 42 ticks (3 full recomputeMaps cycles at the 14-tick cadence, sim.js:5444 — closing the staleness gap the commute series documents at sim.js:5254-5259) after a >= 16-tile cluster abandons: mean landv in the 4-tile annulus around the cluster is >= 15 LOWER than the identical control at the same rollover, and mean crime in the same annulus is >= 10 HIGHER. Both measured on 10 seeded pairs, both bars met on >= 9 of 10.

THE CAMPAIGN BEATS WAITING (S5 outcome gate, comparative, no demand deltas). Two arms from the same blighted save, 10 seeded pairs: the renewal arm (designation funded + mass rezone + ordinance) returns the cluster to within 5% of control mean landv at least 40% FEWER rollovers than the do-nothing arm (>= 9 of 10 pairs), and has >= 25% more developed non-abandoned zoned tiles at rollover 60. The § is REPORTED: lastBudget.renewal is non-zero every month the designation is active and the cumulative charge equals designed §/mo x months within ±1§; the mass-rezone charge equals COST.zr x tiles x the designed discount within ±1§.

CROSSTALK PREDICATES, ASSERTED INDIVIDUALLY. (1) Abandoning N tiles drops this.powerDemand by exactly N at sim.js:2367-2372. (2) The census exclusion at sim.js:4153-4155 fires (covered above but re-asserted here as a site check). (3) The fire-candidacy decision is declared in the scope and the code matches it (boolean). (4) Object.keys(OV).length is UNCHANGED from GP10a (no new over[] id, so the >= OV.ZR auto-join list needs no new predicates). (5) The redevelopment ordinance's new mods key appears in identityOrdMods() and ordMods carries the designed value when enacted-and-unlocked and the identity value otherwise — a silently-ignored unknown key is a FAIL. 5 assertions, 5 pass, each named in the report.

S4 COHERENCE. Abandoned tiles are pairwise visually distinct from healthy AND from all three GP10a distress bands at cam.r = 0,1,2,3 (4 states x 4 rotations, every pair >= 2% tile pixel diff). An abandoned tile contributes ZERO to the night layer (sampled night-layer pixel sum over the tile is 0 while a matched powered healthy tile is > 0) at all 4 rotations. A designated renewal district renders a distinct marker at all 4 rotations. Zero assertions waived.

SPIRAL SURVIVABLE — RE-SPECIFIED, COMPARATIVE (see rationale; the original clause is unmeasurable). From a pinned scripted worst case (power loss → revenue hole → service cuts), the identical scripted recovery returns the city to positive monthly net AND rising pop within 60 rollovers on THIS build in >= 8 of 10 seeded runs, AND this build's success count is >= the pinned pre-GP10 baseline's success count on the SAME script and seeds (no regression). The 'GP7 assessed-value floor observed to bind' clause is DROPPED and reported to the user, not amended by the worker (S6).

SAVE-COMPAT / DETERMINISM / SCENARIOS. Ladder integer = GP10a's version + 1, read live at launch, appended after GP10a's last key, defensive typeof/Array.isArray guards, no version-equality test. Every earlier save (v17 through GP10a) loads with sum(aband) === 0 and no retroactive blight. Round-trip is idempotent (character-identical re-serialize). A loaded healthy city's next 120 rollovers match a native equivalent byte-for-byte (0 differing bytes). Same seed + script reproduces identical aband[] evolution over 600 ticks with Math.random UNSTUBBED, 3 runs. R1 COMPARATIVE: all 5 scenarios run their pinned scripted solutions on THIS build and on the pinned baseline — every scenario that WINS on baseline also wins here (0 regressions); an absolute 'wins N of 10' bar is explicitly NOT used. Zero console errors.
milestones.split_rationale: Everything here is behavior, and every number it claims is read off the instrument GP10a already proved honest — which is the whole point of the S3 order. The half is dominated by two risks that only a behavior half can carry. First, the declared re-pin: making ABANDONED the primary tile verdict and a growth refusal REQUIRES a GROWTH_GATES row, and any matching row there changes which apply() spends this.rng.growth. The drift report shows the ADVISORY route cannot satisfy the original gate wording because advisories attach alongside, never replace, the primary verdict — so the re-pin is unavoidable and must be declared, not discovered. Gate 1 makes it bounded and falsifiable rather than a blanket amnesty: a non-abandoning city stays byte-identical, and divergence must begin at the first abandonment. Second, the crime/census contradiction: the spec asks for an abandoned tile to contribute zero pop/jobs/tax AND emit crime, but crime's source is lvl-derived (density = lvl*40 for ZR/ZC, lvl*20 for ZI at sim.js:3746), so a lvl-zeroed tile emits LESS crime. This half picks keep-lvl + explicit census predicate and patches the other side, per the drift report's instruction to pick one and patch explicitly. Two gates are re-specified rather than inherited, and both are reported for the user rather than silently amended (S6). (a) The original spiral gate requires 'GP7's assessed-value floor observed to bind', but live revenue is the headcount formula at sim.js:5187 with no floor, deptCosts returns exactly eight fixed lines (sim.js:4927-4943), funding has exactly six levers (sim.js:1992), and GP7's own gate 3 permits shipping ONE rate without guaranteeing a floor — the clause is unmeasurable today, so it is dropped and the gate made comparative-vs-baseline instead. If GP7b actually ships a floor before this half launches, re-add the floor clause as a separate gate rather than folding it back in. (b) 'All 5 scenarios remain winnable' is made comparative per R1, since an absolute bar was already ruled mis-specified once on this project. The cost model is also corrected at source: 'priced below individual bulldozing' is meaningless because COST.bulldoze is §1 charged once per whole building, so the § lever is the §100/tile rezone — otherwise gate 6's '§ cost' would measure noise.
milestones.save_version_plan: DO NOT HARDCODE. The ladder reads v17 TODAY (sim.js:5652 `v: 17`), but GP10 is LAST in .execution_order behind GP7b, GP8b and GP9 — and the roadmap marks all three touches_save_format:true. GP10 is only v18 if all three slip. RULE FOR BOTH HALVES: at launch, read the live `v:` integer literal at sim.js:5652 and take LIVE+1; GP10b then takes GP10a's shipped version +1. Two halves = two ladder integers (GP10a adds distress[]/distressCause[]/history.blight; GP10b adds aband[] and the per-district renewal flag). Mechanics, identical in both halves: (1) APPEND new keys strictly after the last existing key — today sim.js:5745 `recallDone` — so the earlier-version prefix stays character-stable; (2) guard every read with typeof / Array.isArray and NEVER a version-equality test anywhere in deserialize (the shipped GP3b/GP5b/GP6 comments at sim.js:5736-5746 and 5916-5926 are the pattern); (3) the two Uint8 planes go through packU8/unpackU8 (sim.js:36-60) alongside sim.js:5734 `traffic/unpow/fire` and restore beside sim.js:5916 `unpackU8(d.unpow, c.unpow);` — unpackU8 already rejects malformed packs and leaves `out` untouched, so an older save lands all-zero with no retroactive blight; (4) the per-district renewal designation needs NO new array and NO new save key — it rides the districts[] object round-trip (serialize sim.js:5683, field-preserving Object.assign restore sim.js:5785-5786) and needs only a defensive default; (5) `history.blight` is added ONCE, in GP10a, to BOTH hardcoded key lists — normaliseHistory at sim.js:31 AND its mirror in collectBudget's >240 trim loop at sim.js:5274 — so GP10b adds no history series at all. Both halves gate on an idempotent serialize→deserialize→serialize round-trip and on every earlier version loading clean.
milestones.launch_order_note: GP10a ships FIRST and alone. It is independently shippable per S8 (a mayor who stops there gets a real diagnostic layer: causes, month counts, a Blight minimap, district and almanac readouts, and a complaint that jumps the camera), and it is decidably safe because it can only write its own two planes — the byte-identical gate is a hash comparison, not an argument. GP10a must land the FIXED SWEEP SLOT (tick()'s %24 block, after approvalTick at sim.js:5499, before collectBudget at sim.js:5500), the ZONED-FOOTPRINT DENOMINATOR (the approvalCensus discipline at sim.js:5082-5099 that the measured self-healing bug at sim.js:5049-5059 forced), the TEN-SITE CLEAR AUDIT, and the BOTH-HISTORY-LISTS extension — every one of those is a known-expensive mistake, and in the read half a mistake costs a re-run rather than a re-pin. GP10b then re-pins against GP10a's pinned hash and is measured entirely by GP10a's counter. GP10a has NO dependency on GP7b/GP8b/GP9 and can launch the moment those three either land or are deferred — it only needs the live ladder integer at launch. GP10b has one real sequencing question and it is already resolved in its gates: the original spiral gate's dependence on GP7's assessed-value floor is DROPPED (the floor does not exist — sim.js:5187 is the headcount formula, sim.js:4927-4943 is eight fixed dept lines, sim.js:1992 is six funding levers, and GP7 status is still 'todo'), replaced by a comparative-vs-baseline survivability gate. If GP7b ships a real assessed-value floor before GP10b launches, ADD the floor clause back as a separate gate — do not fold it into the survivability gate, and never let the implementing worker amend it (S6). Two items to escalate to the user at GP10b launch rather than resolve in implementation: the declared re-pin (authorized here, bounded by gate 1) and the fire-candidacy decision for abandoned tiles (declare it in design; it is a crosstalk assertion, not an implementation detail).

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 5 (BLIGHT RADIATES) — crime clause
preflight_gate_problems.problem: "mean crime in the 4-tile annulus is >= 10 HIGHER than control" is unreachable under the scope's own design. Crime is NEVER diffused: the only diffuse() calls in recomputeMaps are poll (sim.js:3681), land value (3694) and traffic (3700). Crime is a pure per-tile formula, `density - polCov - landv*0.2 - ordMods.crimeCut` (sim.js:3746-3748). The scope puts the blight crime term inside that per-tile loop gated on aband[i], so a NON-abandoned annulus tile receives blight crime only through the landv channel at coefficient 0.2 — a +10 crime annulus requires a -50 landv annulus, i.e. more than three times the gate's own -15 landv bar. No constant choice fixes this; the term simply does not reach the annulus.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Split the measurement to match where each term actually applies: measure crime ON the abandoned cluster tiles (where the added term lives) and landv on the annulus (which the diffused pollution channel does reach). If crime is genuinely meant to radiate, that is a SCOPE change — seed a diffused blight source in the source loop at sim.js:3663-3681 (the `if (this.fire[i]) src[i] += 100` idiom) feeding a diffused plane, and re-derive the annulus bar from the diffusion kernel rather than asserting a number.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 3 (COUNTER EXACTNESS) — the 168/544 = 0.309 clause
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The gate hardcodes "distressShare holds constant at 168/544 = 0.309", citing sim.js:5049-5059. Two problems. (1) WRONG METRIC: those numbers are unpowShare (zoned tiles that are dark), recorded in prose at sim.js:1590-1592 and 5054-5057. distressShare counts ALL FOUR causes, so it is >= unpowShare by construction — cutting power to a third of the city also crashes sector demand, so SLUMP fires on tiles DARK does not cover and the share cannot equal 0.309. (2) NO FIXTURE: repo-wide, 544/168/0.309 appear ONLY inside those two comments. There is no committed script or save that reproduces that city, and it was measured on a build that HAD abandonment (that is the bug the comment describes) — a build GP10a by definition is not. The literal is not reproducible.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Make it a co-measurement instead of a literal. (a) distressShare must be NON-DECREASING across 24 consecutive rollovers with the wire still cut — the actual anti-self-healing property. (b) The DARK-cause subset count (tiles with distressCause === DARK+1) must equal approvalCensus's live zUnpow on the same city at the same rollover, exact integer equality, every rollover — this proves the shared denominator without importing a number. (c) If a fixed number is wanted, commit the scripted city as a fixture and re-measure it on the GP10a build first.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 3 (HYSTERESIS)
preflight_gate_problems.problem: Scope §6 defines revival as "an abandoned tile needs REVIVE_W consecutive rollovers at distress == 0 before the ABANDONED row stops matching." The gate then measures revival latency against REVIVE_W with a ±2 tolerance on >= 18 of 20 runs, plus "EXACTLY 0 tiles revive before rollover REVIVE_W - 2". Both clauses are true by construction — the latency IS REVIVE_W, exactly, because a counter is being compared to its own constant. The gate tests that a decrement works, and the ±2/18-of-20 statistics create the false impression that something stochastic is being measured. It cannot fail without the feature being outright broken.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Replace with the exact identity (latency === REVIVE_W on 20 of 20, zero tolerance — cheaper and strictly stronger), and move the real content into a comparative assertion the constant does NOT trivially satisfy: a DESIGNATED renewal district's revival latency is shorter than an undesignated one by exactly the designed reduction, on the same seed and the same cluster, 10 of 10 pairs. Also assert the distress counter is genuinely re-armed — a tile that hits distress > 0 mid-window restarts at 0, it does not resume.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 4 (CAUSE ATTRIBUTION IS EXACT)
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The two clauses cannot both be met with the stated tolerance. Every tile with distress[i] > 0 got there because SOME DISTRESS_CAUSES row matched (first-match, scope §3), so its distressCause is necessarily one of the four rows. If "each of the other 3 rows [is reported] on 0 tiles", then the target row is on 100% of distressed tiles — the ">= 95%" allowance is unusable. An implementer who measures 96% has already failed the second clause, and will not know which clause is the real bar. This is the same shape as the y=12/y=9/y=15 incident: the fixture described cannot produce the quantity measured.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Pick one bar. Either: "100% of distressed tiles report the target row and the other 3 rows appear on 0 tiles" (clean, and what the fixture actually implies); or, if the single-cause city cannot be made that clean, ">= 95% report the target row, and the report ENUMERATES the residual <= 5% by cause with a stated reason" — dropping the 0-tiles clause. Do not ship both.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 7 (CROSSTALK PREDICATES) assertion 1
preflight_gate_problems.problem: "Abandoning N tiles drops this.powerDemand by exactly N at sim.js:2367-2372" is false in the scenario that produces abandonment. The loop counts `if (this.powered[i] && t >= OV.ZR && ...) demand++` — a tile only contributes when it is POWERED. The primary abandonment path in this milestone is DARK (unpowered for ABAND_W rollovers), and those tiles already contribute 0, so the drop is 0, not N. The assertion is additionally perturbed by the `pdMult` activeMods multiplier and `powerTradeDelta` immediately below (sim.js:2374-2382), either of which breaks exact-N.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the precondition in the gate: run the assertion on a POWERED abandonment path (a CRIME- or SLUMP-caused cluster), with no `powerDemand` activeMod (pdMult === 1) and no regional power trade open, then assert the exact -N drop. Separately assert the DARK case explicitly reads -0 so the null result is recorded rather than mistaken for a bug.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 9 (SPIRAL SURVIVABLE)
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The re-specification correctly drops the GP7 floor clause and adds a comparative clause, but it LEAVES an absolute bar in front of it: "returns the city to positive monthly net AND rising pop within 60 rollovers on THIS build in >= 8 of 10 seeded runs". That is the exact shape of incident 1 ("wins the medal in >= 8 of 10"). It is also the clause most likely to fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the work: GP10b ADDS decline pressure (ABAND_SMOG pollution, blight crime, a landv subtraction, and the census exclusion removing taxable pop), so the absolute success count can legitimately fall below 8 while the comparative clause — the one that actually tests for regression — passes cleanly. Secondly, "rising pop" has no definition: rising measured over what window, against what point?
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Keep only the comparative clause: this build's success count >= the pinned pre-GP10 baseline's on the SAME script and seeds, with the per-seed outcomes tabulated. Report the absolute count as an OBSERVATION, not a bar. Define the success predicate concretely, e.g. "monthly net > 0 at rollover 60 AND pop at rollover 60 > pop at the trough rollover" — a single unambiguous headless read.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 1 (BOUNDED DECLARED RE-PIN)
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The gate's interesting half will almost certainly never execute. 600 ticks is 25 month rollovers (tick()'s %24 block, sim.js:5492). Reaching aband requires ABAND_W CONSECUTIVE distressed rollovers on top of the time to develop the city, so a normal scripted build on 20 seeds will very likely produce ZERO abandoning seeds. The gate then reads 20/20 byte-identical and PASSES, with the "first differing byte >= first aband[i]=1" clause — the entire point of the bounded re-pin — never exercised on a single seed. Nothing in the gate requires that any seed abandon.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Add a coverage precondition and make it a failure condition: the 20-seed script must include a deliberately sabotaged arm (power cut / service collapse) such that >= 6 of 20 seeds actually reach aband, and the gate FAILS if fewer than that number exercise the divergence clause. Report the abandoning-seed count in the results. Consider extending the horizon past 600 ticks for the sabotaged arm so ABAND_W + development time fits.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 2 (CAUSATION) — the 18-rollover / 60% bar
preflight_gate_problems.problem: ABAND_W is never given a value anywhere in the split spec, yet the gate hardcodes 18 rollovers and 60%. If ABAND_W > 18 the result is 0% by construction and the gate is unreachable. Worse, the denominator is ambiguous in a way that swings the answer from ~0% to ~100%: scope §1 says "a zoned tile with distress[i] >= ABAND_W flips to aband=1" with NO lvl guard, and scope §3 walks DISTRESS_CAUSES on any ZR/ZC/ZI tile regardless of level — so EMPTY zoned lots accumulate distress and abandon too, making >= 60% of the zoned footprint trivial. That directly contradicts two other statements: §1's "the tile KEEPS lvl[] so the derelict sprite has a size" (a lvl-0 abandoned tile has no size), and this gate's own separation clause "separates aband===1 from merely-decayed (lvl===0 && aband===0)", which presumes lvl-0 tiles do NOT abandon.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Declare ABAND_W in the scope and require 18 > ABAND_W with stated margin. Declare explicitly whether abandonment requires lvl > 0 (the derelict-sprite and separation clauses both imply it does). Then re-express the bar over the subset the answer is actually about: >= 60% of tiles that were DEVELOPED (lvl > 0) in the pre-cut snapshot, with the zoned footprint reported alongside as the stable denominator.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 6 (THE CAMPAIGN BEATS WAITING) — the 40%-fewer-rollovers clause
