preflight_gate_problems.problem: "returns the cluster to within 5% of control mean landv at least 40% FEWER rollovers than the do-nothing arm" has no horizon and no censoring rule. The do-nothing arm is a blighted cluster with an abandonment feedback loop — the expected outcome is that it NEVER returns to within 5% of control. When the denominator is infinite/undefined the ratio is undefined and the gate can be neither passed nor failed honestly, which is precisely the condition under which an implementer quietly reinterprets the bar. (The second clause, ">= 25% more developed non-abandoned zoned tiles at rollover 60", is sound — it has a horizon.)
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Fix a horizon H (rollover 120 is consistent with the rest of the split) and define non-recovery as censored-at-H. Score the pair as a success when EITHER the renewal arm recovers by H and the do-nothing arm does not, OR both recover and the renewal arm's rollover count is <= 60% of the do-nothing arm's. Require >= 9 of 10 pairs and report the censoring split so "9 of 10 by censoring alone" is visible rather than hidden.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 5 (LEGIBILITY) — the distress complaint clause
preflight_gate_problems.problem: scanComplaints (sim.js:5314-5347) is a CITYWIDE winner-take-all argmax that emits at most one complaint per COMPLAINT_EVERY (= 3) rollovers. The shipped scores are flat: rubble 130, unpowered 150, traffic 60+excess, crime 40+excess, poll 40+excess. The natural way to produce "a district reaching >= 10 distressed tiles" is the DARK cause — which means >= 10 developed unpowered tiles, each scoring a flat 150. Unless the new distress kind scores ABOVE 150, no distress complaint can ever fire in that scenario, and the "within 2*COMPLAINT_EVERY rollovers" window contains at most two emission opportunities. If the implementer does score it above 150, the shipped unpowered and rubble complaints are starved — a regression the gate does not measure.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the distress kind's score RANK relative to the five existing kinds explicitly in the scope (it is a design decision, not an implementation detail). Run the timing assertion on a CRIME- or SLUMP-caused fixture where no higher-scoring kind co-occurs. Add a companion anti-crosstalk assertion: on a pinned pre-GP10a fixture, each of the five existing complaint kinds fires at its pre-GP10a rate over 120 rollovers.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 4 (CENSUS INTEGRITY) — the pop/jobs identity
preflight_gate_problems.problem: "city.pop === Σ RES_POP[lvl] over non-abandoned ZR and city.jobs === Σ COM_JOB/IND_JOB over non-abandoned ZC/ZI" is not the identity the code implements. computeDemandParts (sim.js:4163) also folds arcology contributions into the SAME totals: `else if (isArco(this.over[i]) && this.anc[i] === i) { pop += ARCO_POP[...]; iJobs += ARCO_JOB[...]; }` — a single Launch Arco adds 3000 pop. The stated identity therefore holds only on a city with no arcologies, i.e. it is an identity that passes on the toy fixture and silently stops being true on a real Megalopolis-tier city — exactly the failure mode this review is meant to catch. As written it could also produce a false FAIL if the harness happens to build one.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: State the full identity: pop === Σ RES_POP[lvl] over non-abandoned ZR + Σ ARCO_POP over arco anchors (anc === i), and the matching jobs form including ARCO_JOB. Then run it on a fixture that DOES contain at least one arcology, so the arco term is actually exercised rather than assumed absent.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 6 (S4 VISIBILITY) — the reference block
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The gate diffs a distressed block "against a pixel-identical healthy block". No such reference block can be constructed. Sprite variants are seeded per tile at growth time (`c.varnt[i] = rg.pick(5)` at sim.js:1115 and 1119) and at build time (sim.js:2270), terrain variants are seeded at generation (sim.js:2131-2132), and tiles are further differentiated by land value, pollution and neighbour context. Two distinct blocks on the same map are essentially never pixel-identical, so the gate has no constructible control and the implementer has no way to know whether a 2% diff came from the distress treatment or from varnt.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Diff the SAME tile against itself: capture at distress[i] = 0, then write the band value directly into the plane, re-render with camera, tick, funds and every other input held fixed, and diff. Repeat at cam.r = 0,1,2,3. That isolates the treatment exactly and needs no reference block. Keep the >= 2% threshold and the pairwise-band structure unchanged.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10a gate 7 (TEN-SITE CLEAR DISCIPLINE)
preflight_gate_problems.problem: "fire that site on a tile carrying distress >= 5" cannot be satisfied naturally at the road-crumble site (sim.js:3615). roadWearTick only touches OV.ROAD / OV.WIREROAD tiles, and distress is written ONLY on ZR/ZC/ZI (scope §3). The only route from a zoned tile to a road tile is place(), which passes through the footprint site at sim.js:2266 — a site this same gate requires to clear the planes. So no road tile can ever carry distress >= 5, and the precondition for that site is unconstructible. The gate reads as though all ten preconditions are naturally reachable, which will send an implementer hunting for a state that does not exist.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Say plainly that the harness WRITES distress[i] = 5 and distressCause[i] = k directly into the planes immediately before firing each site — this is a defence-in-depth clear test, not a reachability test. Additionally mark which of the ten sites are naturally reachable from a distressed zoned tile (2266, 2315, 4542, 4718, 4744, 4778, 4806, 4829, 2249) and which are defensive-only (3615), so a future reader does not mistake the defensive ones for live paths.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10a scope §6 band thresholds (>= 6 / >= 12) vs GP10b gate 8
preflight_gate_problems.problem: GP10a pins the three visual bands at healthy / >= 6 / >= 12 and gates on them. ABAND_W is never assigned a value anywhere in the split. If ABAND_W <= 12, a tile flips to aband before it can be observed in the "critical" band, so once GP10b lands the critical band is unreachable state — and GP10b gate 8's requirement that abandoned tiles be "pairwise visually distinct from healthy AND from all three GP10a distress bands" contains a term that cannot be instantiated on a live city. The two halves' constants are coupled but only one of them is written down.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Pin ABAND_W in GP10a's scope (not GP10b's) with ABAND_W > 12 and stated margin, OR define the bands as fractions of ABAND_W (e.g. >= ABAND_W/3 and >= 2*ABAND_W/3) so the two halves cannot drift apart. Then GP10b gate 8 can name the exact distress value it forces to observe each band.

preflight_gate_problems.gate: GP10b gate 5 (BLIGHT RADIATES) — the -15 landv magnitude
preflight_gate_problems.problem: The -15 annulus landv bar is an absolute magnitude that was not derived from the code path that has to produce it. Scope §3 deliberately forbids seeding the blight penalty into lv[] (correctly — diffuse() clamps into a Uint8Array at sim.js:3768), so the fold term at 3730-3741 applies only to the abandoned tile itself. The ONLY radiating channel left into the annulus is `- this.poll[i] * 0.7` in the fold, meaning a -15 annulus mean requires roughly +21 diffused pollution there. Given diffuse(src, poll, 3, 0.24) over a 16-tile cluster, that implies an ABAND_SMOG well above the fire term's `src[i] += 100` (sim.js:3679). No pilot measurement is cited, so the bar may be reachable only with a constant that visibly outweighs an active fire.
preflight_gate_problems.suggested_reformulation: Run a one-off pilot (place a 16-tile abandoned cluster, sweep ABAND_SMOG, read the annulus mean at +42 ticks) and PIN the bar to what the kernel actually yields at a defensible constant. Until then state it comparatively and directionally — "annulus mean landv is strictly lower than the matched control on >= 9 of 10 pairs, with the measured delta reported" — and add the magnitude bar once the pilot number exists.

preflight_missing_coverage: GP10b: the >= OV.ZR auto-join list is only PARTIALLY discharged. sim.js:347 enumerates the idiom sites as conducts / seed / demand / BROWNOUT / Y2K, and the live sites are demand (2370), brownout (2394), y2k (2410) and fire candidacy (4599). Scope §4 declares only demand + fire candidacy, and gate 7 asserts only those two. Nothing declares or asserts whether an abandoned tile is a brownout victim or a y2k victim — both read `this.powered[i] && t >= OV.ZR` and both will silently include abandoned tiles by default.

GP10a: no anti-crosstalk gate on the new `distress` complaint kind. scanComplaints (sim.js:5314-5347) is a single-winner citywide argmax with one emission per COMPLAINT_EVERY, so adding a kind can starve the five shipped kinds (rubble/traffic/unpowered/crime/poll) with no test noticing. Needs a pre/post firing-rate comparison on a pinned fixture over 120 rollovers.

GP10b: the ABANDONED row is placed in GROWTH_GATES after BURNING, i.e. BEFORE the shipped UNPOWERED row (sim.js:1131-1136). firstGate is first-match, so on an abandoned dark tile UNPOWERED's apply() no longer runs — the `c.unpow[i]` increment at 1134 stops and the `chance(0.35)` lvl-decay draw at 1135 stops. That is a behavior change to a shipped mechanic, and neither the scope's re-pin note (which mentions only sim.js:4461/4464) nor any gate covers it.

GP10b: the per-district `renewal` boolean is new PERSISTED state (it rides the districts[] round-trip at sim.js:5683 / 5785-5786). Gate 10 asserts sum(aband) === 0 on old saves but never asserts that a pre-GP10b districts[] record loads with the designation defaulting to false, nor that a DESIGNATED district survives serialize -> deserialize -> serialize with the flag and its § charge intact.

GP10a: gate 8 requires serialize -> deserialize -> serialize to be character-identical, but nothing establishes that this property holds on the PRE-GP10a tree. If the shipped round-trip is not already idempotent (key ordering through the Object.assign district restore, float formatting), the gate fails for reasons unrelated to GP10a and will burn a fix cycle. Measure the baseline first and record it.

GP10a: no cost gate on the new O(n) per-rollover sweep, despite distressTick calling trafficNear(i) per tile for the GRIDLOCK cause. The project precedent (recomputeJobAccess's _jaComp/_jaNC caching, explicitly flagged perf-critical) says per-tile rollover passes are cost-sensitive. Gate 2 counts visits but bounds no time.

GP10b: no S4/copy gate on the distress -> abandoned handoff. GP10a ships under an explicit HONESTY CONSTRAINT (no copy may promise abandonment) and GP10b's scope says it 'amends the copy to add the countdown', but no gate asserts the amended advisory text actually renders with the recovery countdown at the shipped surfaces (hover line, query verdict box, almanac) — gate 4 only checks v.evidence on diagnoseTile.
milestones.split_of: GP10 (preflight-authored S3 split, grounded against the live source 2026-07-30)

reconcile_changelog: ADDED A MILESTONE THAT DID NOT EXIST: Expressways, Ramps & the First Moving Train (now rank 4). The fun lens's strongest finding was that the draft added exactly two buildable things (landfill, incinerator) against four new friction systems, and that the commute milestone creates a bottleneck problem while its own scope defers the only tool that answers it. A road class hierarchy with ramps and a real siting penalty is the SC2K layout dilemma; the animated train closes the aliveness guard's 'N/A until a train ships' slot. This is the one new toy in ranks 1-4.

DROPPED 'Offers & Ultimatums' (old GP9) entirely to make room. Three grounds, all verified: the Federal Prison is a placeable building smuggled into an events table (recomputeDemand consumes only additive demandR/C/I types at sim.js:1509-1513 — there is no spatial modifier channel), full-information binary modals are solved once and become autopilot forever after, and it hard-depended on the ports milestone. Its best idea (state-triggered rather than calendar-triggered pressure) is preserved in the hazard vector's coupling to live state.

PROMOTED the seeded RNG stream from 'a prerequisite milestone the roadmap does not contain' into rank 1 alongside the verdict engine — same surgery, same function. Verified the panel's load-bearing falsehood claim: 46 raw Math.random() calls in js/sim.js cover the whole tick path (growth sampling and rolls, traffic reservoir picks at 1267, road wear 1318, fire spread 1774/1786, disaster roll 2385) while mulberry32 (sim.js:463) serves only terrain and neighbor personalities. Every 'byte-identical' gate in the draft inherited that fragility. Rank 1 now declares the ONE authorized re-pin and makes every later identity gate mean something.

RESTRUCTURED rank 1 from a hard-coded seven-code enumeration into a DECLARATIVE GATE TABLE that growthPass itself consumes. The fun lens showed diagnoseTile would otherwise be rewritten three times (strain gate, job-reach gate, abandoned state), invalidating its own gate each time. Now a new gate cannot ship without its verdict, and three later milestones get their tile verdicts for free.

FIXED the rank-1 verdict set: added the burning-tile check (sim.js:1682, precedes everything), the demand-below-0.15 threshold (sim.js:1701 — the commonest real stall, previously reported as 'growing normally'), and the negligible-fit-odds code (sim.js:1704-1712; a headless rig showed demand.r at 0.78-1.00 with pop flat, i.e. fit was binding, not the enumerated gates). Corrected the water cap's precedence — it fires at lvl >= 1, so it pre-empts the level-2 service cap. Replaced the self-referential '7/7 codes' gate with a differential fuzz against an instrumented growthPass.

CORRECTED the rank-1 drag premise: drags do NOT truncate silently — place() returns {ok:false,reason:'funds'} (sim.js:764) and applyToolAt already plays Snd.denied() with '⛔ Not enough funds!' (ui.js:614). The meter is now a preview that must not be stricter than the budget, since collectBudget can legitimately push funds negative. Also gave the hover readout its own status cell with a message TTL, because a per-pixel mousemove into #sb-tool (index.html:122) would erase transient warnings before they are read.

ADDED RCI decomposition to rank 1. The feedback pass bar demands gauges decompose into named signed contributors; demand.r is literally a sum of six named terms sitting in recomputeDemand (sim.js:1503-1520) and nothing in the draft exposed them. Cheap, and it closes a self-declared pass bar the draft left unmet.

PROMOTED Working Ports 4 -> 2. All three lenses independently asked for this. sim.js:55-64 documents in the code's own words that AIRPORT and SEAPORT 'deliberately join NO predicate — behaves exactly like OV.STADIUM'. Dead content on the two most expensive buildings is bug-shaped work and outranks new systems under a cap. Effort re-rated 2 -> 3 for the directional noise map.

PROMOTED Commute & Job Access 7 -> 3, splitting the difference between the fun lens (rank 2) and the two lenses that wanted it held back. It is the only milestone delivering the north star's central claim, and shipping it before the strain/blight/tax work means those are written once against the final growth model instead of three times against a doomed one. Fixed two defects: the strictly-downhill walk would collapse all trips onto one canonical corridor (now weighted among equal-or-lower neighbours from the seeded stream, with a non-degeneracy gate), and 'C/I trips keep the legacy walk so the change stays surgical' was false pre-rank-1 because both drew from the same interleaved global stream.

DEMOTED Assessed-Value Taxation 2 -> 7 on unanimous panel advice, and corrected its diagnosis. sim.js:1503 is `taxMod = (7 - this.taxRate) * 0.05` — strictly LINEAR, not the 'flat-then-cliff' the draft described. A headless R-heavy rig already produces a single-peaked curve peaking at 7% that would PASS the draft's own Laffer gate on HEAD; only a serviced balanced rig shows the degenerate 'set 13% and win'. The milestone now leads with a measurement spike on a PINNED reference city and will ship one rate rather than three fake ones if equilibrium separability fails through the jobsAvail chain.

GAVE THE DEATH SPIRAL AN OWNER. Four milestones (assessed-value tax, blight, approval, hazard) closed a positive-feedback loop nobody stabilized. The taxation milestone now owns an assessed-value floor, an urban-renewal budget line, and the real debt ladder the economy pass bar demands (BOND_PRINCIPAL/BOND_TERM/BOND_MAX are fixed constants at sim.js:2058) — plus consumption-scaled upkeep, without which assessed revenue would hand an established city a permanent unattended surplus and regress that pass bar.

ADDED THE MISSING PROGRESSION RUNG to the approval milestone. TIERS (sim.js:236-242) is five raw population thresholds topping out at Metropolis/5000 and no milestone in the draft touched it, so economy-progression could not reach its own pass bar. Megalopolis is now gated on population AND sustained approval AND a commute/pollution condition — earned by governing, not by zoning.

ADDED THE EDUCATION PAYOFF to the service-strain milestone, converting it from a pure cost increase into an investment. Verified sim.js:1392 and 1709 SUM eduCov and medCov and 1721 ORs them, so per-department capacity alone could not meet the 'education and health are mechanically distinct with different payoffs' pass bar. Education now accumulates a decade-scale eduLevel stock gating a clean/high-tech industry mix — also satisfying simulation-depth's 'slow stock' requirement.

CUT THE DEMAND DAMPER from the approval milestone and moved riot coupling to the hazard milestone. Crime, pollution, tax and coverage already suppress growth through landv and fit; damping demand.r on top double-charges the same neglect and muddies the causal chain the milestone exists to clarify. Also resolved its two self-contradictions: the EMA is path-dependent by construction so the 'pure function of serialized state' gate is gone, and 'simulates identically outside the approval channel' was impossible while approval fed back into the sim.

RESOLVED THE VERSION COLLISION. Six milestones each independently declared 'save v12' with 'v11 loads'. Rank 1 now owns v12 and establishes an explicit ladder: every later state-adding milestone takes the next integer and the loader maintains a v11..vN migration chain. Under a stop-anywhere cap the ladder rule holds regardless of which milestones actually ship.

FIXED normaliseHistory EVERYWHERE. Verified sim.js:16-22 builds a fresh object from a hardcoded 7-key list and DROPS unknown keys — the draft's claims that it 'already tolerates the new key' were wrong in the direction that silently destroys an approval or commute series on every load. Both milestones adding a series now name the edit and gate on a round-trip with zero dropped points.

SPLIT AND RE-RATED the civil-defense milestone (effort 4 -> 5, three phases with phase 1 shippable alone) and fixed its broken serialization claim. startDisaster('fire') (sim.js:1798-1811) ignites and RETURNS without ever setting this.disaster — fire is 55% of the roll — and fire[] is not in serialize() at all, so saving mid-fire already silently loses the fire. The roster cannot ride inside this.disaster; fire[] and the roster are serialized and the mid-fire save loss is fixed as a bonus. Phase 1 is the two shipped defects (four disasters unreachable from MENUS.disasters at ui.js:322, hardcoded 'tornado' pressure at scenarios.js:362) plus a real scenario difficulty axis.

PRICED THE OV-ID CROSSTALK into the waste milestone (effort 3 -> 4) and applied the same audit to the new expressway ids. 'over[] is a Uint8Array so new ids round-trip for free' is true for SAVE and false for SIM: any id >= OV.ZR joins recomputePower's conducts (905), brownout (924) and y2k (939) idioms and the fire-candidate scan (1803) — a paint-style landfill would conduct electricity across itself and be flammable. Both milestones now carry an explicit predicate task following the isWaterOv/isMega precedent documented at sim.js:106-114, plus the ovName extension at ui.js:1523, and the waste milestone must decide the powerMix sixth-bucket question rather than assume the isPlant() path is free (it breaks the documented Σ === powerSupply contract at sim.js:1050-1065).

REWROTE the blight milestone (demoted to 10, effort 3 -> 4). Its counting substrate did not exist — unpow[] rides a 340-random-tile sampler giving ~1.27 Poisson samples per tile per month, so a consecutive-months counter cannot ride it; it now specifies a deterministic O(n) monthly sweep. And it shipped punishment with no decision ('a real campaign' that was actually a cooldown), so the renewal tools now ship with it and its gates prove the spiral is survivable rather than merely that it exists.

REPLACED the vacuous identity gate in the service milestone. At school ~500 / hospital ~800 / police ~1200 / fire ~1500, any baseline city large enough to be interesting is already strained, so 'byte-identical wherever capacity >= load' only held for toy cities. Now an explicit bounded re-pin plus a strain===1.0 fast-path assertion.

ADDED A SCENARIO-WINNABILITY GATE to every growth-touching milestone. Nothing in the draft checked this, yet the tax reshape, service strain, commute gating and blight each independently suppress equilibrium growth and stack multiplicatively — while Twister Season requires pop >= 4000 and Y2K Ready 2500 pop + §4000 + a power margin, and medals persist across cities in localStorage (recordTrophy, scenarios.js:307), making previously earned golds unreproducible.

FIXED FACTUAL ERRORS: the commute perf gate cited 'a fully built 120x120 map' — MAP_SIZES is [64, 80, 128] (sim.js:7), now 128x128. process_scaffolding: S1 BASELINE LEDGER: every commit that changes what is live in the tree updates baseline_ledger in the same commit. A workflow brief always quotes the ledger, never memory.

S2 TWO-STRIKE SPLIT: a milestone refuted twice is never attempted a third time whole — it is split (read-surfaces half vs behavior half) or blocked for a user decision. Splitting GP1 is what made GP1a byte-identical-provable.

S3 READ-FIRST SPLITS: instrumentation and player-facing readouts ship BEFORE the behavior they describe. The read half carries a byte-identical gate; the behavior half re-pins against it and is measured by the instrumentation the read half proved honest.

S4 SIM-ART COHERENCE (the SC2K bar): every new sim state must have a visible expression, consistent at all 4 rotations, and every failure state must be visually distinct from its working state. In actual SimCity 2000 nothing invisible ever bills the player. (Lesson: dead port identical to a working one; noise cone perpendicular to the drawn runway.)

S5 OUTCOME GATES FOR THE ECONOMY: never gate on instantaneous demand deltas — demand is a self-correcting pressure signal, so an additive bonus is absorbed into growth. Gate on OUTCOMES over a horizon vs a control city: built development, census jobs, realized revenue.

S6 INTEGRITY: implement-phase self-assessment never stands as certification (twice caught false); workers never amend a gate so work passes it — mis-specified gates are reported and decided by the user; agent-set statuses are reverted pending independent verification.
S7 LIVENESS: the driving loop checks transcript mtime + worker processes every firing; a stale-25-min workflow is resumed from cache, never waited on.
S8 INDEPENDENT SHIPPABILITY: stopping between any two items leaves a coherent, certified, published game.
